**Review round 1 (fresh-adversarial) — 0 must-fix, 2 should-fix + 2 nits, all taken:** (i) the in-repo sibling the app/-scoped audit missed (canon #7): `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` still accepted only `card#<id>` — CI would have redded the exact form DL-201 ratifies as primary; widened to `card[-#]`, AND its leading boundary class gained `_` (`[^0-9A-Za-z_]`) to mirror `\b` semantics — the lint previously accepted `foo_card-<id>` titles the classifier ignores (a title the lint passes must also correlate); 8-case matrix driven on real bash. (ii) `docs/writeback.md` DL-160 operator paragraph still said the push leg needs a `DL-NNN` (stale since DL-179, Rule X1). (iii) the near-miss probe gained the `card #123` space-hash shape (`/\bcard(?:[_:.]|\s#)?\d/i`); bare `card 2` (space, no `#`) stays deliberately silent — prose in PR titles would warn. (iv) `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` constant unified the three DL parse sites (the diff had just symmetrized the two tokens' boundary while leaving their homes asymmetric).

**Consequences:** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` (both token constants + both surfaces + helper + docblocks), `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` (dash alias + `\b`-aligned boundary), `docs/writeback.md` (FR-7 correlation paragraph + DL-160 operator paragraph), tests. Consumer-visible: `card-<id>` correlates once installs upgrade to the release carrying this; both peers byte-pin their `post-checkout` hook filters to this pattern's boundary semantics (their side). agent-board-toolkit `HOOKS.md:29` states the old regex — separate toolkit doc PR. **No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.** The regex is strictly WIDER (every previously-correlating token still correlates identically); the only new writes are moves for tokens that previously silently no-opped — same board-membership + no-regression guards as every move. Roundtable #48; card #4382.

## DL-202 — Action-level consumer declarations + the `bridge:check` action inventory: a declared type's unhandled action is no longer invisible (INFO, deliberately never a WARN)

**Date:** 2026-07-15
**Context:** DL-196's event-follows-consumer check compares at the TOP level (`explode('.', …)[0]`), so once any family declared `issues`, an `issues.<action>` that arrived and was dropped by every family was invisible — before DL-200, `issues.closed` on a coord repo was exactly that (the arrived-and-dropped drift DL-196 exists to surface, one granularity down). Card #4354, filed as a canon-#7 sibling finding while building DL-200. Constraint from the card: preserve "false-WARN possible, false-clean IMPOSSIBLE" at the WARN level; a naive action-level diff would false-WARN on every benign unhandled action (`issues.labeled`…), noise that gets the check ignored — the benign-action posture was THE design question. Fresh-adversarial design review ran to convergence before any code (8 findings, all folded in).

**Decision:** `DeclaresConsumedEvents::consumedEventTypes()` may return QUALIFIED entries (`issues.opened`) alongside bare types. **Bare = ownership** (every action covered; unlisted actions are deliberate no-ops); **qualified = "actions outside this list are inventory-worthy."** The WARN compare PROJECTS declarations to the top level — WARN semantics, the false-clean-impossibility, and noise level all unchanged for conforming installs (bare-only declarations are the identity under projection). NEW: an aggregated **INFO** line per scope+type — `'issues' actions observed but not action-declared by any family: closed (2x, last …)`, actions sorted by count desc, count+last-seen reusing the #4321 aggregate's per-row granularity (retained, not collapsed) — emitted only where the type is consumed ONLY via qualified declarations. Actionless observed types (`push`) never enter the inventory. The undeclared-classifier caveat co-travels (an undeclared classifier might consume an action just as it might a type). **INFO, never WARN, on the mechanism:** GitHub hook `events[]` has no per-action granularity — the WARN's remedy ("drop from the subscription") does not exist at action level, and deliberately-unhandled actions are the majority class; an alarm that is usually a non-issue trains operators to ignore the check that shares its output.

**Who declares qualified (from the review, each with the reason):** `coord-card-create` → `issues.[opened,reopened]`, `coord-card-move` → `issues.[closed,reopened]` — single-sourced consts now shared by the family dispatch guards and the declaration, so neither drifts. `coord-message` → `HANDLED` **unioned with the install's `coord_extra_actions`** (DL-190) — the exact inputs of `subject()`'s action gate; omitting the extra-actions union would false-INFO on precisely the installs that customized (review must-fix #1); pure-`$cfg` read, the hard contract holds. **`impl-ci-wake` stays bare** (`workflow_run` consumes every action — non-terminal runs are considered-and-dropped by design; qualifying would inventory `requested`/`in_progress`, one per CI run). **`GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` stays bare `['pull_request','push']`** — its action surface is per-repo `writeback.json`-gated: a mapping-dependent declaration violates the pure-map contract (file I/O) AND has no scope parameter to answer per (one call per agent, recorded against every scope), and a load failure inside the declaration would flip the classifier to undeclared and spray false WARNs; an unconditional superset would read draft actions as "covered" on installs where `draft_overlay` is off (the shipped-but-not-activated confusion). Its unhandled actions are the benign-majority class the INFO posture exists to keep quiet.

**Honest behavior-change note (review should-fix #5):** a nonconforming classifier that returned a qualified entry BEFORE this change had it sit inert in the consumed set (never matching a top-level observed key ⇒ the type false-WARNED, conservative). Under projection that WARN is suppressed and the coverage becomes real. Qualified returns were documented-invalid until now and all shipped implementors are bare-only (verified at source), so conforming installs are byte-identical — but the compare DID change for that class of return; a lying qualified declaration false-cleans exactly as a lying bare one always could (trust model unchanged).

**Alternatives considered:** (i) action-level WARN — rejected (no per-action remedy exists; cry-wolf degrades the co-located top-level WARN). (ii) a config'd benign-action list gating a WARN — rejected: list staleness reintroduces false-clean, violating the card's own invariant; the bare-vs-qualified declaration IS the benign list, co-located with the consuming code (the anti-drift choice DL-196 already ratified). (iii) per-action INFO lines — rejected (a stable ~10-20-line inventory per run buries the signal; one aggregated line per scope+type, bounded by #types). (iv) cross-install "some family somewhere handles it" — rejected: fleet knowledge `bridge:check` doesn't have; registry-shaped rot DL-196 already refused. (v) qualifying `impl-ci-wake`/`GitHubPrCardMove` — rejected per the paragraph above.

**Mutation-verified:** dropping the `coord_extra_actions` union reds exactly the extra-actions test; treating bare declarations as qualified-empty reds exactly the ownership test. Matrix: the motivating `issues.closed` inventory (count+last-seen), bare-ownership silence, extra-actions honored, undeclared caveat, WARN-unchanged-under-projection.

**Consequences:** `CoordinationClassifier` (qualified derivations + `qualify()` + the shared action-set consts + family-guard rewiring), `CheckCommand` (dual projection off the retained per-row aggregate + the INFO inventory), `DeclaresConsumedEvents` (docblock: qualified entries valid), `docs/customization.md` (§ declaring consumed events), tests. **Supersedes DL-196's "top-level event types" statements** (that entry stays as-written — the log is append-only). No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change; `bridge:check` diagnostics only. Card #4354.

## DL-203 — The machine writeback survives echo: a gate hit on a github writeback-emitting classifier classifies-then-strips to `DurableReaction` targets instead of dropping

**Date:** 2026-07-15
**Context:** The pre-classify echo gate treats every dispatch as an agent surface: an actor matching the agent's own ids (auto-seeded from `identity.github_user_id`, DL-007) drops the whole dispatch — including the **machine writeback** the classifier would have emitted. So the seat whose PR merge / issue close should move its own card is exactly the seat whose events the gate eats: aimla's coord-card creates died this way (their own `issues.opened` events were reattributed-author drops → cards never created), and the documented workaround was "never seed `github_user_id` on the writeback seat" — a footgun disguised as guidance. The ruling (roundtable #52, card #4386): **echo is a SURFACE concern — it exists to stop own-write wakes/inbox noise/self-react loops, none of which a card writeback is.** The writeback is machine-only ("no agent in the loop", DL-021); suppressing it on own-write is a category error. Design converged via fresh-adversarial review before code; operator-approved.
**Decision:** three gates — pre-classify echo, `isSignal`, and the DL-005 reattributed-author completion gate — get **classify-then-strip** when (the resolved classifier implements `EmitsWritebackReactions`) AND (`provider === 'github'`): the classifier runs, then the result is stripped to its machine half — **intents removed** (so inbox staging AND `route_intents` pushes derive nothing) and **targets filtered to those resolving to a `DurableReaction` handler**. Machine targets remain → proceed to handlers; ledger `outcome=delivered` with `reason='echo: agent surface suppressed'` (the one delivered-row reason in the DL-036 vocabulary; `error_message` stays handler-failure-only). Strip empties the result → `markDropped` under the **original** gate reason (`echo: own write` / `actor is not a signal` / `echo: own write (reattributed author)`) — never `classifier emitted no reactions` (the classifier may well have emitted; the gate ate it). Non-qualifying dispatches keep today's cheap pre-classify drops **byte-identical EXCEPT for one measured case** (below). `ClassifierResolver::for()` moves ahead of the gates for the marker check — the marker cannot be read without loading the class — wrapped in the same `recordError` treatment as classify; classify-throws on a pre-known-echo path is likewise `recordError` (ruled: the error is real and must stay replayable, not be folded into the drop).
**The partition primitive is `instanceof DurableReaction` on the RESOLVED handler** — the marker DL-009 already defined as "non-loss-tolerant machine side effect", which is *exactly* the "machine writeback" set (the 5 kanban handlers) vs the agent surface (`log_intent`, `registry_append`, `channel_push`, `spawn_detached`). Fail-closed by construction: a custom `register()`ed handler without the marker — or an unregistered name — is agent-facing and suppressed on echo, so a classifier bug can never leak an own-write wake/spawn through an unmarked handler. Documented as the custom-handler contract: durable ≡ machine writeback ≡ survives echo.
**The `isSignal` gate is the same defect one line down** (canon #7 sibling): a `treat_as_signal` allowlist that filters a non-signal actor was also eating the machine writeback that actor's PR events should drive. Same strip, same reason discipline.
**The provider-`github` gate** keeps the kanban global-echo stream on the cheap drop: the writeback identity's own `card_updated`/`task.created` echoes (DL-009 seam, `bridge.global_echo_ids`) must never re-classify — including on a `kanban-triage` seat, whose `KanbanTriageClassifier` shim *inherits* the marker via `CoordinationClassifier`, and whose re-classified own-create echo would be the DL-198 self-wake loop the `identity_id` echo-gate exists to prevent. No shipped writeback is driven by a kanban-provider event, so nothing is lost.
**Footgun scoping (precise):** the "never seed `github_user_id`" guidance is retired for **writeback targets only**. A wake-purposed seat that seeds it still loses its own-push **wakes** — by design: those are agent surface, and DL-190's never-seed-on-a-wake-identity invariant stands unchanged.
**F7:** suppression is per-emitting-dispatch — it keys on the serving agent's own gates, regardless of where a stripped `channel_push` would have been delivered. **F8:** the delivered log line carries the `reason` marker, so a suppressed-surface delivery is distinguishable in the live log.
**Backfill:** historical `echo: own write (reattributed author)` drops (aimla's dead creates) are recoverable with `bridge:replay <id> --force` on the fixed bridge — the re-run now delivers the machine target (pinned by test).
**Alternatives considered:** (i) a **name-list const** of the 5 kanban handlers — rejected: a second divergent copy of "what is a machine writeback" that drifts the first time a sixth handler ships; the `DurableReaction` marker already IS that set, maintained at the handler. (ii) a **per-target flag** (`ReactionTarget::survivesEcho`) — rejected: N classifier call-sites must remember to set it, and it is classifier-emitted = attacker/bug-influenceable — a classifier bug could flag a `channel_push` as echo-exempt and leak an own-write wake; the handler marker is un-spoofable from the classify path (the exact DL-009 argument). (iii) **exempting only the echo gate, not `isSignal`** — rejected: same defect one line down, found by the same audit. (iv) **no provider gate** (strip on kanban too) — rejected: re-opens the DL-198 self-wake loop analysis for every kanban echo and buys nothing (no kanban-driven writeback exists). (v) **keep the never-seed-github_user_id workaround** — rejected: it is N downstream config patches for one upstream category error, and it makes the same-seat topology (`coord-card-create` on the wake agent, the shipped default guidance) silently lossy.
**The one measured behavior change on the non-qualifying path (probe-verified against `origin/dev`, both providers — NOT byte-identical, stated because an earlier draft of this entry claimed otherwise):** a dispatch whose classifier FQCN is **unresolvable** AND whose actor is an echo previously recorded `dropped`/`echo: own write` (the gate fired first, masking the config error); it now records **`errored`** with `processed_at` NULL (replayable). This holds for **kanban** dispatches too — the hoisted resolver runs ahead of the provider gate, so `provider === 'github'` does not shield it. **Ruled acceptable and better:** a broken classifier config is a real error that must surface rather than be silently absorbed by an echo gate; the row stays replayable. Separately, a **DL-025 stale-signature** classifier is an *uncatchable* `E_COMPILE_ERROR` that fatals (→ 5xx → redelivery) — hoisting **widens which events reach it** (a `treat_as_signal` seat's gated majority no longer acks 200 first) but does not create the failure mode: such an install already fatals on every ungated event, and `bridge:check`'s out-of-process `probeLoadable` is the documented pre-deploy gate. An earlier draft's "never a 5xx retry storm" was false and is corrected here and in the code comment.

**Amends DL-036/DL-037's satellite-field invariant** ("each `mark*` writes the full terminal tuple so a `dropped`→`delivered` re-run can't leave a stale `reason` beside a `delivered` outcome"): a `reason` beside `delivered` is now **legitimate and exclusive to this leg** (`echo: agent surface suppressed`). Those entries stay as-written — the log is append-only (the DL-202 precedent).

**Mutation-verified:** skipping the intent-strip reds the `route_intents`-zero-pushes test (routed push fires) plus the inbox-staging assertions. 12-item matrix: mixed-result strip · route_intents zero pushes (mutation) · byte-identical drops for unmarked classifiers (all three reasons `assertSame`-pinned) · seeded-`github_user_id` writeback survives · kanban-triage global-echo loop pin (+ a provider-gate never-classifies pin via a throwing marker classifier) · `isSignal`+marker survives · redelivery no re-fire · durable throw 5xx then completes · `--force` backfill · custom unmarked handler suppressed · classify-throw-on-known-echo ruling · strip-to-nothing original-reason pin (+ a no-gate control).
**Consequences:** `DispatchService` (classifier resolution hoisted ahead of the gates; `$gateReason`/`$stripToMachine`; the strip; `markDelivered` gains the `reason` param), `docs/writeback.md` (seat-placement guidance: identity-less dedicated seat preferred, same-seat-now-safe supported, footgun scoping), `docs/customization.md` (the durable ≡ machine-writeback ≡ survives-echo contract line), `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` (ledger contract: the one delivered-row `reason`), `CLAUDE_ARCHITECTURE.md` lifecycle line, `EchoSuppression` docblock, `tests/Feature/Dispatch/EchoExemptWritebackTest.php` + `tests/Fixtures/WritebackEmittingClassifier.php`. No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change; kanban-provider dispatches and unmarked-classifier github dispatches are byte-identical **except** the unresolvable-FQCN-plus-echo case measured above. Consumer-visible: a same-seat coord/writeback agent's own github events now drive their card writebacks; `bridge:inspect` shows `delivered` + `echo: agent surface suppressed` for them. Roundtable #52; card #4386.

## DL-204 — The coord-issue → card MOVE writeback (`move_coord_cards`) becomes a guarded fleet default: absent ⇒ on where the terminal is configured, inert where it is not

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Context:** DL-200 shipped `move_coord_cards` as a per-mapping opt-in (default false) — a second flag every install had to set on top of already configuring the per-board stage ids. Roundtable #18(b), approved 3/3 (aimla operator-directed + sola proposer + kanban-solo): make the real-time close→terminal / reopen→revive MOVE a **fleet default**, so an install whose coordination board already carries the stage ids gets the leg without a separate flag. The naive `default: true` was refused by all three: every coord-mapped install lacking the two stage ids would **throw at load** (the DL-200 fail-closed guards), i.e. the fleet default would detonate on adoption. The pinned 3-point guard shape: (1) present stage ids → on, absent → inert byte-identical; (2) inert must not be silent-inert — a `bridge:check` discovery nudge; (3) unconfigured → inert vs misconfigured → loud. Design converged via fresh-adversarial review before code (which caught the family-gating gap below); operator-approved.
**Decision (gate 2 — the handler-side default, `WritebackConfig::load`):** when `move_coord_cards` is **absent** it resolves **ON iff `coord_card_terminal_stage_id` is present**, inert otherwise. The terminal key — which has **no other consumer** — is the "operator configured the move leg" signal, so keying the default on its presence makes "byte-identical for unconfigured" exact and "active where configured" precise. An **explicit** `move_coord_cards` (true or false) is honored exactly (opt-in still fail-closed on an incomplete config; opt-out still silent-off). The existing DL-200 fail-closed guards are **unchanged** and now deliver points 1 + 3 for free: terminal absent ⇒ resolved false ⇒ guards skip ⇒ inert; terminal present + revive stage missing/equal ⇒ the guards throw ⇒ loud at that board. Only one config shape changes behavior: **terminal present + `move_coord_cards` absent** flips inert → active (the intended activation).
**Scope — GATE 2 ONLY; `DEFAULT_FAMILIES` (gate 1) is untouched.** The leg fires only where BOTH the `coord-card-move` classifier family (gate 1, in the agent YAML) AND `move_coord_cards` (gate 2) are on. `coordCardMoveFamily()` self-gates on `move_coord_cards`, so flipping gate 2 alone is strictly **inert** where gate 1 is off — never a wrong move. The card was titled "flip *move_coord_cards*" and the approvals were for the guarded move_coord_cards default; adding `coord-card-move` to `DEFAULT_FAMILIES` would change classification for installs that never opted into coord-card handling (canon-#6 scope creep) and was **not** approved. Consequence, stated plainly: the flip is a **no-op for installs already running the family with explicit `move_coord_cards: true`** (e.g. AIMLA board 10, live since v0.58.0); its beneficiaries are family-enabled installs whose terminal is set but the flag omitted. A thin-but-legitimate delivery of the approved 3-point shape (whose point-2 nudge explicitly names the family as the separate step).
**Decision (`bridge:check` — point 2 + the finding-1 gate).** The design review found that after the flip `move_coord_cards` resolves true from terminal-presence alone, decoupled from whether the leg can fire (gate 1). So the check keys on the **`coord-card-move` family being enabled for the scope** (a `$coordCardMoveScopes` set mirrors `$writebackEmittingScopes`; `coord-card-move` is never in `DEFAULT_FAMILIES`, so a raw-config membership test is the resolved answer), not on `move_coord_cards`: (a) **two config-only discovery WARNs, one per silent-inert direction** — a family-enabled scope whose `coord_card_terminal_stage_id` is absent (classified but the handler won't move), AND (the impl-review sibling) the mirror: a mapping whose move leg resolved on (terminal present) but whose scope runs no `coord-card-move` family (the handler would move but nothing classifies a move — the adoption-path death of "set the terminal, no flag needed" when the family is never enabled); both placed in the config-only block beside the DL-198 nudge, never in the board-read method; (b) the DL-200 terminal-agreement compare is **gated on the family** so it never verifies a terminal for a leg that cannot fire and reads as though it were live (this gate is exactly why the mirror WARN is needed — it removed the weak signal that path used to get). The nudge is scoped to family-enabled installs so a pure PR-writeback install gets **no** coord-move noise (the DL-202 no-false-alarm posture) — the review flagged `create_coord_cards`-on as the wrong signal (false-miss on move-only installs, false-alarm on create-only).
**Live validation:** **no fleet seat live-witnesses the `absent → on` path** (confirmed on all three configs post-approval, not assumed): AIMLA is explicit-true (the flip never runs there; it is instead the **byte-identical regression witness**, cards 4388/4392/4416/4421/4423/4428/4435 → stage 74 on 07-15), kanban-solo is Layer-B (inert), and sola carries **neither** coord key on any mapping (terminal absent everywhere → resolves inert; not merely flag-omitted — the terminal is the blocker). So the `absent → on` path ships **phpunit-matrix + mutation + fresh-adversarial design/impl-review verified only** — the one path no live board exercises. Pre-adoption correctness rests on that; the sole live check is AIMLA's post-adoption re-confirm of the explicit-true regression leg on board 10.
**Live-witness update (2026-07-16, post-adoption — SUPERSEDES the "no live witness" posture above):** the `absent → on` path is now **live-witnessed on AIMLA board 10** (roundtable #18). AIMLA adopted v0.59.0 (`bridge:check` exit 0, `/up` 200) and ran a reversible exercise on a throwaway coord issue: (a) explicit-`true` regression fires **byte-identical** (close → terminal 74); (b) with the explicit `move_coord_cards` **dropped** and only `coord_card_terminal_stage_id: 74` kept (family on), a close moved the card to 74 — the DL-204 default resolved the leg **ON** in the real loader/dispatch, exercising the exact path no fleet seat previously could; (c) window co-check **clean** — `bridge:check` exit 0, the terminal-agreement compare ran ("coord config agrees"), and neither DL-204 discovery nudge fired. Config restored byte-identical (no residue). Canon-#9 first-real-exercise of the boundary: **met.**
**Alternatives considered:** (i) naive `default: true` — rejected (throws at load on every under-configured coord install). (ii) also flip `DEFAULT_FAMILIES` to include `coord-card-move` — rejected (out of the approved scope; changes classification for non-opted-in installs; the self-gate makes gate-2-only safe). (iii) key the default / the nudge on the `move_coord_cards` boolean or on `create_coord_cards` — rejected (both decouple from "the leg can fire": the boolean reads true even when the family is off; `create_coord_cards` mis-signals in both directions). (iv) a new `move_coord_cards`-was-explicit field to suppress the nudge on explicit-false — not needed: the nudge keys on terminal-absent, and explicit-false-with-terminal-present is respected (terminal present ⇒ no nudge).
**UPGRADING:** an install with `coord_card_terminal_stage_id` configured but `move_coord_cards` unset will **start moving cards** on coord-issue close/reopen (where the `coord-card-move` family is enabled). To keep it off, set `move_coord_cards: false`. Installs with the terminal unset, or with an explicit `move_coord_cards`, are byte-identical.
**Mutation-verified / matrix:** WritebackConfig — default-on-when-configured · absent+terminal-absent inert (byte-identical) · default-on partial (no revive stage) throws · explicit-false stays off with a full config · explicit-true regression pins unchanged. Handler + classifier — default-on-without-flag moves/emits · explicit-false opt-out moves/emits nothing. bridge:check — nudge fires on family-enabled+terminal-absent · mirror nudge fires on terminal-present+family-off · silent on a pure-PR install (no terminal) · terminal-agreement compare skipped when the family is off.
**Consequences:** `WritebackConfig::load` (the default resolution + the reworded partial-config guard message), `CheckCommand` (`$coordCardMoveScopes`; the discovery WARN; the family gate on the terminal-agreement call), `docs/writeback.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`, the `WritebackConfig` docblock. No migration, no new config key, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. Installs without a terminal, or with an explicit `move_coord_cards`, upgrade byte-identically; a family-enabled install with a terminal set but the flag omitted flips from inert to active (the intended fleet activation). Roundtable #18(b); card #4357.

## DL-205 — A kanban 4xx refusal logs the server's response body (scrubbed), and log lines state what was OBSERVED instead of asserting an unchecked cause

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Context:** A live incident (the DL-204 rollout) surfaced two defects in the writeback handlers' 4xx-refusal logging. **(1)** Every `RequestException`-catch on a kanban 4xx logged **status only** (`['status' => $e->response->status()]`) and discarded the response body, so a permission refusal (403), a validation refusal (422), and a state refusal (404/409) were indistinguishable in the log — the operator could not tell *why* kanban refused. **(2)** Two log lines **asserted a cause the handler never checked**, pointing away from the fault: `KanbanMoveCardHandler` on a move-4xx said "check the writeback.json stage maps to a stage on the card's board" and on a stamp-4xx said "the board likely lacks the dl_number/pr_number custom field" — both FALSE in the real incident, which was a DL-204 authz refusal (the stage WAS mapped, the custom field DID exist). A sibling of the same shape lived at `KanbanClient::correlationCards` ("the token's user is likely **not a member** of this board") — a guess on a 200-with-0-cards read that is genuinely ambiguous (an empty board reads identically).
**Decision:** Fix the primitive, not the 9 call-sites (canon #5): a single shared `App\Bridge\Support\RefusalContext::from(RequestException)` returns `['status' => int, 'body' => string]` — the response body **verbatim, truncated to 500 chars, credential-scrubbed** — merged into each site's existing context (`['card_id' => …] + RefusalContext::from($e)`). Every 4xx refusal log across the five writeback handlers (9 sites: `KanbanMoveCardHandler` getCard/move/stamp, `KanbanBlockReasonHandler` getCard/set, `KanbanCoordCardHandler`, `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandler` ×2, `KanbanDependabotCardHandler`) now hands over what the server said. The two unchecked causal clauses are **deleted** — the messages state only the observation ("kanban refused the move — see `body`") and defer the cause to the body. `KanbanClient::correlationCards`'s 0-card warning is reworded from asserting membership loss to stating the observed no-op and listing what to verify (membership / board_id / genuinely-empty), since a 0-card read cannot distinguish those.
**Scrub mechanism (`RefusalContext::scrub`):** three passes, run on the **full body before truncation** (so a credential split across the 500-char boundary can't leak its head): (a) JSON string values of any key *containing* a sensitive word (`token`, `secret`, `password`, `authorization`, `api_key`, `access_token`, …) → `"[REDACTED]"`; (b) query/form `key=value` pairs for those keys; (c) HTTP auth schemes `Bearer`/`Basic`/`token` **followed by a credential-LONG value (`{16,}` of the token charset)** → `[REDACTED]`. The length gate on (c) is load-bearing: a bare-`token` scheme match with no length floor redacted the prose word after "token" ("token cannot write …" → "token [REDACTED] write …"), mangling the very reason the body exists to surface — real tokens are long, English words after the keyword are short, so `{16,}` separates them cleanly (keyed credentials of any length stay covered by (a)/(b)). Over-redaction is the safe failure mode; a leaked token is the one designed against.
**Scope:** logging only — no change to what is accepted/rejected, to the transient(5xx→retry)/permanent(4xx→log+no-op) split, or to any control flow. The `bridge:check`/`bridge:reconcile` CLI catch-sites are deliberately **out of scope**: they are operator-interactive, already interpret the status into remediation hints, and do not silently discard into a log — a different class from the swallowed-4xx handler sites.
**Alternatives considered:** (i) add `body` inline at each of the 9 sites — rejected (9 divergent copies of the truncate+scrub logic; canon #5). (ii) log the body unscrubbed — rejected (a kanban error body can echo the request, which may carry the writeback token). (iii) delete the `KanbanClient` 0-card warning entirely — rejected (the observation is genuinely useful; only the asserted cause was wrong, so it is reworded, not removed). (iv) no length gate on the auth-scheme scrub — rejected (mangles prose; surfaced by a test).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `RefusalContextTest` (status+body carried, truncation, per-vector scrub matrix, benign body untouched, split-across-boundary still redacted); `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` (move-4xx and stamp-4xx assert the body is in the context AND the deleted guessed strings are absent; a token echoed in a 403 body is scrubbed); `KanbanClientTest` (the 0-card warning no longer says "likely not a member" and states the observation).
**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Support/RefusalContext.php`; the 9 handler log sites + `KanbanClient::correlationCards` (message + docblock); `docs/writeback.md` (the diagnose note that a logged refusal now carries kanban's response body). No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. 903/903 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. Card #4409.

## DL-206 — Bridge-created dependabot cards can carry an opt-in `id:` provenance tag (per-mapping `card_id_tag_template`) so tag-keyed promoters can find them

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Context:** `KanbanDependabotCardHandler` creates dependabot cards tagged `['dependencies','triaged']` with `payload[pr_number,pr_url,origin]` — but **no `id:` provenance tag**. The bridge correlates its own cards **by-ref** (`pr_number`/`pr_url` → `by-ref.json`); the `id:{PREFIX}-pr-{N}` tag is an **impl-side** convention stamped on **impl-created** cards, which the fleet's tag-keyed Shipped→Released promoters read. Dependabot is the one PR-provenance card the **bridge itself** mints, so it lacked the `id:` tag its impl-created siblings carry — invisible to any tag-keyed promoter (sola's `reconcile-released-to-main.py` reads the `id:` tag only; **27 dependabot cards stranded** in Shipped-to-dev on sola board 3). Roundtable #75, converged 3-way (sola-pm + aimla-pm + kanban-solo). aimla verified their own promoters are **payload-keyed** (0 stranded on board 9) — proving `payload` is a usable correlation key and `id:` is the *canonical* one, i.e. stamping the tag is **strictly additive**, not a migration.
**Decision:** an opt-in per-mapping **`card_id_tag_template`** (free-form non-empty string). When set, the handler renders it into an `id:` tag **prepended** to the create tags; **unset ⇒ no tag (inert, byte-identical)**. Placeholders: `{n}`/`{pr_number}` = the PR number, `{repo}` = the repo NAME (`basename(owner/repo)`). Per-tenant grammar — sola `id:DEV-pr-{n}` (matches its reconcile's `id:(DEV|BE|INV)-pr-(\d+)`), AIMLA `id:dep:{repo}#{n}`. Parsed exactly like `draft_block_reason` (present-must-be-non-empty-string, else `ConfigException` at load — fail-closed). This **restores parity** between bridge-created and impl-created PR-provenance cards (canon #5 — extend the existing key, don't sibling it), not a new convention: the card stays idempotent on `payload.pr_number` for its create/move lifecycle AND correlatable by the `id:` tag for external promoters — no read-side union of two formats anywhere.
**Why the write-site, not a read-side fallback:** teaching each promoter to read `payload` would be N payload-aware readers of two formats for one thing — the canon-#5 anti-pattern. One write-site guarantees the canonical key.
**AIMLA namespace constraint (roundtable #75, aimla traced to source):** aimla's `kanban-board9-dev-sync.py` owns the `id:pr:` namespace and its `owns_id` keys on the **sid string only** (can't see payload/tags). It has **no "archive owned-absent-from-source" pass**, so a bridge-stamped card is never archived — the *only* constraint is that AIMLA's template resolve to a namespace **disjoint from `id:pr:`** (hence `id:dep:{repo}#{n}`), which their existing `sid.startswith("pr:")` then excludes with **zero aimla code change**. The free-form template delivers exactly that lever.
**Relationship to #4483 (promote-on-release leg):** #4483 keys on the **bridge-native `payload.pr_number`/`pr_url`** correlation (which every card carries, dependabot included), so it covers dependabot cards **regardless** of this tag — this template serves the **external** `id:`-keyed readers (sola's reconcile), not the bridge's own leg.
**Scope:** the dependabot **create** path only. Unknown template placeholders are left **literal** (the tenant verifies its template against its own `id:`-keyed reader at activation, not here). No cross-field guard — a template set with `create_dependabot_cards: false` is inert (no cards created ⇒ nothing stamped), not an error. No change to the create/move/archive lifecycle, the correlation, the transient/permanent split, or the token scope.
**Alternatives considered:** (i) teach every promoter to read `payload` — rejected (N readers, two formats; canon #5). (ii) a hardcoded `card_id_prefix` scalar — rejected (AIMLA's `id:dep:{repo}#{n}` is not a prefix apart from sola's `id:{PREFIX}-pr-{n}`; the grammars differ, so a per-tenant **format template** is required). (iii) key #4483 on the `id:` tag — rejected (would inherit the tagless blind spot; #4483 keys on bridge-native `payload.pr_number` instead).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `WritebackConfigTest` (loads the template / absent ⇒ null / empty-string throws / non-string throws); `KanbanDependabotCardHandlerTest` (stamps the rendered tag, `{repo}` → `basename`, absent template ⇒ tags are **exactly** `['dependencies','triaged']`). Mutation-verified: reverting the conditional stamp reds the two stamp tests, the back-compat test stays green.
**Consequences:** new nullable `WritebackMapping::$cardIdTagTemplate`; `WritebackConfig::load` parse + docblock; `KanbanDependabotCardHandler::renderIdTag` + conditional tag; `docs/writeback.md` + `docs/config-schema.md`. No migration, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change; **inert unless configured**. Per-tenant **activation** (set the template + redeploy) and the one-time **backfill** of existing tagless cards are separate, operator/user-gated steps (not autonomous). 913/913 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. Card #4485.

## DL-207 — An opt-in `promote_on_release` writeback leg promotes Shipped cards to Released on a release merge, keyed on POSITIVE reachability of the card's merge sha from `main`

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Context:** A card-first board with a **Shipped-to-dev / Released-to-main** column split has **no steady-state promotion**. A feature PR merges to `dev` (`base=dev` ⇒ outcome `merged` ⇒ card → Shipped); its commits reach `main` only later, folded into a **release PR** (`release/vX → main`). That release merge fires exactly ONE `merged_to_main` event — for the release PR's *own* card — so the constituent feature cards stay at **Shipped** until a manual `bridge:reconcile`. And `bridge:reconcile` deliberately **defers** the Shipped→Released transition to "the promote workflow" (`ReconcileCommand` excludes `merged_to_main` from move-in, ~:319-328, and treats a card already at the released stage as terminal). So nothing promotes in steady state. Roundtable #73, converged with sola-pm (sola supplies `reconcile-released-to-main.py` as the reference — `get_dev_only_shas` + tag→merge_sha). **This leg IS that promote workflow, event-driven.**
**Decision:** an opt-in per-mapping **`promote_on_release`** (bool, default false). On the `merged_to_main` event, `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` emits — via a single choke-point wrapper (`classify()` appends the target once rather than threading it into each move/overlay return) — one `kanban_promote_released` target, INDEPENDENT of whether the release PR itself carries a card token. The new **`KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler`** (`DurableReaction`, always-on in `HandlerRegistry`) scans the mapped board for cards **at the Shipped stage** (`stages.merged`) that are tooling-managed (a PR reference), not pinned, and — on a shared board — attributable to this repo, and promotes each whose merged PR's commit is now on `main` to the Released stage (`stages.merged_to_main`). Reuses the existing stage keys; `promote_on_release` fails **closed at load** when `stages.merged`/`stages.merged_to_main` is unmapped.
**The promotion predicate is POSITIVE reachability, not a dev-only proxy:** promote iff `GitHubReadClient::compareStatus(merge_commit_sha, RELEASE_BASE='main') ∈ {ahead, identical}` — main is ahead-of/equal-to the merge sha ⇒ the sha is an ancestor of main ⇒ the card's work is ON main ⇒ released — **gated on `getPull(...).merged === true`** (an OPEN PR carries a non-null *test-merge* `merge_commit_sha` on no branch; the emptiness guard would never catch it). The first-round design used sola's negative `merge_sha ∉ compare(main...dev)` proxy; adversarial design review found `∉ dev-only-set` is ALSO true for shas on **neither** branch (open-PR test-merge shas, PRs merged to a third base, cross-repo shas) → false promotions into the **terminal** Released stage. The positive test rejects all three populations, needs **no `integration_branch` config**, and has **no 250-commit compare-truncation risk** (only `status` is read). It is self-healing: a card stranded by a prior failed release promotes on the *next* release event (its sha is on main via the earlier merge-commit).
**Merge-strategy precondition (documented, unguardable):** correctness rests on the release→`main` merge preserving `dev`'s commit shas — a **merge-commit or fast-forward** (verified this fleet's method: `Merge pull request #N from …/release/vX`; dev PRs squash-merge, so a squash-sha on dev becomes reachable from main via the release merge-commit). A **squash/rebase RELEASE merge** rewrites shas, so no feature sha ever joins main and the leg promotes nothing; `bridge:check` cannot detect merge strategy, so this is a doc precondition, not a guard.
**First runtime GitHub-read dependency:** this is the FIRST path to call GitHub in the **FPM runtime** (today only the reconcile CLI reads GitHub). Under FPM `GH_TOKEN` is absent (DL-184) and the `git-credential-coord` store helper is CLI-only, so in practice a **placed `<secret_dir>/github/token`** (or `providers.github.token_path`) is required. Unresolved token ⇒ durable `WritebackAlertNotifier` alert + loud log + **no-op** (a permanent config gap; a 5xx would retry-storm an unfixable event). `bridge:check` warns when `promote_on_release` is on but no token resolves **from a file** (the store/GH_TOKEN leg that satisfies reconcile does NOT hold under FPM), and when `stages.merged === stages.merged_to_main` (the promote is a no-op). A tighter runtime GitHub timeout (8s vs reconcile's 15s) and a `MAX_CANDIDATES` cap bound the synchronous webhook; overflow is alerted and drains across successive release events (a promoted card leaves the Shipped filter). **No reconcile backstop for this transition**, so every gap is made LOUD (alert + `bridge:check`), and recovery is fix-the-gap → the next release re-scans.
**Not gated on #4391:** #4391 is the CI PROMOTE SECRET (a `release-promote` Action token that 403s on `task.move`). This leg runs in the bridge RUNTIME and moves via the runtime **writeback** token (`WritebackClientFactory`) — the SAME `KanbanClient`+token the existing `merged_to_main` release-PR-card move already uses successfully — so `task.move` demonstrably works here; the leg is decoupled from #4391. (Corrects an earlier token-conflation claim on roundtable #73.)
**Shared code (canon #5):** the card→(repo, PR) precedence (pr_url → bare-pr_number-on-1:1-board → dl-only-skip, with the shared-board bare-pr_number ambiguity rule) is extracted into a pure `TrackedCardRef`/`TrackedRefKind` helper adopted by BOTH `ReconcileCommand::resolveTracked` and this handler, so the two can't derive a card's PR differently. `ReconcileCommand`'s inline precedence + dead `parsePrUrl` are replaced by the shared helper (behavior byte-identical — `ReconcileCommandTest` green).
**Scope / boundary:** DL-only cards (no PR reference) are not promotable — the SAME PR-driven boundary the reconcile draws ("DL→PR resolution out of v1 scope"). First-adoption of a large existing Shipped backlog is bounded by the cap (steady-state N is a handful) — a `bridge:promote` CLI backfill is a filed fast-follow, not this PR. `merged_to_main` fires for any merge to main (release, hotfix, dependabot-to-main); the scan is idempotent and semantically correct on all (anything landing work on main releases it), so over-firing is safe.
**Alternatives considered:** (i) sola's negative dev-only-set proxy — rejected (admits neither-branch shas → false terminal promotions; design review). (ii) a separate promote classifier — rejected (`ClassifierResolver` runs exactly ONE classifier per agent, so a sibling would displace the move classifier; embed as an opt-in leg like overlay/dependabot/revive). (iii) scatter-merging the promote target into each classifier return — rejected (canon #7 N-edit sibling-hole shape; a dependabot-to-main return already drops it — single choke point instead). (iv) an `integration_branch` config for the compare — dropped (the positive against-main test needs only `RELEASE_BASE`).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `GitHubReadClientTest` (getPull carries `merge_commit_sha`; `compareStatus`); `WritebackConfigTest` (`promote_on_release` default false / fail-closed on missing shipped/released stage); `TrackedCardRefTest` (the shared precedence); `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` (promote target on a bare release PR / alongside a DL move / on the dependabot-to-main edge; none on merge-to-dev or flag-off); `KanbanPromoteReleasedHandlerTest` (promotes only Shipped cards whose merge is on main; skips diverged/open-PR/no-pr/pinned/not-shipped; no-token no-op; transient 5xx propagates, permanent 4xx skips the card); `HandlerRegistryTest` (registered as a `DurableReaction` — the DL-203 strip-survival invariant); `BridgeCommandsTest` (the two `bridge:check` warns + the quiet case).
**Consequences:** new `KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler`; new `TrackedCardRef`/`TrackedRefKind`; `GitHubReadClient` widened (`merge_commit_sha`, `compareStatus`, injectable timeout); `WritebackMapping::$promoteOnRelease` + `WritebackConfig::load` parse/fail-closed; classifier wrapper; `HandlerRegistry` registration; `CheckCommand` two warns; `ReconcileCommand` uses the shared helper; `docs/writeback.md` + `docs/config-schema.md` + `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`. No migration, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change; **inert unless configured**. Per-tenant **activation** (set `promote_on_release` + place a runtime GitHub token file + redeploy) is a separate operator/user-gated step. 949/949 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean; two fresh-adversarial design-review rounds (predicate corrected round 1→2) + an impl-review pass. Card #4483.

## DL-208 — `EventDrivenClassifier` inherits the DL-191 `route_intents` wake-guard: the guarded `wakePush()` lifts to the shared `InboxOnlyClassifier` base, closing the last double-wake copy

**Date:** 2026-07-17
**Context:** DL-191 gave `CoordinationClassifier` a guarded `wakePush()` that suppresses a family's hand-emitted `channel_push` on a `route_intents:true` channel (the dispatcher already routes every staged intent → a hand-emit is a second push). `EventDrivenClassifier` — the *other* shipped hand-emitting classifier, a sibling subclass of `InboxOnlyClassifier` — was **never** given that guard: its `classify()` appended a `channel_push` per intent **unconditionally**. Coalescing does not save it: the classifier's target defaults `debounceKey → targetId` (`channel_push|<subject>`) while the dispatcher's routed push namespaces it (`channel_push|channel_push:<subject>`), so the two survive under distinct keys and the handler fires **twice** with identical payload. Any agent on `EventDrivenClassifier` + `channel.route_intents:true` double-woke every event — the exact hazard DL-191 fixed for the coord families, guarded here only by a code comment ("pair route_intents with a plain inbox classifier, not EventDriven"). The N=2 copies (this + the coord families) are the sibling-duplication canon #5/#7 flag: one behavior, two byte-identical emitters, and the guard reached only one.
**Decision:** lift the guarded emitter to the **common base** `InboxOnlyClassifier::wakePush()` (`protected`; byte-identical to DL-191's private coord copy — the canonical guarded semantics). Both wake-emitting subclasses now share it: `EventDrivenClassifier::classify()` becomes a flat-map of intents through `$this->wakePush($intent, $ctx)`; `CoordinationClassifier` deletes its private copy and inherits (its `KanbanTriageClassifier` subclass inherits transitively). The base's *own* `classify()` still emits no reactions — `wakePush()` is shared subclass machinery, not a base reaction. (No trait: the codebase has no traits and the two emitters already share the `InboxOnlyClassifier` ancestor, so the base is the single natural home.)
**Behavior:** `route_intents:false` is **byte-identical** for both classifiers (the emitted `ReactionTarget` is unchanged — same handler/targetId/debounceSeconds:0/payload). `route_intents:true` changes only `EventDrivenClassifier`: **one wake, was two**. This reverses the documented "don't pair EventDriven with route_intents" footgun — pairing is now safe, matching `CoordinationClassifier`. Only a **raw custom classifier** that emits `channel_push` without routing through `wakePush()` still double-pushes (docs updated to steer custom authors to the guarded helper).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `EventDrivenClassifierTest::test_suppresses_hand_emit_on_route_intents_true` (zero targets on a `route_intents:true` channel; intent still staged) + `test_multiple_intents_each_hand_emit_on_route_intents_false` (behavior-preserving one-push baseline); the existing `CoordinationClassifier`/`KanbanTriage` `route_intents` suppression tests stay green against the inherited method.
**Consequences:** `InboxOnlyClassifier` gains `protected wakePush()`; `EventDrivenClassifier` flat-maps through it (drops its direct `ReactionTarget` construction/import); `CoordinationClassifier` deletes its private `wakePush()`. Doc-sync (Rule X1 — the reversed footgun): `DispatchService` route_intents comment, `docs/multi-agent.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`, `docs/multi-host.md`, and the `docs/customization.md` subclass example (now shows the guarded `wakePush()`). Historical records left as-is (the 2026-05-31 architecture review, DL-006/190/191, past CHANGELOG rows). No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. 945/945 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. Card #4494.

## DL-209 — `bridge:check` defers the `alert_channel` url gate to the runtime sender (`LocalhostUrl::assertValid`); the loopback-host membership test is extracted to a shared `LoopbackHost::matches`

**Date:** 2026-07-17
**Context:** The writeback alert `alert_channel.url` SSRF gate — scheme must be http, host must be loopback (`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`[::1]`), no userinfo — is enforced at send time by `WritebackAlertNotifier` → `LocalhostUrl::assertValid`. `CheckCommand::checkAlertChannel` hand-rolled its own copy of that gate to preflight the same url, and the copy had **drifted**: it checked scheme and host but **dropped the userinfo rejection**. So `http://user:pass@127.0.0.1/hook` **passed `bridge:check`** (green info line) yet was **rejected by the sender** at the first alert push — the check green-lit a config the runtime refuses. The loopback allowlist + host-normalize (`strtolower(trim($host,'[]'))`) was additionally **triplicated** across `LocalhostUrl` (the loopback-only SSRF gate), `UrlValidator::secureHttpUrl` (its http-loopback exception for secret-bearing api_base urls), and this now-dead inline copy — the canon #5/#7 sibling-duplication flag: one predicate, three copies, and the userinfo rule reached only one of the two real validators.
**Decision:** (1) `CheckCommand::checkAlertChannel` **defers to the runtime authority** — wrap `LocalhostUrl::assertValid($url, 'writeback.json alert_channel: url')` in try/catch, emit `$this->info` on success and `$this->warn($e->getMessage().' — the alert push will fail (caught) until fixed')` on `EndpointValidationException` (preserving the check's warn-not-fail semantics for this opt-in diagnostic). The check and the sender now run **the same gate**, so they can never disagree again. (2) Extract the shared loopback sub-predicate to `App\Bridge\Support\LoopbackHost::matches(string $host): bool` (the allowlist + normalize) and have **both** legitimate validators call it — `LocalhostUrl::assertValid` and `UrlValidator::secureHttpUrl`. The third "copy" (the inline check code) is pure drift and is **deleted** by the deferral, not preserved.
**Why not merge the two validators:** they have **opposite scheme policies** — `secureHttpUrl` allows https **anywhere** (a secret-bearing api_base may be a remote https host) and permits http only for loopback; `LocalhostUrl` **forbids https**, permitting http-loopback only (a pure SSRF gate for a local channel). Only the loopback-host **sub-predicate** is common, so only that is shared; the two validators stay distinct.
**Behavior:** `bridge:check` now **warns** (still exit-0, still opt-in-diagnostic) on an `alert_channel.url` with a userinfo component, where it previously green-lit it — matching the sender. Scheme/host warn cases are unchanged in effect (the surfaced message text changed: it now carries the sender's field-named reason instead of the hand-rolled `(got '…')` echo). `LocalhostUrl` and `secureHttpUrl` are behavior-identical (pure refactor to the shared predicate). No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `BridgeCommandsTest::test_check_warns_on_alert_channel_url_with_userinfo` (reds — the inline copy green-lights it — when the deferral is reverted); `LoopbackHostTest` (predicate matrix: loopback variants + case/bracket normalization + non-loopback/empty/lookalike-suffix rejections); `LocalhostUrlTest` (characterization for the refactored gate: accepts loopback http, normalizes scheme/IPv6, rejects userinfo/https/non-loopback). Existing `UrlValidatorTest` + the two prior `alert_channel` check tests stay green.
**Consequences:** new `App\Bridge\Support\LoopbackHost`; `LocalhostUrl` + `UrlValidator::secureHttpUrl` call it; `CheckCommand` drops its inline url parse/validate block and imports `LocalhostUrl` + `EndpointValidationException`. Doc-sync: `docs/writeback.md` alert_channel warn-cases sentence updated to state the check applies the sender's gate (incl. userinfo). No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. Card #4495.

## DL-210 — `bridge:reconcile` + `bridge:check` share one GitHub token resolve→probe→classify primitive (`GitHubRepoProbe`); `bridge:check` gains the status→hint classification it lacked

**Date:** 2026-07-17
**Context:** Both commands resolve a GitHub read token per writeback repo (`GitHubTokenResolver`, DL-185), build a `GitHubReadClient`, probe `GET /repos/{repo}`, and map the outcome to an operator diagnostic. DL-185 shared the **resolution** so the two could not disagree on *"is a token available?"*, but the **probe + classification** was left duplicated across `ReconcileCommand` (per-repo startup probe) and `CheckCommand` (the DL-186 preflight validity probe) — and the copies had **drifted worse than a warn-vs-error split**: (a) `ReconcileCommand` branched the status into a hint (`401` ⇒ *expired/revoked*, `403/404` ⇒ *lacks access — needs `repo` scope*) while `CheckCommand` did **no** status branching — every status yielded a bare `HTTP {status}`, so an operator got a precise root-cause from the run and a vague one from the preflight; (b) the network-failure branch was **opposite** (reconcile errors loudly + sets `hadError`; check `catch (Throwable)` swallowed it silently); (c) a comment at the check site claimed it *"can't drift from what reconcile resolves"* — true for resolution (shared since DL-185) but **false for classification**, which had. The canon #5/#7 shape: one behavior, two copies, and the hint table reached only one.
**Decision:** Extract `App\Bridge\Writeback\GitHubRepoProbe` (+ result value object `GitHubRepoProbeResult` + `GitHubRepoProbeKind` enum) as the single authority for resolve→construct→`probeRepo`→classify, mirroring the `PrOutcome`/`TrackedCardRef` "single authority for a drift-prone decision shared by two paths" precedent. It owns the canonical 401/403/404→hint table once (`GitHubRepoProbe::hintFor`); the semantics are **`ReconcileCommand`'s** (the one that had classification). Each command keeps its own posture on the result kind: `ReconcileCommand` stores the client + sets `repoUsable`/`hadError` + loud `error`; `CheckCommand` `warn`s on `Unresolvable`/`Http` and stays silent on `Ok`/`Network` (a network blip is not a token-validity signal). Non-throwing (the resolver is total; the probe's exceptions are caught) so a consumer can layer its posture. **[DL-251 (2026-07-31) SPLIT THAT SHARED SILENCE, and the parenthetical here is why it survived so long. "A network blip is not a token-validity signal" is true and was never the problem; making it share `Ok`'s arm was. The two produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output, so an operator could not tell "this token is valid" from "we never reached GitHub to ask" at the leg whose whole subject is that token. `Network` now reports `unvalidated` — naming the repo, refusing to accuse the token, and naming the action — while `Ok` keeps the silence. Read "stays silent on `Ok`/`Network`" as the state DL-210 shipped.]**
**Behavior:** `bridge:check`'s reconcile-token probe warn now carries the **same status→hint as reconcile** — a `401` reads `HTTP 401 (token expired/revoked)` and a `403/404` `HTTP 403 (token lacks access to this private repo — needs `repo` scope)`, where it previously emitted a bare `HTTP {status}`. This is an **intended behavior change** (the card's stated MIGRATION RISK: medium — it gives check a real status→hint table it lacked); the message templates, the shadowing-file steer, and the warn-never-fail exit-0 posture are otherwise unchanged. `bridge:reconcile` is **behavior-identical** (same messages, same `-v` line, same `hadError`); one dead store was removed — it previously assigned `clients[$canon]` *before* the probe even on a failing probe, but `clients[$canon]` is only ever read under `repoUsable[$canon] === true` (set only on a successful probe), so storing on `Ok` only is provably equivalent. No migration, no new config, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** new `GitHubRepoProbeTest` (the classification matrix: `Ok`/`Unresolvable`/`Http` 401·403·404·500·hint-table/`Network`, via `GH_TOKEN` + `Http::fake`); new `BridgeCommandsTest::test_check_classifies_the_reconcile_token_probe_status_into_a_hint` (401) + `test_check_classifies_a_403_probe_as_a_scope_hint` (403) — each reds when the check-side hint is reverted. *(Note: Laravel's `expectsOutputToContain` registers one Mockery `->once()` per substring, so two substrings from one warn line collide — each hint assertion is a single contiguous substring.)* Existing `ReconcileCommandTest` (auth-probe-names-leg, repo-probe-skip) + `BridgeCommandsTest` (resolved-token-invalid-warns) stay green, proving reconcile's behavior is preserved.
**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Writeback/GitHubRepoProbe.php` + `GitHubRepoProbeResult.php` + `GitHubRepoProbeKind.php`; `ReconcileCommand` + `CheckCommand` route their probe loop through it and drop the now-unused imports (`GitHubReadClient` from both; `GitHubTokenResolver` from `ReconcileCommand` — `CheckCommand` keeps it for the DL-207 promote-token file check; `RequestException` from `CheckCommand`). Supersedes the DL-186 note that `CheckCommand` re-imports `GitHubReadClient`/`RequestException` (that inline probe is now the shared primitive). Doc-sync: `docs/writeback.md` — the `bridge:check` validity-probe sentence notes it now carries reconcile's status hint. No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. Card #4496.

## DL-211 — The two path-segment sanitizers (`PathHelper::sanitizeSegment`, `BridgePaths::sanitizeAgent`) consolidate into one primitive with the stricter dot-stripping/run-collapsing/non-empty semantics; migration proven unnecessary by empirical zero-files on the only live instance

**Date:** 2026-07-17
**Context:** One behavior — turn an opaque caller key into one filesystem-safe path segment — had two divergent implementations (dedup audit F4, card #4497). `PathHelper::sanitizeSegment` (`preg_replace('/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/','_',$v) ?? ''`) **kept dots**, did **not** collapse runs, and fell back to `''`; it backs `registry-<targetId>.jsonl` (`RegistryAppendHandler:20`) and `spawn-<targetId>.log` (`SpawnDetachedHandler:68`). `BridgePaths::sanitizeAgent` (`preg_replace('/[^a-z0-9_-]+/i','_',$a) ?? ''` then `''=>'agent'`) **stripped dots**, collapsed runs (via `+`), and fell back to `'agent'`; it backs `inbox-<agent>.jsonl` / `inbox-seen-<agent>.json` (`BridgePaths:90,95`). The drift was empirically divergent (`foo.bar`→`foo.bar` vs `foo_bar`; `a...b`→`a___b` vs `a_b`; `''`→`''` vs `'agent'`), and `sanitizeSegment` left `..` **intact** — a latent traversal hazard, not live-exploitable today only because every call-site wraps the output between a literal `registry-`/`spawn-` prefix and a suffix and sanitizes `/`, so no bare `..` component forms; any future caller using the output as a standalone path component would get real traversal. The canon #5/#7 shape: one behavior, two copies, and the traversal-safe semantics reached only one.
**Decision:** one primitive — `PathHelper::sanitizeSegment(string $value, string $fallback = '_')` takes the **stricter** semantics (`preg_replace('/[^a-z0-9_-]+/i','_',$value) ?? ''`, then `''=>$fallback`): dots are stripped and runs collapse, so a `.`/`..` component **can never form** and the result is safe as a *standalone* segment, not only when wrapped. `BridgePaths::sanitizeAgent` becomes a thin delegate `PathHelper::sanitizeSegment($agent, 'agent')` — regex + `'agent'` fallback identical to before, so its output is **byte-identical**. `registry_append`/`spawn_detached` keep calling `PathHelper::sanitizeSegment($target->targetId)` (now stricter). The stricter direction is the audit's deliberate choice: it is slightly **lossier** (`a.b` and `a_b` both →`a_b`; `a//b` and `a/b` both →`a_b`), but each is an append-only ledger / detached-spawn log whose lines carry the true `target_id` in-body (`RegistryAppendHandler:24`, `SpawnDetachedHandler:88`), so a reader disambiguates — and the traversal-safety + dedup win dominates. No core classifier emits either opt-in handler today (custom-classifier extension points), so the collision + the new empty-id fallback (`registry-.jsonl`→`registry-_.jsonl`) are unreached in the shipped fleet.
**Migration (the audit's flagged HIGH risk) — proven unnecessary, not deferred:** both sanitizers back persistent on-disk files, so a naive regex swap would rename/orphan existing `registry-*`/`spawn-*`/`inbox-<agent>-*`/`inbox-seen-<agent>-*` files. Resolved by the *"prove keys unaffected"* branch, empirically: the fleet's **only** live bridge instance (`/home/kanban/.config/agent-webhook-bridge-prod/state/`) contains **only** `inbox.jsonl` + `inbox-seen.json` — the SHARED-layout paths that bypass **both** sanitizers (`inbox-seen.json` is `InboxCommand::seenPath()`'s `$agent===null` branch, not `agentSeenPath`). Zero sanitizer-derived files exist (verified across prod + dev installs), so a clean swap orphans nothing; and the `sanitizeAgent` (inbox/seen) side is byte-identical regardless, so even future per-agent files match today's naming. A rename step would be defending against a state that cannot happen (canon #6).
**Behavior:** inbox/seen naming — **unchanged** (byte-identical delegate). registry/spawn naming — **stricter**: dots stripped, runs collapsed, `..` neutralized to `_`, empty targetId →`registry-_.jsonl`/`spawn-_.log` (was `registry-.jsonl`). No API receiver accept/reject change, no error-handling change, no new config, no token-scope change.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `PathHelperSanitizeSegmentTest` (the full matrix: dot-strip, version-dots, `..`/`a..b` neutralized, run-collapse, all-invalid→single `_`, empty→default and caller fallback, non-empty-never-hits-fallback, never-a-traversal-component); `FileHandlersTest::test_registry_append_strips_dots_from_target_id` (`v1.2.3`→`registry-v1_2_3.jsonl`, reds against the pre-consolidation regex which keeps the dots). `BridgePathsSanitizeAgentTest` is a characterization/no-change lock — it passes pre- and post-change (asserting the delegate did not alter `sanitizeAgent`). Verified the drift assertions red against the old regex (`v1.2.3`→`v1.2.3`, `..`→`..`, `a///b`→`a___b`).
**Consequences:** `PathHelper::sanitizeSegment` gains the `$fallback` param + stricter regex; `BridgePaths::sanitizeAgent` drops its own regex and delegates (same-namespace, no import). No doc stated the old charset except the `sanitizeSegment` docblock (updated); `docs/customization.md` + `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` references to `registry-<target>.jsonl`/`spawn-<sanitized-target>.log` are charset-agnostic and stay accurate. 994/994 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean; adversarial impl-review APPROVE (migration proof + byte-identical claim independently re-verified). Card #4497.

## DL-212 — `bridge:prune` sweeps seen-cursors independently (`glob inbox-seen*.json`) instead of pairing each to an inbox file, closing the DL-012 retention gap for shared-layout per-agent cursors; the read/write/path cursor primitives hoist to `BridgePaths` (kills the Inbox↔Prune dup)

**Date:** 2026-07-17
**Context:** Dedup audit F5 (card #4498), two coupled findings on the seen-cursor. **(1) Duplication:** the seen-cursor read/write/path shape was implemented twice — `InboxCommand` (`seenPath`/`readSeen`/`writeSeen`, the writer) and `PruneCommand` (`seenPathFor`/the read+write inside `pruneSeen`, the retention side); the write bodies were byte-identical and the two path derivations, though computed differently (Inbox from the agent, Prune reconstructed from the inbox-file basename), resolved to the same file for every paired inbox. **(2) Latent retention bug (DL-012 gap):** `pruneInboxFiles` bounded seen-cursors by iterating inbox **files** (`glob(inbox*.jsonl)`) and deriving each file's paired cursor. Under `shared` inbox layout with `bridge.default_agent` set (or any `--agent` run), `bridge:inbox` resolves a non-null agent, reads the **shared** `inbox.jsonl` via the `agentInboxLines` fallback (no per-agent `inbox-<agent>.jsonl` exists on disk), yet advances the cursor at `inbox-seen-<agent>.json`. Prune's file-sweep finds only `inbox.jsonl` → bounds only `inbox-seen.json`, and **never** visits `inbox-seen-<agent>.json` (there is no `inbox-<agent>.jsonl` to pair it with) → that cursor grows **unbounded**, defeating the DL-012 retention guarantee for exactly that file. The canon #5/#7 shape again: one behavior in two copies, and the retention invariant reached only one derivation of the pairing.
**Decision:**
  - **Prune enumerates cursors, not inbox files.** After trimming every `inbox*.jsonl` to the surviving lines (unchanged), it sweeps `glob(inbox-seen*.json)` and bounds **each** cursor against the ids that survive. A cursor with no paired inbox file (the shared-layout per-agent case) is now visited and bounded like any other — the gap closes.
  - **Bound against the union of all surviving ids — provably the exact per-agent bound.** An intent id embeds its agent (`id = delivery_id:agentName:index`, `IntentLog`), so every id in agent A's cursor can only ever match an A-tagged line. Intersecting each cursor against the union of surviving ids across all inbox files therefore equals the precise per-agent bound, with **no reconstruction of the agent name from the (sanitized, DL-211-lossy) cursor filename** — which would over-prune a cursor whose agent name differs from its sanitized form (e.g. `foo.bar` → `inbox-seen-foo_bar.json`, then a `line.agent === "foo_bar"` filter matches nothing and empties the cursor, re-surfacing every seen intent). The union avoids that failure mode entirely and is strictly safe (an id is only dropped when its line aged out everywhere).
  - **Hoist the cursor primitives to `BridgePaths`** — `seenPath(?agent)` (null → `inbox-seen.json`, else `agentSeenPath`), `readSeen(path)`, `writeSeen(path,ids)` — so the writer (`bridge:inbox`) and the retention prune can never derive the path or (de)serialize the cursor two different ways. `InboxCommand` calls them and drops its three private copies; `PruneCommand::pruneSeen` reads via `readSeen`/writes via `writeSeen` and `seenPathFor` is **deleted** (the file-pairing derivation it existed to compute is gone).
  - **Skip the no-op cursor write.** Because the sweep now touches every cursor each run (not only those whose paired file was trimmed), `pruneSeen` returns early when the intersection equals the current set — so an unchanged cursor's mtime is never churned.
**Behavior (the intended change):** a `shared`-layout install running `bridge:inbox --agent=<x>` / `BRIDGE_DEFAULT_AGENT` now has its `inbox-seen-<x>.json` bounded by `bridge:prune --older-than` where before it grew forever. This **changes what Prune trims** — the whole point of the fix. No change to inbox-file trimming, to the shared `inbox-seen.json` path, to dry-run (still writes no cursor), to receiver accept/reject, error handling, config, or token scope.
**Migration risk — medium, but no on-disk rename and self-healing:** the change is purely a behavior change (which cursors get bounded), not a file-format/name change, so there is nothing to migrate on disk. A cursor the old code left unbounded is **retroactively** bounded on the first post-fix prune (ids whose lines already aged out are intersected away) — the fix heals the state the bug produced. Worst case on any single prune is that an id present only in a cursor but in no surviving line is dropped from that cursor, which is precisely the DL-012 intent.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `BridgeCommandsTest::test_prune_bounds_a_shared_layout_per_agent_seen_cursor` — the positive control: a shared `inbox.jsonl` holding two `pm`-tagged lines (one aged out) + an `inbox-seen-pm.json` with **no** `inbox-pm.jsonl`; asserts the aged id is bounded out of `inbox-seen-pm.json` (reds against the file-paired sweep, which leaves it) while the harness-sanity assertion on the trimmed shared inbox passes. `test_prune_dry_run_leaves_per_agent_seen_cursor_untouched` locks the dry-run no-write. Existing `test_prune_trims_inbox_lines_and_seen_cursor` (shared cursor) + the per-agent `bridge:inbox` cursor tests still pass unchanged.
**Consequences:** `BridgePaths` gains `seenPath`/`readSeen`/`writeSeen`; `InboxCommand` loses its three private cursor methods; `PruneCommand` loses `seenPathFor`, restructures `pruneInboxFiles` to a file-trim pass + a cursor sweep, and routes `pruneSeen` through the shared primitives. Supersedes the **mechanism** described in DL-012's decision (which paired the cursor to the inbox file) while keeping its **intent** (exact-id set bounded by the trimmed inbox) — DL-012 stays as the historical record of the original design. No doc described the internal pairing (the `docs/reviews/2026-05-31-*` mentions are dated archives and their exact-id-set claim stays true; `docs/config-schema.md` / `docs/consumer-guide.md` / `docs/multi-agent.md` cursor references are charset/mechanism-agnostic and stay accurate). 996/996 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. Card #4498.
