## DL-213 — `comment_to` becomes a `wake_membership` fleet DEFAULT (`[to_me, to_all]` → `[to_me, to_all, comment_to]`); a straight default-flip (no guarded-default), plus a `bridge:check` warn for the explicit-narrow population the flip can't reach; `from_me` stays opt-in

**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Context:** Roundtable #87 (sola-pm FR, converged 3/3). The most common coordination flow — post to a counterparty, wait for their directed reply — was dark out of the box: `comment_to` (DL-192), the body-`TO:<self>` grant that live-wakes a cross-thread pull-in, was an opt-in absent from the inherited default `[to_me, to_all]`. An install with no explicit `wake_membership` never live-woke on a comment addressed TO it on a thread it neither opened nor was labelled on; those replies downgraded to SessionStart pickup. Two wild populations (6/6 fleet seats): absent-key installs (inherit the default) and explicit-narrow installs (`[to_me, to_all]` set deliberately, pre-flip).
**Decision — a STRAIGHT default-flip, not a DL-204-style guarded default.** `wake_membership`'s default becomes `[to_me, to_all, comment_to]` at the one source (`CoordinationClassifier` classify + the `strings('wake_membership', …)` default). It does **not** need the "absent → on iff sibling-key present" guard DL-204 used, and the reason is structural: DL-204 (`move_coord_cards`) guarded a leg with a **required sibling key** (`coord_card_terminal_stage_id`) whose naive `default:true` would **throw at load** on an under-configured install. `comment_to` has **no such sibling** — it is self-contained and inert outside the `coord-message` family (the comment branch only runs there), so there is no partial-config throw to guard; a guard here would defend a failure mode that cannot occur. Three properties make the flip safe (all verified at source): **(1) additive-only** — the grant only ever *grants* on a comment whose body `TO:` names the agent; the unconditional narrow (a comment addressed to someone else denies membership) is untouched, so it drops nothing; **(2) echo-safe by construction** — `comment_to` keys on `RecipientAddressing::addresses(body, me)`, the comment's directed `TO:` line, **not authorship**, so under the shared account (all seats post as one identity) a comment the agent itself authored TO someone else does not wake it (this is precisely why `from_me` — which keys on `from:<me>` thread membership — is the wrong knob and stays opt-in); **(3) no over-wake** — every wake it adds is a comment that named the agent (sola's replay: device dropped→delivered on the `comment_to` add, backend/inventory correctly stayed dropped).
**`from_me` stays OFF in the default** — it is the over-wake/self-wake knob (wake on ALL activity on threads you opened); unchanged, opt-in.
**Necessary complement — a `bridge:check` warn.** A default only reaches installs with **no explicit** `wake_membership`. An install that set it explicitly before the flip **overrides** the default, so its directed-reply wakes stay dark — and the flip must not silently rewrite a deliberate operator config. `bridge:check` warns on exactly that population: `coord-message` family on **+** explicit `wake_membership` present **+** `comment_to` omitted → "directed replies are dark; add `comment_to` to catch them, or leave it off deliberately." Absent-key installs get no warn (the default now covers them). Presence is detected via a new `ClassifierConfig::has()` (explicit-key test, distinct from the resolved value); the warn parses `wake_membership` lazily inside a per-agent try/catch (mirrors the DL-197 `ci_failure_workflow_patterns` warn — a malformed value surfaces cleanly instead of aborting the run).
**Behavior:** an install with no explicit `wake_membership` starts live-waking on comment-directed replies (`TO:<self>`); every other membership class, the narrow, the no-`TO:` label-fallback, `from_me`, and inbox-staging are byte-identical. No migration, no new config key, no receiver accept/reject change, no error-handling change, no token-scope change. An install already listing `comment_to`, or one that explicitly omits it by choice, is byte-identical.
**UPGRADING:** an install with **no explicit** `wake_membership` will start live-waking on comment-directed replies after this flip; set `wake_membership` explicitly (omitting `comment_to`) to keep them dark.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `CoordinationClassifierTest` — a comment `TO:<self>` on a thread NOT labelled to the agent, with NO explicit `wake_membership`, now live-wakes (reds against the pre-flip `[to_me, to_all]` default, which returns null); the echo-safe case (a self-authored comment TO someone else does not wake) locks property (2). `BridgeCommandsTest` — explicit `[to_me, to_all]` + coord-message ⇒ the `wake_membership`/`comment_to` warn fires (exit 0); absent `wake_membership` ⇒ NO warn (the default covers it); explicit list WITH `comment_to` ⇒ NO warn; a malformed `wake_membership` fails per-agent (exit 1).
**Consequences:** `ClassifierConfig` gains `has()`; `CoordinationClassifier`'s default membership list + its docblock/inline comments update; `CheckCommand` gains the explicit-narrow warn; `docs/config-schema.md` `wake_membership` default + the comment_to default-OFF→ON prose + an UPGRADING note update in the same PR. Card #4632.

## DL-214 — `issue_population` (`prefixed` default | `all`): the general non-prefixed coordination issue → card writeback, correlated by the `github_issue` by-ref key (roundtable #18(b))

**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Context:** Roundtable #18(b), design-converged 3/3 (sola-pm + aimla-pm). DL-198/DL-200 real-time a coordination issue's card only when its title carries a recognized `[PREFIX]` (`stableId` non-null), correlated by the `id:<sid>` tag. The remaining #18(b) leg is the **general** case — card **any** coordination issue (`[PROPOSAL]`, `[FR]`, plain titles) that the prefix set doesn't recognize. The kanban half already shipped: `github_issue` is a live by-ref correlation system (kanban DL-203, v0.32.0), **verified end-to-end on the shared prod server** (canon #9 — card 4642 on board 5: `by-ref?system=github_issue&ref=990001` resolves; the ref derives from the `issue_number` payload key, NOT `external_link`). This DL is the **bridge-only** half.
**Decision — ONE `issue_population` axis + a PER-ISSUE correlation key, NOT a new family.** A per-mapping `issue_population` (`prefixed` default | `all`) on `WritebackConfig`, consumed by the existing `coord-card-create`/`coord-card-move` families and their handlers (canon #5 — consolidate, no sibling family, no `correlation_mode` axis). The correlation key is chosen **per issue, never per mapping**: a **prefixed** issue (`stableId` non-null) always uses the `id:<sid>` **tag** (unchanged DL-198, the same key the tag-keyed reconcile uses — so bridge and reconcile never double-card a prefixed issue); a **non-prefixed** issue (`stableId` null, only under `all`) uses the `github_issue` **by-ref** key (`KanbanClient::correlateIssue` → the by-ref endpoint; the card stamps `issue_number` in its payload so the ref derives). `prefixed` is **byte-identical DL-198/200** (empty payload, `[id:, type:]` tags, tag-only correlation). Under `all` a prefixed card is **dual-keyed** (tag + `issue_number`), and the create/move **unified pre-check tests BOTH derivable keys** — closing the DL-198 reconcile race AND the edge where an issue's title gains/loses a prefix between `opened` and `reopened` (found + fixed in design review; a per-mapping mode would double-card it).
**Handler fork (each step RED-on-revert tested).** The create/move handlers' sid-required guard becomes **conditional** — sid required only on the tag path; the by-ref path carries an empty sid legitimately, and an empty-sid target under `population=prefixed` (no derivable key) **fails closed**. The create stamps every eligible key + per-key post-create collapse; the move correlates by tag and/or by-ref (union under `all`).
**Correctness rests on a verified server property, not a spec both sides re-implement (canon #5/#12).** Both the bridge and sola's reconcile (framework #299) correlate by **hitting the by-ref endpoint** — canonicalization is kanban's, so parity is a server property. sola's real-surface probe found `github_pr` empty on their board 3; root-caused (same physical multi-tenant server as boards 5/9/10 where it resolves) to a **per-card stamping gap** (their cards stamped a divergent `github_pr_number` key, not the recognized `pr_number`) — NOT a mechanism failure and NOT a reason to alias a second key (migrate producers to the one key).
**`bridge:check` preflights (converged config surface).** Under `population: all`: **(a) FAIL-CLOSED** (exit non-zero) if the board doesn't register the `issue_number` custom field — an absent field 422s every by-ref create as a permanent no-op, and an empty by-ref lookup is byte-identical to "not indexed" (an unknown `system` returns the same empty), so the sole real-time mover would silently double-card; **(b)** a **non-prefixed no-backstop warn** (the prefix/tag-keyed reconcile ignores non-prefixed issues; the consumer must extend its reconcile to correlate by-ref, else a bridge-missed non-prefixed event self-heals nowhere); **(c)** a **three-state cross-config compare** (agree / DISAGREE / CANNOT-VERIFY, warn-never-fail) binding the bridge's runtime `issue_population` (`writeback.json`, FPM-reachable) to the reconcile's (`$COORD_CONFIG` `kanban.boards[].issue_population`, absent ⇒ prefixed) — `bridge=all` + `reconcile=prefixed` is the checkable no-backstop gap. The compare reuses the DL-200 CLI-only `$COORD_CONFIG` read (the FPM webhook path cannot read `$COORD_CONFIG` — verified — which is why the bridge's runtime axis lives in `writeback.json`, not there). **NO `isAlreadyClassified` content-sniff** (R2 dropped it — it would be a fleet-wide triage regression); the echo guard stays `identity_id`.
**Behavior:** absent `issue_population` ⇒ `prefixed` ⇒ byte-identical DL-198/200. Only an explicit `issue_population: all` adds the by-ref complement. No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. Validation order (roundtable): aimla board-10 (prefixed, byte-identical positive control) first → sola board-2/3 (non-prefixed leg, with sola's #299 reconcile backstop in place) second.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `WritebackConfigTest` (population parse + fail-closed on unknown value); `KanbanClientTest` (`correlateIssue` hits by-ref with `system=github_issue` + canonical `source`); `CoordinationCard{Create,Move}ClassifierTest` (non-prefixed carded/moved only under `all`, sid null; prefixed + prefixed-default byte-identical); `KanbanCoordCard{,Move}HandlerTest` (by-ref create with `issue_number` payload + no `id:` tag; dual-key under `all`; prefix-change-edge skip; by-ref move; empty-sid-under-prefixed fail-closed); `CoordConfigTerminalsTest` (`issuePopulationsForBoardId` resolution); `BridgeCommandsTest` (fail-closed on missing `issue_number`; agree/DISAGREE/CANNOT-VERIFY compare). `ExternalReferenceNormalizer` gains `github_issue` (completing the bridge's mirror of kanban's closed system set). Doc-sync: `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` `{dl, github_pr}` → add `github_issue` + the ref-from-payload-key / empty-vs-unindexed contract; `docs/config-schema.md` + `docs/writeback.md` the `issue_population` axis. Card #4553.

## DL-215 — `coord_non_addressed_disposition` (`drop` default | `inbox_stage`): the coord-message sibling of `impl_non_wake_disposition` — a durable inbox backstop for the non-addressed coordination event

**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Context:** Roundtable #90 (bridge-classifier unification, converged 3/3 with sola-pm + aimla-pm). A PM seat that retires a custom `SolaPmClassifier` to the generic `CoordinationClassifier` has two completeness-backstop models for coordination events it isn't directly addressed on: **(a)** aimla's — addressed-only live-wake plus a **GitHub-direct SessionStart sweep** as the net (the bridge inbox is not load-bearing); or **(b)** keep the **bridge inbox** as the durable net. `coord-message`'s recipient gate (`if (! $forMe) return null;`) gate-DROPS every non-addressed event, so path (b) had no generic knob — while the sibling `impl-ci-wake` family already ships exactly this seam (`impl_non_wake_disposition: inbox_stage`, DL-190), which stages a non-wake event to the inbox instead of dropping it. That asymmetry — one family carries the disposition, its sibling does not — is a gap in the generic classifier independent of any one seat's migration.
**Decision — mirror the existing seam, do NOT mint a new mechanism (canon #5).** Add `coord_non_addressed_disposition` (`drop` default | `inbox_stage`) to the `coord-message` family, semantically identical to `impl_non_wake_disposition`: default `drop` gate-drops (byte-identical to pre-DL-215); `inbox_stage` builds the **normal** coord `Intent` (`coord_issue`/`coord_pr`/`coord_comment`) with **no** `channel_push` — staged to the durable inbox, never a live wake. It softens **only** the recipient gate (`$forMe`): the earlier `subject === null` (unhandled action) and `drop_title_all_of` (noise-title) drops still return null for **both** dispositions, and an **addressed** event still live-wakes (`targets: $forMe ? wakePush(...) : []`). Reattribution (§1) runs on the staged path too, so the inbox record carries the recovered author. Any value other than `inbox_stage` falls back to `drop` (mirrors the sibling). NOT gated on a new family and NOT a `bridge:check` warn — parity with `impl_non_wake_disposition`, which has neither.
**Why the seam is echo-safe under a shared account.** Under `inbox_stage` a shared-account seat's own outbound coordination posts (`TO:` someone else) would stage to its inbox — acceptable and symmetric with `impl_non_wake_disposition` (which likewise stages the seat's own pushes); the primary own-write suppression remains the dispatcher's pre-classify echo gate (identity-keyed), unchanged. The seam decouples "durable inbox record" from "live wake"; it never widens the WAKE past the recipient gate (a non-addressed event gets `targets: []` in every channel mode, incl. `route_intents:true`, where the staged intent is routed like any other — no double-wake, and no hand-emit added).
**Behavior:** absent `coord_non_addressed_disposition` ⇒ `drop` ⇒ byte-identical to pre-DL-215. Only an explicit `inbox_stage` stages non-addressed events. No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change. Path (a) needs no bridge change (this DL is for seats taking path (b)); sola's stated lean is (a), so this ships as adopt-at-tag with no current consumer — closing the generic-classifier asymmetry regardless.
**Tests (`CoordinationClassifierTest`):** three **revert-reds** (fail if the production change is reverted) — `inbox_stage` stages `coord_issue` with `targets: []` + reattribution intact; a comment whose body `TO:` narrows to someone else is inbox-staged (still `coord_comment`, no push, exercising the `$addressed === false` branch); `route_intents:true` stages the intent with no hand-emit. Plus four **back-compat / mutation guards** (pass under revert by design — they pin the preserved behavior the seam must not break): default `drop`s a non-addressed event; an addressed event still wakes under `inbox_stage`; the earlier subject/noise drops still fire under `inbox_stage` (positive control that both precede the recipient gate); an unknown value falls back to `drop`. Doc-sync: `docs/config-schema.md` (new row beside `wake_membership`/`impl_non_wake_disposition`) + the `CoordinationClassifier` class docblock (coord-message bullet). Card #4650.

## DL-216 — `BridgePaths::updateSeenLocked`: the locked read-modify-write for a seen-cursor (closes the #4630 RMW-clobber race); `writeSeen` retired

**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Context:** DL-199 review point 1 (this file) identified — but deliberately did not close (canon #6 scope) — a seen-cursor sibling of the inbox lost-update race it fixed. `bridge:inbox` advances a cursor with an UNLOCKED `readSeen` → merge → `writeSeen`, and the DL-212 prune sweep does an unlocked `readSeen` → intersect → `writeSeen` on the same file. `writeSeen` locked only the write, not the read-modify-write around it, so a prune landing between inbox's read and its write could write an intersection computed from the pre-advance cursor, dropping a just-marked id back to unseen. Consequence is BOUNDED — one re-delivered wake, never data loss: DL-012's read-side collapse dedups duplicate unseen ids within a single inbox read. Filed as card #4630.
**Decision — add the locked RMW primitive and route BOTH callers through it (canon #5/#7).** New `BridgePaths::updateSeenLocked(path, transform)`, the JSON-array sibling of `filterJsonlLocked`: it holds ONE `flock(LOCK_EX)` across read → `$transform` → write, skips the write when the transform returns an unchanged set (mtime-churn parity with the old `pruneSeen` early-return), and creates a missing cursor (`c+`). `InboxCommand` and `RetentionService::pruneSeen` both go through it — the inbox advance now merges onto the cursor read UNDER the lock (not the earlier unlocked `readSeen` at the top of the command), so a concurrent prune can neither clobber nor be clobbered. `writeSeen` is **retired**: its only two callers now use the locked RMW, so `updateSeenLocked` is the sole cursor writer — the unlocked-write primitive that let the race exist is gone, not merely unused (canon #7). `readSeen` stays for the non-mutating unseen-scan (a slightly stale filter read is harmless — the advance re-reads under the lock); the JSON parse is hoisted to one `decodeSeen` home shared by `readSeen` and `updateSeenLocked`.
**Behavior:** byte-identical on-disk cursor format and single-process semantics; the change is purely the concurrency guarantee. No config, no migration, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `BridgePathsSeenLockedTest` — the lock-held-across-the-whole-RMW probe (a second `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` inside the transform must fail; reds if the lock is dropped, mirroring `BridgePathsRewriteLockedTest`), the transform-sees-the-locked-read invariant, the no-change-no-rewrite mtime guard, missing-file-creates, garbage-decodes-to-`[]`, and shrinking-write-leaves-no-garbage. The DL-212 prune + inbox cursor-advance behavior tests (`BridgeCommandsTest`) stay green unchanged — the behavior-preservation guard. Card #4630.

## DL-217 — Two-way board tools: a loopback-gated, channel-identity-scoped request/response surface (`board_my_cards` read-proxy + `board_create_card` own-swimlane write) so an impl seat with no kanban token gets a board window

**Date:** 2026-07-20
**Context:** The bridge was strictly one-way: it pushes wake events, and an impl agent with no kanban token / no toolkit had no way to see or capture its own board work (aimla's PM-side `STATE/agent-cards/<agent>.md` was the stopgap). Roundtable #102 (from aimla-pm, cc sola-pm) asked for a request/response upgrade. Investigation confirmed the bridge had NO tool-registration seam: the channel is one-way at every layer (`ChannelPushHandler` reads only the ACK; the reference Node MCP server declares only `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`, zero `setRequestHandler`). So the seam is build-step 1, not a reuse. Converged over five fresh-adversarial review rounds + 3-way roundtable convergence (design comment #5017099438).
**Decision — three thin-edge/fat-middle pieces, opt-in + fail-closed end to end.** (1) The Node channel server, env-gated by `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOOLS=1`, advertises a `tools` capability and PROXIES `tools/call` to the bridge over HTTP loopback with a per-agent bearer — a dumb pipe (no board logic, no kanban token, no retry); a half-configured server returns a structured refusal naming the activating config. (2) A new `POST /agent-tools/call` in Laravel, **network-gated FIRST**: the `LoopbackOnly` middleware tests the TCP peer (`$request->ip()` ∈ `127.0.0.0/8` + `::1`) — deliberately NOT `LocalhostUrl::assertValid` (that validates an outbound URL host string; a category error), sound only under the documented no-`TrustProxies` posture (a code comment names the dependency). The per-agent bearer is defense-in-depth ON TOP: token→agent is a NEW iterate-and-`hash_equals` index (the AgentRegistry carries no tokens), fail-closed on an unreadable token (per-agent) and on a token collision (BOTH agents refuse); the agent name is DERIVED from the token, never the body. (3) Two tool classes on a new `BoardToolsRegistry` (a `HandlerRegistry` sibling), running on the existing `WritebackClientFactory` least-privilege client — the kanban token never leaves the box.
**Authz shape:** one new per-agent secret-file key `board_tools.auth.token_path` (same class as every token, provision-minted; HTTP installs may alias it to the channel token file) — the FR's "no new credential class" does not survive the config layer (`resolveChannel` throws if `channel.auth.token_path` is set without `channel.url`, so the tools bearer can't ride the existing key). The write scope (`board_id`/`swimlane_id`/`create_stage_id`, optional `shared_swimlane_id`/`coord_board_id`/`address_tags`) lives in the same per-agent `board_tools:` block — agent-keyed authz belongs on the agent config, not repo-keyed `writeback.json`. Parse posture mirrors `create_coord_cards`: absent ⇒ byte-identical no-op; present-but-malformed ⇒ throws at load.
**Tool contracts (v1):** `board_my_cards` returns the caller's own swimlane grouped by stage + shared swimlane + coord cards addressed via `address_tags` (when `coord_board_id` set), via `tasks/search.json` with the new kanban `swimlane_id=` q-term AND a bridge-side row filter that DROPS+logs any non-matching-swimlane row — per-agent read isolation is 100% bridge-enforced (kanban scopes reads by the token USER's board membership, never by swimlane). `board_create_card` forces the swimlane from config (args cannot name it), stamps `created-by:<agent>` and `idem:<agent>:<key>`, REJECTS caller tags matching reserved prefixes (`created-by:`/`idem:`/`id:`/`type:`) and the bare `triaged` (422-class), constrains `idempotency_key` to `[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,64}` (its `"`/`*`/`_`/`%` are kanban tag-search metacharacters), runs the full DL-198 both legs (correlate-before-create + post-create re-read + `CardCollapse`), payload `{}`, born untriaged (the triage contract).
**Alternatives rejected:** bearer-only on the internet-reachable vhost (below the webhook HMAC bar → loopback-gate first); a secret-keyed token map ("constant-time" + hash-keyed contradict — iterate/`hash_equals`); a `tool_calls` ledger table (v2 — v1 audit is one structured log line per call); stamping `origin` (a custom field only some boards register → permanent 422 — identity rides the tag); escaping `_`/`%` in kanban's exact tag-search branch (the cleaner fix-the-primitive, but a hard-gate change to a shared endpoint — filed kanban card#4745, out of scope).
**Behavior:** absent `board_tools` AND absent `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOOLS` ⇒ byte-identical existing behavior (proven by test). New ingress only; does NOT pass the webhook HMAC / `dedupCreate` / classifier — single-writer invariant preserved precisely as "the kanban token + writer never leave the box", with its own audit trail. **Functional prerequisite:** kanban's `tasks/search.json` `swimlane_id=` term (a sibling of `workflow_stage_id=`); an un-upgraded kanban returns empty (broken-but-safe, never the whole board). **Owed verification debt:** the multi-host forward-tunnel leg + the `authorized_keys` correction (`no-port-forwarding` forbids `-L` AND `-R`; drop it, scope with `permitlisten`/`permitopen`) are documented but exercised only when the first genuinely multi-host seat is built (prod is same-box).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `LoopbackOnlyTest` (127.0.0.0/8 + ::1 + ::ffff:127.* admitted; RFC1918/public/off-by-one/hostname/empty refused); `BoardToolsConfigTest` (parse posture); `AgentToolsCallTest` (loopback refusal mutation-checked — defeating the gate reds it 403→500 and the create runs; bearer success/unknown/collision-fail-closed; swimlane-force; reserved-tag matrix one-per-prefix + bare `triaged`; idem-key charset; idempotency both legs; foreign-swimlane row drop); `BridgeCommandsTest` (bridge:check board-tools swimlane/collision/ok probes). Card #4719, roundtable #102.

## DL-218 — GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier FR-7 conflict rule: a resolving DL whose card DIFFERS from a co-present explicit `card#` is a CONFLICT → warn + prefer the `card#` (foreign-DL-mention guard)

**Date:** 2026-07-21
**Context:** The FR-7 precedence in `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` had a hijack hole (card #4815, operator-approved hard-gate fix). When a merged PR's title/head carried a `DL-NNN` that RESOLVED to a card, the DL won unconditionally and any co-present `card#<id>` was merely info-logged as "ignored" — **without checking whether the `card#` named a DIFFERENT card**. So a descriptive/foreign DL mention in a title silently hijacked the move to the wrong card. Concretely: PR #148 "Static guard against **DL-219** re-introduction (card#4811)" — DL-219 resolves to card #4770 — moved #4770 and dropped the intended #4811; #4811 never moved. The `card#` is the specific, intentional correlation token; a DL can appear descriptively (a guard/reference PR naming another card's DL), so DL-wins-always is wrong when the two disagree.
**Decision (option a — prefer the explicit `card#` on a genuine conflict, warn loudly).** After `correlateDl` returns non-empty, compute the conflict via a single shared predicate `cardConflicts(?int $cardToken, list<int> $cardIds): bool` = `$cardToken !== null && ! in_array($cardToken, $cardIds, true)`. **No conflict** (no `card#`, or the `card#` IS one of the DL-resolved ids): behavior UNCHANGED — the DL wins (the agree-case info log is reworded from "the card# token is ignored" to "names the same card, so nothing is dropped"). **Conflict:** `Log::warning` LOUDLY naming the DL, its resolved card id(s), and the `card#`, stating the explicit `card#` is authoritative; then do NOT return the DL targets — fall through to the existing `card#<task-id>` path, which builds the `kanban_move_card` target for the `card#` and stamps refs. Net: the conflict path moves + stamps the `card#` card, not the DL card. Unchanged branches: DL-only-resolves still wins; DL-resolves-to-nothing still falls through to `card#` or warns high-value-miss; `card#`-only unchanged; dependabot untouched; shared-board `$sourceRepo` logic preserved.
**Applies to ALL THREE token-resolution sites via the shared `cardConflicts` predicate (canon #5 + #7 — the same defect shape appeared three times; ship all three or none).** (1) The move path (`classifyInner`) — a merged/opened PR's stage move. (2) `classifyPush` — the branch-create `started` move: SAME defect, SAME harm (a stage move); a branch like `card-4811-guard-DL-9-reintro` where DL-9 resolves elsewhere is a conflict → warn + move the `card#` + do not stamp the foreign DL (via `$conflictDl` → `stampRefs($branch, null, $conflictDl)`), mirroring the move path. (3) `correlatedCardIds` (the draft `block_reason` overlay, DL-193) — SAME defect, LOWER harm (a block-reason marker, not a move): on a conflict it returns `[$cardToken]` (the intended card gets the overlay) instead of the DL's `$cardIds`; it stays SILENT by design (the move path already logs on an opened-as-draft PR, so re-logging would double-log the same event). The predicate is defined ONCE and called at all three sites — no hand-copied conflict test.
**Sibling defect closed in the same change (canon #7):** the `card#` fallback stamps the sole DL in the text onto the selected card (FR #3866, for cards created before their DL). On a conflict that sole DL is FOREIGN (it belongs to a different card), so stamping it onto the `card#` card would re-introduce the hijack as a correlation POISON — the `card#` card would thereafter answer to the foreign DL. `stampRefs` gains a `?string $excludeDl` argument (the `stampRefs` docblock already declared this intent for the foreign-DL case); both the move-path and push-path conflict branches record the resolved-elsewhere DL and pass it so `stamp_dl` is dropped. The PR-number stamp still lands on the move path (it is genuinely this card's PR); the push path has no PR so no `stamp_pr`. Callers passing no `excludeDl` ⇒ byte-identical.
**Alternative considered:** warn + SKIP the move entirely on a conflict (emit no target). Rejected as more disruptive for the common foreign-mention case: the operator's explicit `card#` clearly names intent, so moving it (with a loud warning for the ledger) serves the PR better than a no-op that strands the intended card, while still surfacing the anomaly.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest`):** move path — `test_conflicting_card_token_overrides_the_dl_and_warns` (DL-9→card 7, title also `card#4811` ⇒ target 4811 not 7, `stamp_pr` present, `stamp_dl` ABSENT, warning logged; reverting the classifier reds it "7 is identical to 4811"), `test_dl_wins_when_a_co_present_card_token_names_the_same_card` (agree — DL-9→7 + `card#7` ⇒ target 7, no warning), `test_dl_only_move_targets_the_resolved_card` (lone DL, unchanged); push path — `test_conflicting_card_token_overrides_the_dl_on_a_branch_create_push` (branch `card-4811-guard-DL-9-reintro` ⇒ `started` target 4811 not 7, `stamp_dl`/`stamp_pr` ABSENT, warning); draft overlay — `test_draft_overlay_prefers_the_card_token_on_a_conflict` (converted_to_draft `DL-9 … card#4811` ⇒ `block_reason` target 4811 not 7, overlay silent). Card #4815.

## DL-219 — KanbanClient sends FLAT task-write bodies (no `{"task":{…}}` wrapper) — the bridge companion to kanban's DL-219, an initially-MISSED write consumer

**Date:** 2026-07-21
**Context:** kanban card#4770 / kanban DL-219 drops the `{"task":{…}}` request-body wrapper from its v3 write API: every write endpoint now takes task fields TOP-LEVEL/FLAT and **strict-rejects** an unknown top-level `task` key (422, no compatibility shim). The bridge's `app/Bridge/Writeback/KanbanClient.php` was a write consumer that the kanban-side cutover did NOT initially enumerate — it was still sending WRAPPED bodies at every task-write site. Once kanban prod flips to flat, a wrapped body 422s, so ALL bridge card automation (moves, ref stamps, block-reason writes, card creation) would break at the same instant. An exhaustive `app/` audit (grep `'task' =>` / `"task"` / `['task'` and every `->post('/tasks`/`->patch("/tasks`/`->put` body trace) found the wrapped writes confined to KanbanClient's four sites; every other `/tasks` call is a GET read; the archive/delete `['_action' => …]` bodies are TOP-LEVEL control keys (never `task`-wrapped) and are correctly left as-is; `KanbanProvisionClient` posts only to `/webhooks`, not `/tasks`.
**Decision — send flat at all four write sites, unconditionally (no version probe), matching kanban's no-shim cutover.** `moveCard` → `['workflow_stage_id' => $stageId]`; `stampCorrelationRefs` → `['payload' => $refs]`; `setBlockReason` → `['block_reason' => $reason]`; `createCard` → the assembled `$task` array posted flat (no `['task' => $task]` wrapper). The `_action` archive verb is untouched — it was always top-level, and the strict-key reject targets the `task` wrapper, not the `_action` control key. Docblocks referencing the `{"task":{…}}` shape (setBlockReason, archiveCard) are corrected to the flat shape + this DL reason. A version probe was rejected: kanban ships no shim and strict-rejects the wrapper, so there is no mixed regime to straddle — a probe would only add a failure surface for a state that cannot exist post-cutover.
**Lockstep (deploy contract):** this is one leg of a 3-way flat cutover. A flat bridge against a still-wrapped kanban 422s (kanban has no flat parser yet); a wrapped bridge against a flat kanban 422s (strict-key reject). The three move together: the kanban-flat upgrade, this bridge deploy, and the toolkit v0.20.0 install activate simultaneously. Do NOT deploy this bridge build ahead of the kanban-flat prod flip.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `KanbanClientTest` (move/create), `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` (move + ref-stamp — asserts `$r->data() === ['workflow_stage_id' => …]` / `['payload' => …]`, the whole flat body), `KanbanBlockReasonHandlerTest` (flat `block_reason`, incl. the null-clear via `array_key_exists`), `KanbanCoordCardHandlerTest` / `KanbanDependabotCardHandlerTest` / `AgentToolsCallTest` (flat create — top-level `board_id`/`workflow_stage_id`/`name`/`payload`/`tags`, each guarded by `! isset($r['task'])`), `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandlerTest` / `KanbanPromoteReleasedHandlerTest` / `ReconcileCommandTest` (flat move). Reverting the source to wrapped bodies reds 56 assertions across these files (proven). Card #4770 (kanban DL-219 companion), roundtable #118.

## DL-220 — Board-tools same-box enablement package: provision-minted bearer (`bridge:provision-tools`), live `bridge:check --probe-tools` isolation probe, the Apache/FPM endpoint runbook, and the XFF posture-pinning test (DL-217 delivery-gap closure)

**Date:** 2026-07-21
**Context:** aimla-pm's first-validation pass (roundtable #102, 2026-07-21) found the v0.63.0 board-tools surface short of turnkey on a same-box Apache→PHP-FPM install: no way to mint the bearer DL-217 had specified as "provision-minted" (`bridge:provision` registers webhook subscriptions only — a delivery gap against DL-217's own record); no live preflight for the loopback+bearer path; and the docs' "same-box installs call `127.0.0.1` directly" claim oversimplified to the point of being a trap. A correctness question rode along: does the `LoopbackOnly` gate hold behind Apache→mod_proxy_fcgi, where a reverse-proxy mental model predicts `REMOTE_ADDR` is the proxy and the client is in `X-Forwarded-For`?
**Gate finding (confirm, not change):** the gate IS sound on this topology — mod_proxy_fcgi forwards Apache's own connection peer as `REMOTE_ADDR` (this is not the separate-proxy-hop pattern), and `$request->ip()` returns it raw because the app registers no TrustProxies middleware, so a forged XFF is inert in both directions. But the posture was documented (LoopbackOnly header comment), not PINNED — a later `trustProxies('*')` would open the gate with zero red tests. Shipped: the XFF-spoof feature test pair (external peer + XFF `127.0.0.1` → 403 with no outbound call; loopback peer + external XFF → admitted), which goes red the moment a TrustProxies registration lands.
**Endpoint recipe (the trap):** `BRIDGE_TOOLS_ENDPOINT=https://<real-host>/agent-tools/call` on-box FAILS the gate — DNS resolves to the public IP and the kernel's local-route source selection makes the TCP peer the public IP, which the gate correctly refuses. Canonical same-box recipe: `/etc/hosts` loopback-pin of the bridge hostname + the https endpoint — TLS verification stays ON against the real cert, SNI selects the right vhost, peer is genuinely loopback. Plain `http://127.0.0.1/...` is the documented alternative with the default-vhost caveat. Lands as the docs/board-tools.md same-box runbook; the old "call `127.0.0.1` directly" line now points there.
**Provisioning shape:** `bridge:provision-tools {--agent=} {--dry-run}` mints the per-agent bearer at the configured `board_tools.auth.token_path` — 0600, idempotent (readable+secure existing file is a no-op), fail-loud on insecure perms (DL-010 posture), cross-agent collision detection at provision time (DL-217 fail-closes a collision at request time for BOTH agents; surfacing it at mint time beats discovering it on the first live call). It never edits agent YAML: for an explicitly-named agent without a `board_tools:` block it prints a paste-ready skeleton and exits non-zero (scaffold-by-print keeps hand-authored YAML the single write-surface). aimla's fallback shape (documented mint recipe + check-time flags) is subsumed.
**Preflight:** `bridge:check --probe-tools=<endpoint-url>` (opt-in — check stays offline by default; the endpoint value belongs to the channel server's env and cannot be derived bridge-side) exercises the real loopback+bearer path per configured agent with a live `board_my_cards` call, verifying reachability, bearer→agent resolution, and the swimlane isolation property — the exact property the first-validation seat (aimla, magento same-host) signed up to prove, now exercisable before flipping `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOOLS=1`. Failure modes are named (403 → endpoint recipe/peer; bearer failure → token path; refused → vhost), non-2xx or an isolation violation exits non-zero.
**Alternatives rejected:** editing agent YAML from the provision command (formatting/comment-preservation risk on a hand-authored file; print-to-paste is safer and idempotent-by-construction); an always-on live probe in `bridge:check` (check is used offline/CI; a network call needs opt-in); deriving the probe endpoint from bridge config (the value is channel-server-side by design — inventing a bridge-side copy would mint a second source of truth).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** XFF pair reds if LoopbackOnly trusts proxy headers; probe tests (Http::fake) cover success, 403→named-cause mapping, isolation-violation→non-zero. Card #4846, roundtable #102.

## DL-221 — The DL-resolution move path stamps PR provenance (`pr_number` + `pr_url`, sole-DL-gated, never `dl_number`); `pr_url` joins the stamped ref set on both paths (supersedes DL-187 point 1)

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** Observed live at the v0.65.0 release (card#4852): PR #357 (title carried its DL, no `card#` token) auto-moved card 4846 but stranded it without `pr_number`/`pr_url` — the DL-resolution path built bare move targets while only the `card#` fallback stamped (DL-187's deliberate stance). And no path stamped `pr_url` at all, though it is a registered payload key and drives kanban's multi-repo by-ref `source` derivation. The DL-187 rationale (a release PR naming a feature card's DL could poison its `pr_number`) predates two guards that now bound that risk: handler-side add-if-missing (#3866) and the DL-218 conflict machinery.
**Decision:** (1) `stampRefs` gains `stamp_pr_url` (from `pull_request.html_url`), emitted on both stamping paths; the handler writes `pr_url` add-if-missing exactly like `pr_number`, flat body (DL-219). (2) The DL-win branch now passes stamp refs into every per-card move target — with the resolved DL **excluded** (`dl_number` is never re-stamped on the DL path; identity-poison protection stands) and **gated on the sole-DL shape**: a title carrying 2+ `DL-NNN` tokens is bundled/descriptive (release-shaped), so its own PR refs are foreign to the resolved card and nothing is stamped (the move itself still fires — pre-existing behavior). The explicit-`card#` path stamps regardless of DL count: its token asserts "this PR tracks this card." (3) The `started` push path is byte-identical (no PR exists at branch-cut).
**Poison analysis (the DL-187 concern, re-examined):** the residual vector is a *sole-DL* foreign PR (a descriptive mention with no `card#`) arriving **before** the card's own PR event stamps — it would both mis-move (pre-existing DL-resolution class) and now stamp foreign PR refs, add-if-missing being the remaining guard. The dominant harm there is the mis-move, not the stamp; the multi-DL class (releases, bundles) is excluded by the gate, and a resolved-foreign DL alongside a `card#` is excluded by DL-218 + `excludeDl`. Accepted.
**Alternatives rejected:** stamping `dl_number` on the DL path (delivers nothing, identity-poison risk — DL-187's core point stands); leaving the DL path unstamped and hand-stamping at release time (the v0.65.0 experience: operator toil + the provenance gap this DL closes); gating the card# path's stamps on sole-DL too (the explicit token is the disambiguator — weakening it re-opens FR #3866).
**Supersedes:** DL-187 point 1's "only the `card#` fallback path stamps" is no longer the current invariant (this entry is the back-pointer a DL-187 reader needs). DL-187's `dl_number`-never-on-DL-path rationale is unchanged and load-bearing.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, all proven):** DL-only PR → targets carry `stamp_pr`+`stamp_pr_url`, never `stamp_dl` (reds on bare `moveTargets`); bundled DL → every target stamped; multi-DL title → moves but stamps nothing (reds without the sole-DL gate); handler `pr_url` add-if-missing + never-overwrite (reds without the `pr_url` block); card# path emits `stamp_pr_url`. Card #4852.

## DL-222 — Board-tools default-ON with maximal config reuse: bearer = the channel token, structural default-suppression ("a default block never throws"), tri-state channel advertise — supersedes DL-217's opt-in parse posture and DL-220's provision-minted default path

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** The fleet operator's ratified goals for the board-tools surface (roundtable #102 arc, bridge card#4907): consistency + config reuse above all; no root steps unless unavoidable; reuse the existing impl-agent↔bridge shared token; ONE channel-side config surface (.mcp.json — no mixed token-file/env regimes); everything defaults ON. aimla live-certified the bearer-isolation property solo (aliasing the channel push-token as the bearer + a loopback port — `--probe-tools → 200`, scoped to their lane), proving the mechanism sound and the enablement surface heavier than needed. Scope was operator-extended mid-design: EXISTING config surfaces converge on the same model, not just the new path. The design ran a SEVEN-round fresh-adversarial loop (must-fix trajectory 5→2→2→1→2→1→0; design record: card#4907's description carries the headlines).
**Decision — what defaults, what stays explicit, what throws:**
- **Bearer = the agent's channel token** (`channel.auth.token_path`), resolved once in `BoardToolsConfig` (tokenPath := `auth.token_path` alias ?? channel token). The alias is a DEPRECATION path, honored first — a pinned `.mcp.json` `BRIDGE_TOOLS_TOKEN_FILE` never silently flips bearer source mid-upgrade. **Named blast-radius widening (the accepted risk, on the record per aimla's bounding rationale):** the push-auth channel token now also buys own-lane board authority — own-swimlane reads + untriaged own-lane creates, bearer-isolated, loopback-gated, forced-scope. A channel-token compromise buys more than fake wakes; the bound is the DL-217 isolation set, all preserved (see disposition below).
- **THE RULE (structural):** classification precedes parsing. A block is EXPLICIT iff it is a mapping carrying strict-bool `enabled: true` — explicit malformation THROWS at load (DL-217 posture unchanged: an operator-written assertion that cannot be satisfied is malformed config). EVERYTHING else present is DEFAULT-CLASS and **never throws**: non-mapping blocks (incl. the bare `board_tools:` → YAML null), non-bool `enabled` (incl. `enabled: null`; also `yes`/`on` — symfony/yaml does NOT booleanize them), and any unsatisfiable requirement (missing bearer, incomplete scope, malformed optional) SUPPRESS: `enabled=false` + a `suppressedReason` that `bridge:check` renders as **FAIL**. Rationale: a config-load throw propagates through the all-or-nothing `SubscriptionRegistry` into `DispatchService` → an install-wide webhook 5xx storm — a DEFAULT may only ever enable, never break the fleet (the round-4 finding). Loud moved from load-time to check-time for the default class only; no silent cell exists.
- **What stays explicit, permanently:** the write-scope block `{board_id, swimlane_id, create_stage_id}` (caller-side placement would let the agent aim writes; the swimlane is the read-isolation boundary and is NOT derivable — the writeback mapping's `swimlaneId` is the repo-keyed DL-027 CREATE-lane, a semantically different field; deriving the security boundary from it is a category error) and the channel-side `BRIDGE_TOOLS_ENDPOINT` (one per-install line; DL-220's default-vhost trap stands, and a push-handshake endpoint derivation was rejected as a bearer-exfiltration edge — the authenticated push leg must never redirect bearer-carrying calls).
- **Channel side:** `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOOLS` is tri-state — `=1` force-on, `=0`/empty off, unset ⇒ advertise iff the endpoint is set AND a token resolves (`BRIDGE_TOOLS_TOKEN` → `_FILE` — a configured-but-unreadable explicit source SHORT-CIRCUITS, never falls through — → the new `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOKEN` fallback). Advertise keys on observable intent, never on transport (bridge-side state is not channel-observable — the same reason-class as the endpoint ruling).
- **UDS seats are inert by construction:** `resolveChannel` forbids a channel token on UDS (that constraint is load-bearing and stays), so the reuse model yields no bearer there; the retained explicit path (`enabled: true` + alias, provision-tools mint) is the UDS opt-in. `bridge:provision-tools` is demoted to that explicit-override path and skips channel-reuse agents (minting into a reused channel token file would clobber push auth).
- **Check severity re-ruling:** a suppressed default block, an unreadable bearer, and a token COLLISION all FAIL `bridge:check` (collision was WARN under opt-in; under default-ON a dead-for-both-agents surface is a broken enablement). Kanban-visibility/membership/swimlane/stage checks stay WARN (the DL-220 split — transient/empty states must not FAIL). **[NARROWED by DL-254 and DL-262:** "an unreadable bearer" was one label over states that are not alike. A bearer this process cannot SEE (DL-254) or cannot READ (DL-262) reports `unvalidated`, because the resolver serving the runtime is built as a different OS user; only the perms and absent halves remain the measured `fail` this bullet describes.**]**
**DL-217 fail-closed property disposition (all ten enumerated at design round 6):** preserved — absent-block byte-identical no-op, swimlane forced-from-config/never-caller-supplied, bearer 0600 fail-closed read, collision fail-closed-for-all-sharers at the resolver, per-agent runtime failure isolation, token→identity derived bridge-side; inverted with named replacements — "present block MUST carry enabled" (→ THE RULE), "auth.token_path required when enabled" (→ requireBearer), collision check WARN (→ FAIL), provision-minted default (→ explicit-override path); **Superseded DL-217 sentences (this entry is the forward pointer for all three):** (1) the parse-posture line "present-but-malformed ⇒ throws at load" — no longer holds for the DEFAULT class (explicit stays loud-at-load); (2) the Authz-shape argument that the tools bearer "can't ride the existing key" / "no new credential class does not survive the config layer" — the channel token IS now the default bearer (the `resolveChannel` constraint that motivated the separate key still stands and is what makes UDS inert; the separate key survives as the alias/override); (3) the Behavior line "absent `board_tools` AND absent `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOOLS` ⇒ byte-identical" — the channel gate is now tri-state and an absent-gate install with a satisfiable block comes ON (the absent-BLOCK half still holds byte-identically). DL-220's "provision-minted bearer" default-path premise is likewise superseded (the command remains for explicit installs).
**Alternatives rejected (with the round that killed each):** deriving the swimlane from the writeback create-lane (R1 — category error); null-swimlane whole-board reads (R1 — unguardable silent widening when a board gains a second agent); push-handshake endpoint derivation (pre-R1 — bearer-exfil edge); endpoint defaulting (R1 — DL-220 default-vhost trap); advertise-on-transport (R2 — bridge state not channel-observable); load-throw for unsatisfiable default blocks (R4 — install-wide 5xx blast radius); hard removal of the alias key (R1 — live 401 mid-upgrade); enumerated suppression doors (R6 — replaced by the structural rule so future fields inherit correct behavior).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, proven at build):** the 12-row truth table as named cases; the 7-input/6-path parametrized fleet-outage regression (each default-class malformation loads without throwing, carries its case-specific suppressedReason, FAILs check); the suppressedReason scan + collision + bearer-unreadable check FAILs (each seen red); default-flip authentication via channel token; mixed-source collision fail-closed; preserved-by-name: `test_absent_board_tools_is_a_no_op`, `test_colliding_token_fails_closed_for_both_agents`. The `.mjs` tri-state has no in-repo harness — live-fire verification (canon #9) rides the first enablement (aimla's seat, roundtable #102). Card #4907, roundtable #102.

## DL-223 — Board-tools SSH-forced-command transport: a second front door into the same dispatch machinery, selected by an explicit `board_tools.transport: http|ssh` — the no-root, no-forwarding, FIPS-viable cross-host alternative to the HTTP loopback endpoint

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** The existing cross-host board-tools path (`docs/multi-host.md § forward leg`) needs a `-L` FORWARD tunnel on host B to carry the B→A `tools/call` over HTTP loopback. sola's `device` account is locked to `AllowTcpForwarding remote` (a live `Match User device` drop-in) — `-L` forward tunnels are BLOCKED there, so the HTTP-loopback path literally cannot run on that seat. SSH-forced-command needs NO forwarding (the call rides the ssh channel's own stdin/stdout), so it is the ONLY cross-host board-tools transport that works on an as-hardened `AllowTcpForwarding remote` seat; same-box installs also gain a no-root, no-vhost path. Converged 3-way on roundtable #133 (kanban-solo owns it; aimla = same-box live-fire witness; sola = cross-host FIPS live-fire witness), then locked through a 4-round fresh-adversarial design-review loop (DR1: 7 folded · DR2: 9 folded · DR3: 1 must-fix + 3 folded · DR4: clean; core held every round). Card #4952.
**Decision — TRANSPORT ONLY.** Tool semantics, the forced-swimlane scope model, default-ON, and the writeback single-writer invariant are all UNTOUCHED. This adds a second front door + a config discriminator + verification/provisioning around the exact same dispatch machinery. The four converged findings:
- **A — one shared dispatcher.** The post-agent-resolution body of the HTTP controller (tool/args validation → writeback build → invoke → exception→status map + the audit log line) is extracted into `BoardToolDispatcher`, returning a transport-neutral `DispatchOutcome{ok,status,result,error}`. Both doors serialize the identical body from ONE serializer (`DispatchOutcome::body()`, DR4 body-shape parity); the HTTP door maps `status` to a JsonResponse byte-identically (existing controller tests stay green unchanged), the ssh door maps it to an exit code (0 ok / 1 caller-fixable 4xx / 2 service-fault 5xx). The audit log line gains a `transport` field.
- **B — an explicit `board_tools.transport: http|ssh` (default http), NOT an inferred one.** `http` ⇒ resolve-by-bearer (the channel token, post-DL-222); `ssh` ⇒ resolve-by-the-pinned-forced-command-`--agent`, NO bearer. `ssh` lifts ONLY the bearer requirement at load; `board_id`/`swimlane_id`/`create_stage_id` stay fail-loud (a typo'd ssh block must fail, not fail-open). An ssh block that ALSO carries any `board_tools.auth` key is contradictory and fails closed (DR2-1: the trigger is `array_key_exists('auth',$block)` — it catches bare `auth:`, `auth: {}`, `auth: {token_path:null}`, and a real token_path alike; the throw is a board_tools-scoped ConfigException inside `build()`, so it inherits the DL-222 4-branch throw/suppress classification — explicit throws at load, default suppresses, no default block can 5xx the fleet). `BoardToolAgentResolver` also excludes ssh agents from the HTTP index explicitly (`transport !== 'http'`).
- **C — `bridge:tools-call` writes JSON-ONLY to stdout.** The ssh channel captures the command's fd 1 as the tool result, so the command writes NOTHING to stdout but the one JSON envelope (raw `fwrite(STDOUT)`, never `$this->info/line/warn/error`); every diagnostic goes to stderr/Log, and `display_errors` is pinned to stderr early. Identity is the trusted `--agent` (SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND is never read); STDIN is a bounded (64 KiB) deadline-guarded read.
- **D — a two-sided `bridge:check` probe that asserts the restriction OUTCOME, not a `restrict` keyword.** Per enabled ssh agent, an offline pinned-`authorized_keys`-line probe: exactly-one line forces `bridge:tools-call --agent=X` and DENIES pty + agent/X11/port-forwarding, via a last-writer-wins capability model (DR3 must-fix — `restrict,pty` FAILs because sshd grants the pty; `permitopen`/`permitlisten`/`tunnel` are treated as port-forwarding permits; the option list is parsed with a quoted-field tokenizer (F5) and matched on parsed KEYS case-insensitively, never a substring scan (DR2-4 — a keyword inside a value never counts as a deny). Plus a root-gated `sshd -T` password-auth OUTCOME leg and a new `--probe-tools-ssh=<user@host>` live round-trip.
**FIPS folds (two, from sola's real substrate):** (FIPS-1) the board-tools pinned key MUST be FIPS-approved (ECDSA P-256), NOT ed25519 (a FIPS sshd rejects ed25519 auth keys) — every place that generates/documents the key parameterizes it (`docs/multi-host.md` recipe + `bridge:provision-tools` scaffold-by-print), never a hardcoded `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`; `bridge:check` asserts the key algo on a FIPS seat. (FIPS-2) the pinned-line drift probe asserts the restriction OUTCOME, not a literal `restrict` token — a FIPS sshd's `restrict` disables forwarding without honoring `permitlisten`, so a valid FIPS line uses the enumerated `no-pty,no-agent-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding,no-port-forwarding` form and carries no `restrict`; the probe accepts BOTH.
**B-12 pre-emption (why an explicit key here, when the channel-transport enum was declined):** architecture review B-12 (2026-05-31) declined a named-profile transport enum for the CHANNEL-PUSH axis as "elegance not correctness… revisit only if the config product genuinely grows." This is a DIFFERENT axis (how the bridge AUTHENTICATES a board-tools call), and inference is genuinely fail-open here: post-DL-222 the channel token is ALWAYS a candidate bearer, so "no bearer ⟹ ssh" is unreachable and would mask a genuinely-misconfigured http agent. An explicit 2-value `board_tools.transport` is the honest discriminator this new mutual-exclusion needs, scoped narrowly to board_tools (not a channel-push rewrite) — exactly the "config product genuinely grows" trigger B-12's decline named.
**⚠ SEPARATE FLAGGED ITEM (hard-gate class) — the shipped HTTP-relay corrupt-body hardening.** The `.mjs` ssh leg and the existing HTTP fetch leg now share ONE parse-or-`isError` relay helper (DR2-2, canon #5 — fixed at the second caller). The helper's success signal is LEG-SUPPLIED (`res.ok` / clean ssh exit), never inferred from the body, so a 200 (or exit 0) with a php-warning-prepended body is now `isError:true`. **This intentionally CHANGES the shipped default-ON HTTP path's corrupt-body behavior from `isError:false` → `isError:true` — a change to how errors are reported to devices (hard-gate class).** It is covered by the standing autonomous-dev-branch authorization ([[feedback-git-workflow]]: fully autonomous dev PRs incl. hard-gate changes, self-merge on green; per-instance approval is release/main only), and is surfaced here + in the PR body as its own item, not buried. The parse-failure message keeps a truncated raw-body snippet with Authorization/Bearer substrings stripped (DR3 nit + DR4).
**Provisioning:** `bridge:provision-tools` mints no bridge-side secret for an ssh agent (the private key is host B's; authorized_keys is never edited) — it scaffolds by print (the pinned forced-command line, the FIPS-approved keygen recipe, the `Match User` sshd drop-in, and the `sudo bridge:check` certification gate — DR2-3a: ssh enablement is NOT certified until a root `bridge:check` verifies the sshd posture), exit 0.
**Exit-code semantics (DR2-3/DR2-6):** on a normal UNPRIVILEGED `bridge:check`, the root-gated sshd-posture legs emit an explicit UNVERIFIED warn + the `sudo bridge:check` cert step (never a false OK, never a hard CI red); a present-but-bad pinned line (grants pty/forwarding, or an absent line at a root-resolved authoritative path) FAILs even unprivileged; an http/disabled/not-ssh agent invoked over the ssh door → exit 2 (a bridge-side config fault the caller cannot fix, consistent with unknown-agent=2).
**Scope explicitly NOT in v1:** ControlPersist/handshake reuse (per-call Laravel boot accepted, as the HTTP loopback path already pays); dual-wire per agent (single-valued); auto-editing authorized_keys / auto-generating host-B keys; the framework's `setup-bridge`/`onboard-agent` FIPS-algo default (coord plugin, cross-repo — a follow-up FR on the roundtable, not built here).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, proven at build):** the capability model matrix (`restrict` / enumerated-`no-*` pass; `restrict,pty` / `restrict,permitopen` / `no-pty,pty` fail; keyword-in-value never a deny; quoted-comma no-split); FIPS ed25519 FAIL vs ecdsa pass; sshd password-auth enabled FAIL / disabled OK / non-root UNVERIFIED warn; the DR2-1 four-auth-shape matrix (ssh throws-explicit / suppresses-default, http unaffected); the resolver ssh-exclusion (a spurious ssh config with a real token file is not indexed); `bridge:tools-call` exit-code class mapping + stdout purity (an internal diagnostic never pollutes fd 1); the shared `DispatchOutcome` status/exit mapping; two CheckCommand integration reds (present-but-bad line → exit 1; password-auth-enabled → exit 1). **Owed live-fire debt (canon #9):** the `.mjs` ssh leg and the `--probe-tools-ssh` round-trip have no in-repo harness — live-fire rides the witnesses (aimla same-box + sola cross-host+FIPS) post-merge; the `sshd -T` root requirement and a FIPS sshd's `restrict` behavior are reasoned from the OpenSSH 9.x man page, confirmed on a real FIPS seat when sola's seat fires. Two further reasoned-not-run items ride the same witnesses: (i) the offline pinned-line probe (`AuthorizedKeysLine::forcesToolsCallFor`) matches only the `bridge:tools-call` verb + a bounded `--agent=`, NOT the full artisan path — a line pinned at a stale/wrong artisan path passes the offline probe silently (low security impact: the live `--probe-tools-ssh` round-trip catches a truly broken path); stricter forced-command path matching is deferred as reasoned-not-run. (ii) Whether `stream_set_timeout`'s `timed_out` meta actually fires on a real ssh-channel stdin (the plain pipe sshd hands a forced command, vs. the socket it is reliable on) is unverified — the in-process stdin deadline is best-effort and sshd-level idle/concurrency limits are the authoritative backstop. Card #4952, roundtable #133.

## DL-224 — SSH-transport probe certifies the FORCED-COMMAND account, not the invoking one (new `board_tools.ssh_account`), and asserts the sshd idle/concurrency backstop it previously only recommended

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** DL-223's `SshTransportProbe` (Finding D) resolved the **invoking** OS account at two sites where it means the **forced-command** account. `SystemSshProbeEnvironment::runUser()`/`runUserHome()` = `posix_getpwuid(posix_geteuid())` — the account running `bridge:check`. But the root-gated posture leg is documented as `sudo bridge:check`, so under sudo `euid=0` ⇒ it certified **root's** Match-resolved `sshd -T -C user=root` posture and read **`/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`** (default path + `%h`/`%u` expansion), false-negativing the very seat it targets whenever the forced command runs as a non-root account (the common case — a dedicated bridge/device user). Separately, DL-223's `docs/multi-host.md` carried an operator note to add `ClientAliveInterval`/`ClientAliveCountMax`/`MaxSessions` to the `Match User` block — but `bridge:check` never verified them, and with the forced command as the sole entry point those sshd limits are the ONLY real bound on a key-holder that deliberately holds stdin open (the in-process stdin deadline is best-effort + unverified on the pipe, per DL-223 owed-debt (ii)). An unverified operator note is worthless. Converged on roundtable #133 (kanban-solo). Card #4977.
**Decision — a coupled account-resolution + backstop-verify fix, TRANSPORT-PROBE ONLY.** No change to tool semantics, dispatch, the forced-swimlane scope model, or the HTTP path. Three parts:
- **New optional `board_tools.ssh_account` (string).** Parsed into `BoardToolsConfig` as `readonly ?string $sshAccount` via a new `optionalString` helper mirroring `optionalInt` (present ⇒ must be a non-empty string, else a board_tools-scoped `ConfigException` inheriting the DL-222 4-branch throw/suppress classification; absent ⇒ null). Only meaningful for `transport: 'ssh'` — parse-and-store, no cross-transport contradiction throw (an `ssh_account` on an http block is inert, not contradictory like `auth`-on-ssh; a throw there would be over-engineering per canon #6). **Not required** — absent ⇒ the invoking run-user (byte-identical to pre-4977).
- **Resolve the forced-command account + home.** `SshTransportProbe` gains `?string $sshAccount` (constructor) → `forcedCommandAccount() = sshAccount ?? env->runUser()` and `forcedCommandHome() = sshAccount ? env->homeForUser(sshAccount) : env->runUserHome()`. New `SshProbeEnvironment::homeForUser(string): string` (`posix_getpwnam`; '' when unresolvable, fail-safe → a non-authoritative path ⇒ warn, never a false OK). Injection seam: **a per-agent constructor arg**, not a shared singleton — `ssh_account` is per-agent config, so `CheckCommand::checkSshTransport` constructs one probe per agent (pinned-line + keys are per-agent) and dedupes the posture leg **by resolved account** (N agents sharing one account — incl. the all-unset default — emit posture once, byte-identical). The keys-path `sshd -T` query passes `$this->sshAccount` (null when unset ⇒ no `-C`, byte-identical; the account when set ⇒ Match-resolved for that account); the posture query passes `forcedCommandAccount()` (already did, now via the resolver).
- **sshd idle/concurrency backstop asserted on the posture leg.** Reading the SAME Match-resolved `sshd -T -C user=<forced-command-account>` output, assert `ClientAliveInterval`>0 (0 = no server-side idle timeout — a hung holder never drops), `ClientAliveCountMax` present (the idle window `interval × countmax` is bounded), and `MaxSessions` present (concurrency capped). A missing/unbounded directive **fails** with the exact directive named + a `Match User <account>` remedy (actionable, matching the file's `ok`/`warn`/`fail` style); a bounded config reports the computed idle bound. The backstop is a new finding for every ssh seat (not gated on `ssh_account`); the `ssh_account`-unset byte-identical invariant is scoped to WHICH account is resolved, per canon #6.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, proven at build):** split-topology (invoking=root, `ssh_account=device` ⇒ posture query + authorized_keys + backstop all resolve `device`, never `root`/`/root/...` — RED when the resolver is reverted to `runUser()`); fallback (unset ⇒ keys query passes null/no-`-C`, keys path uses the invoking home, posture queries the invoking account — stays GREEN under the revert, guarding canon #6); backstop unset/interval-0 ⇒ fail with the named directive + `Match User` remedy, bounded ⇒ ok with the computed idle bound (all three RED when the backstop finding is removed). Existing posture fixtures gained a bounded backstop block so they isolate the password-auth assertion. 1334/1334 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. **Owed live-fire debt (canon #9, inherited from DL-223):** the account-resolution + backstop assertions are unit-verified through the `SshProbeEnvironment` fake; the real `posix_getpwnam` home resolution and `sshd -T -C user=<non-root>` Match-resolution ride the same post-merge witnesses (aimla same-box + sola cross-host+FIPS). Card #4977, roundtable #133.

**Follow-on (2026-07-23, card #4977) — two security-correctness gaps in the above closed (canon #7 guard-consistency + honest-fail).** Two adversarial reviewers found, and confirmed at source, that the DL-224 change certified two unsafe states green:
- **Backstop non-positive gap.** The backstop guarded `ClientAliveCountMax`/`MaxSessions` on `=== null` **only**, while the interval sibling correctly rejected `|| <= 0`. But `sshd -T` ALWAYS emits both directives (defaults 3/10), so the `null` branch is effectively dead and the real failure state — a non-positive value — was unguarded. With `ClientAliveCountMax 0` (which per `man sshd_config` DISABLES sshd's client-alive disconnection — the exact unbounded-idle case the backstop exists to catch) the null-check passed, `idleBound = interval × 0 = 0`, and the leg returned **ok** with "…= 0s idle bound". **Fix:** both guards now match the interval sibling — `=== null || <= 0` — with messages distinguishing unset vs non-positive; the countMax message conveys that `0` *disables* the idle disconnect, the maxSessions message that a non-positive value fail-shuts the forced command entirely (still not `ok`).
- **Unresolvable configured account.** `forcedCommandHome()` returned `homeForUser($sshAccount)`, which is `''` for a nonexistent account; that `''` flowed unchecked into `authorizedKeysPath()` → the default path became `/.ssh/authorized_keys` and the `%h` expansion substituted `''`, so a **configured** `ssh_account` that does not resolve to an OS account was certified/misattributed against a phantom path instead of failing honestly. **Fix (root-cause):** a single private `configuredAccountUnresolved(): ?string` helper, checked at the entry of the account-dependent legs (`probeSshdPosture`, `probePinnedLine`), returns a `fail` naming the problem (*"board_tools.ssh_account '<acct>' does not resolve to an OS account on this host — the SSH transport cannot be certified"*) rather than build a path from an empty home. **Canon #6 — gated strictly on `sshAccount !== null`:** the unset fallback path (`runUserHome()`, which can also return `''` pre-4977) is byte-identical — its pre-existing non-authoritative `warn` on an empty home is a deliberately-unchanged edge, NOT the new hard-fail. Only a *configured* account that fails to resolve is the new fail.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, proven at build):** `clientalivecountmax 0` (interval bounded) ⇒ `fail` not `ok` (RED — got `ok` — when the countMax guard reverts to `=== null`); `maxsessions 0` ⇒ `fail` (RED when reverted); configured `ssh_account` with `homeForUser ⇒ ''` ⇒ `fail` (account-unresolved) with **no** `/.ssh/authorized_keys` false-`ok` (RED when the helper is neutered); and the fallback invariant — `ssh_account` UNSET with `runUserHome ⇒ ''` ⇒ unchanged non-authoritative `warn`, stays GREEN under the fix (pins canon #6). Full suite green, pint clean, phpstan L7 0 (baseline unchanged). Card #4977.

## DL-225 — SSH is the DEFAULT board-tools transport (unset `board_tools.transport` reads as `ssh`, was `http`), with a `bridge:check` pre-upgrade advisory keyed on a new `transportExplicit` flag

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** DL-223 introduced `board_tools.transport: http|ssh` with `http` as the default so the SSH front door was purely opt-in and every pre-existing block stayed byte-identical. The fleet direction (roundtable #133/#138, kanban-solo proposal to sola-pm/aimla-pm) is **ssh-first**: the SSH forced-command door is no-root, firewall-uniform, carries no bearer secret, and is the preferred cross-host shape. Leaving `http` as the default means every new agent silently gets the loopback-HTTP posture unless it remembers to opt in. Flipping the default is a behavior change that must be **loud, fail-closed, and migration-guided** — not a silent permissive shift. Roundtable #138.
**Decision — flip the default at both sites + add a keyed advisory; touch nothing caller-facing.** No change to tool semantics, dispatch, the forced-swimlane scope, the runtime resolution path, or error handling:
- **`BoardToolsConfig` defaults `transport` to `ssh`** at both the parse site (`parseTransport` absent-key return) and the constructor default. A block that relied on the implicit `http` default now parses as `ssh` (which lifts the bearer requirement — identity is the forced-command `--agent`), so its bearer stops resolving over the HTTP door.
- **New readonly `transportExplicit` bool** — `true` iff a `transport` key was PRESENT in the parsed block (`array_key_exists('transport', $block)` in `build()`), `false` when it fell through to the default. This is what the advisory keys on: an operator who wrote `transport: ssh` chose it; one who wrote nothing was moved by the default.
- **`bridge:check` pre-upgrade advisory (warn, NEVER a hard fail).** In the ssh leg (`checkSshTransport`), an ssh-transport agent with `transportExplicit === false` whose ssh setup is **incomplete** (the pinned-line + sshd-posture probes already run in that leg report any non-ok finding) is flagged: *"agent X is on ssh by the v0.68.0 default (no explicit transport:) with no completed ssh setup — pin `transport: http` to keep the loopback path, or complete ssh setup."* Advisory only — the runtime break is already loud (below), so this is the pre-deploy backstop, not a fix.
- **The caller-facing 401 in `AgentToolsController` is deliberately untouched.** It does not distinguish "unknown token" from "collided/unreadable/re-classed-to-ssh" — that is a **security property**: a message naming "re-classed to ssh" would leak that the presented bearer is a VALID token. Post-flip, an implicit-http block reads as ssh → `BoardToolAgentResolver`'s existing `transport !== 'http'` exclusion drops it from the HTTP index → `resolve($bearer) === null` → 401. So the runtime break is ALREADY fail-closed and loud; no loud-fail guard was added.
- **Migration:** any block relying on the implicit `http` default must set `transport: http` explicitly BEFORE upgrading (CHANGELOG UPGRADING note). Explicit `http`/`ssh` blocks are unaffected.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) keep `http` default, ship ssh docs only — rejected, leaves the preferred posture perpetually opt-in. (b) Emit the advisory as a hard FAIL — rejected, a default flip must not red an install's `bridge:check` for a config that was valid yesterday; the runtime is fail-closed and the advisory names the one-line fix. (c) Change the 401 to name the re-class — rejected, leaks token validity (see above).
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `BoardToolsConfigTest` — unset `transport` ⇒ `ssh` + `transportExplicit === false` + enabled (reds if the default reverts to `http`); explicit `http`/`ssh` ⇒ that value + `transportExplicit === true`; the HTTP-intended rows across the truth table pinned with explicit `transport: http`. `BridgeCommandsTest` — the advisory FIRES on an implicit-default ssh agent with incomplete setup (positive), and does NOT fire on an explicit `transport: ssh` agent with equally-incomplete setup (negative control — proves failability). Card #4952, roundtable #138.

## DL-226 — `bridge:provision-tools` (ssh path) GENERATES a guided, idempotent root-run setup script whose output PASSES the `bridge:check` sshd backstop (was print-only scaffolding that omitted the DL-224 directives)

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Context:** DL-223's `printSshScaffold` was **print-only** and OMITTED the three DL-224 backstop directives (`ClientAliveInterval`/`ClientAliveCountMax`/`MaxSessions`, all `>0`) that `bridge:check` now HARD-ASSERTS via `probeSshdPosture`. So an operator following the scaffold verbatim, then running `sudo bridge:check`, **FAILED the backstop leg** — the scaffold and the check disagreed. The motivating defect: the guidance a command emits must pass that command's own verification. Roundtable #138.
**Decision — generate the setup script; keep it operator-run.** "Guided" = generate + verify, NOT silent full automation — root surfaces stay operator-run (the script is printed for review and run as `sudo bash <script>`; the private key never touches the bridge). The generated script wires **idempotently** (append-or-verify; it never clobbers existing config):
- **(a)** the forced-command `authorized_keys` line — the exact FIPS-enumerated form (`command="php <artisan> bridge:tools-call --agent=X",no-pty,no-agent-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding,no-port-forwarding <pubkey>`, NOT `restrict`); artisan path + agent name substituted at generation, host B's public key a filled-in `HOST_B_PUBKEY` placeholder (the script refuses to run until it is set); appended only when `grep -qF` finds no existing forced-command line for the agent.
- **(b)** an sshd `Match User <ssh_account>` drop-in at `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/<account>-board-tools.conf` with `PasswordAuthentication no` AND the three backstop directives set to sane positives (`ClientAliveInterval 300`, `ClientAliveCountMax 2`, `MaxSessions 10`) — the exact directive set + `>0` thresholds `probeSshdPosture` asserts, so the output PASSES `bridge:check`; written only when the drop-in is absent (an existing one is left with a verify note).
- **(c)** validate-then-reload — `sshd -t` BEFORE `systemctl reload` (a bad drop-in never takes sshd down).
- **(d)** the FIPS ECDSA P-256 keygen documented to run FIRST on host B (`ssh-keygen -t ecdsa -b 256`, never ed25519 — a FIPS sshd rejects it).
- **Flow:** provision-tools generates + prints the script → operator runs `sudo bash <script>` → `bridge:check --probe-tools-ssh=<user@host>` certifies (a real `board_my_cards` round-trip). The ssh account comes from `board_tools.ssh_account` (DL-224; unset ⇒ the invoking run-user).
**Alternatives considered:** (a) leave print-only, just add the three directives to the printed note — rejected, still asks the operator to hand-edit sshd config correctly and re-verify; the whole defect is the gap between guidance and check. (b) Fully automate (run the root steps from the command) — rejected, root surfaces stay operator-run; the command has no business editing `/etc/ssh` or `authorized_keys` unattended. Generate + operator-run + `--probe-tools-ssh` verify is the middle path.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `BridgeCommandsTest` — the generated output carries the exact forced-command line (enumerated no-* flags), the PASTE placeholder, `ssh-keygen -t ecdsa -b 256` (and NOT ed25519), `Match User` + `PasswordAuthentication no` + `ClientAliveInterval 300`/`ClientAliveCountMax 2`/`MaxSessions 10`, `sshd -t` + reload, the append-or-verify idempotency marker, and the `bridge:check --probe-tools-ssh` certify step; no bridge-side token file is minted for the ssh agent. Card #4952, roundtable #138.

## DL-227 — A same-box one-shot wrapper (`bin/provision-board-tools-samebox.py`) collapses the 6-step cross-user SSH board-tools runbook into one root-run command, running EACH agent's OWN checkout's provisioner (never a global bin) behind a fail-closed preflight

**Date:** 2026-07-24
**Context:** When the agent's Claude seat and the bridge share one box, the SSH board-tools enablement (DL-223/226, FR #5010 §2) is a ~6-step cross-user runbook root drives by hand: resolve the agent's `.mcp.json` → `--project-dir`/`--channel-name`; make the tool readable by the agent user; `sudo -H -u <agent>` `--role b` (capture the printed pubkey path); root `--role a --pubkey-from`; restart the agent's Claude session; `bridge:check` then `chown storage`. It is mechanical, error-prone, and easy to get wrong in a version-unsafe way — aimla's live runbook did `install -m0755 provision-board-tools.py /usr/local/bin/…`, staging the tool at a **shared global path**. That is a version-collision hazard: multiple agents on one host can run **different** bridge versions, and a shared global path lets a redeploy of one clobber the others. Card 5090 (follow-on to FR #141/#5010).
**Decision — a thin python orchestrator that runs each leg's OWN checkout, fail-closed.** `bin/provision-board-tools-samebox.py --agent <name> --ssh-account <host-A user>` (plus `--agent-home`/`--agent-bin`/`--hostA-checkout`/`--project-dir`/`--channel-name` overrides and `--dry-run`). Two load-bearing properties, both card-5090 hard requirements:
- **(a) NO global binary staging (version isolation).** Each leg runs *its own checkout's* `provision-board-tools.py`: the agent user runs the agent's version (`sudo -H -u <agent> python3 <agent-checkout>/bin/…`), root runs the host-A checkout's version. The wrapper NEVER copies the tool into a shared/global path. The agent's own copy is discovered under its home (or `--agent-bin`); if it is absent, ambiguous, or **not readable by the agent user** (probed as that user via `sudo -u <agent> test -r`), the wrapper FAILS with an actionable "give the agent its own checkout" message — no shared/global fallback exists in any code path.
- **(b) Robust, fail-closed preflight before any mutation.** Validates: running as root; both OS users exist (`getent passwd`); the agent's `.mcp.json` resolves unambiguously (→ project-dir + the single `mcpServers` key as channel-name; 0/many ⇒ fail, `--project-dir`/`--channel-name` to disambiguate); both checkouts' `provision-board-tools.py` + host-A `artisan` present; `php` on PATH; and (post role-b) the printed pubkey path exists + is readable. Every failure names its fix; no silent skips.
- **Flow:** preflight → role-b as the agent (capture + validate the pubkey path; NO `--self-cert`, the key is not pinned yet) → role-a as root (`--pubkey-from` the captured path) → print the one manual step (restart the agent's Claude session) → `php <artisan> bridge:check` → `chown -R <ssh-account>:<ssh-account> <host-A storage>` (a root-run artisan can leave root-owned logs). Idempotent: the underlying `--role a`/`--role b` already are, and the wrapper adds no non-idempotent state.
**Language — python, not bash.** Matches the repo's `bin/` provisioning convention (the sole tool + its CI-wired `unittest` harness are python), cleanly reuses `provision-board-tools.py`'s validation primitives (`_AGENT_RE`/`_SSH_ACCOUNT_RE`) by importing it rather than re-deriving the contract (canon #5), and lets the selftest follow the repo's established "factor pure decisions, unit-test them red-when-reverted" architecture. A bash wrapper would need a shell test harness the repo does not have and could not reuse the tool's helpers.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) keep the hand-run runbook — rejected, it is exactly the error surface (the global-staging footgun) this closes. (b) Fully automate incl. the root sshd work with no operator visibility — rejected; the wrapper is a thin orchestrator of the existing operator-run legs, it changes nothing about what those legs write. (c) A shared `/usr/local/bin` copy of the tool (aimla's runbook) — rejected as the version-collision hazard that motivated the card.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `bin/test_provision_board_tools_samebox.py` (25 cases, CI-wired via `provision-tools-python.yml`) — preflight fail-closed modes (not-root, missing agent user, missing ssh-account user, missing/ambiguous `.mcp.json`, agent provisioner absent → the "own checkout" message with NO `/usr/local/bin`/`install -m` global fallback, agent provisioner unreadable-by-agent, missing host-A provisioner/artisan/php, bad agent/account names); happy-path exact role-b/role-a argv assembly; pubkey-path parse. Reverting the readable-by-agent guard reds `test_agent_provisioner_unreadable_by_agent_fails`; reverting the `.mcp.json` ambiguity guard reds `test_ambiguous_mcp_json_fails` (both verified). Card 5090.
