That is incomplete for a mechanical reason, not a matter of taste: the event-consumer reconciliation — which github event types **arrived** on a scope versus what any enabled classifier **declares it consumes** — was computed as local variables inside `EventFollowsConsumerCheck` and thrown away. The only thing that survived the run was the WARN sentence. **A generic JSON renderer over the existing `CheckReport` therefore emits that prose as a JSON string, and a consumer still parses prose** — and it breaks toward a FALSE CLEAN, because a parser that matches nothing reports nothing. DL-236 had already reworded findings in this command once. So stage 9 is the renderer split **and** the reconciliation extracted as data; the plan's row is corrected in the open, the third stage row in this program falsified by the stage that built it (6 and 8 were the others).

**Decision (1) — ONE front door: `--format=json` on `bridge:check`, not a standalone `bridge:consumed-events`.** The card left this fork open and argued the two are not equivalent. They are not, and the asymmetry decides it: **a standalone query command cannot carry the other half.** The resolved opt-in-probe decision (DL-242/DL-248) owes `NotRequested` **per check**, which is an *inventory* fact — a query command has no inventory, so shipping one would close card#5229 and leave the plan row open, at the cost of a second write contract and a second guard for one known consumer. The card's binding constraint — **do not ship a second derivation** — is honoured either way, and it is precisely what makes a second front door cheap to add later: `EventConsumerReconciler` is the one derivation and a query command would be a third renderer over it, not a fork of it. Precedent: the DL-223 `BoardToolDispatcher` split, one core behind the HTTP and ssh doors.

**Decision (2) — the reconciliation moves out WHOLE, as a value, and `EventFollowsConsumerCheck` becomes a renderer only.** `EventConsumerReconciler` / `EventConsumerReconciliation` / `EventConsumerScope`; the derivation runs in `handle()` (plan constraint (c), the treatment stage 5c gave the `AgentRegistry` build) and is published on `CheckContext`. **A check deriving its own would re-run the per-scope query behind the other renderer's back and could disagree with it** — which is the failure card#5229 named. The value carries the derived projections (`unconsumed()`, `unlistedActions()`) rather than leaving them to each consumer, because those two *are* what the WARN and INFO lines say and the whole point is that nobody re-implements the projection rule. **The type/action tier is load-bearing, not decoration:** a consumer that flattens bare (`issues` — type owned, every action covered) and qualified (`issues.opened`) declarations opens with hundreds of findings on a healthy install; one fleet seat measured `labeled (468×), edited (14×)` on a type whose bare declaration already covered them. **The declaration half is computed even when nothing arrived**, deliberately: `observed` can only ever show events that were both SUBSCRIBED and DELIVERED, so it structurally cannot answer *"what does this scope's classifier consume"* — the half a config-auditing consumer reads. The text renderer stays silent for a scope with no arrivals; the data does not inherit that bound.

**Decision (3) — the document is a WRITE CONTRACT: versioned, guarded by an exact-key-set test, and owned by a doc.** This is the gate's real subject, and the plan row's own gate rationale said so before the build confirmed it — the additive-flag framing would have justified skipping the gate. Once a machine consumer parses this it cannot be un-shipped. So: `CheckJsonRenderer::SCHEMA_VERSION` (currently `1`); `CheckJsonContractTest` asserts the exact key set at **every level** with `assertSame` against literals, because a *contains* assertion greens on a renamed key and a renamed key is exactly the change that breaks a consumer silently; and `docs/check-json-contract.md` is the shape's **owning doc**, so there is no second copy to drift. **An ADDED key is deliberately NOT a version bump** — consumers are told to ignore unknown keys, and versioning additive growth makes the number churn until it means nothing. **`message` strings are excluded from the contract by name**: they are operator prose, they have been reworded before and will be again, and a consumer keying on them has re-created the coupling this surface exists to break. The test deliberately does not pin them.

**Decision (4) — the four fail-soft envelopes in `handle()` now emit captured `Finding`s, surfacing as `findings_outside_registry`.** A malformed agent YAML, an unloadable `writeback.json`, and two client-construction failures belong to no registered check, and **two of the four set the exit code**. A registry-shaped document would be tidier and would report every check clean with `ok: false` and nothing naming the cause — **a machine-readable false clean, this program's own defect re-minted at the new surface**. `emitUnattributed()` deliberately does not touch `$ok`; the two `fail` sites set it themselves exactly as they did when they called `error()` directly, and the property that matters is asserted instead — the contract test requires `ok === false` on any document carrying a `fail` anywhere, so a future envelope that forgets its `$ok = false` reds rather than shipping a document that contradicts itself.

**Decision (5) — the reconciler's failure is a FIELD on the value, not an exception channel.** The reconciler is fail-soft, because a DB hiccup must never break `bridge:check`. **A fail-soft producer that returns only its successes hands every consumer an empty list that reads as "nothing to report."** An empty `scopes` with a null `error` is a clean install; an empty `scopes` with a non-null `error` is a measurement that did not happen, and a consumer that cannot tell them apart is the false-clean shape again. Scopes completed before the fault are retained — the first throw ends the walk exactly as the inline loop did, and the findings for the scopes that got through are still owed to the operator.

**Decision (6) — only the RENDER arm is format-gated, which makes "the exit contract is untouched" true by construction rather than by agreement.** `emitFinding()`'s tally and its `fail`-only return run either way; a `--format=json` run walks the identical decision path and differs solely in which bytes reach stdout. Skipping the call in json mode would have made the verdict depend on the renderer — the coupling card#5229 warned this stage could introduce. **The document's `ok` and the exit code are literally one variable**, and `CheckGoldenTest` asserts across all 33 install shapes that the JSON run's exit matches the committed **text** capture's and that `ok` agrees with it. **An unknown `--format` fails closed** (exit 1, no report of either kind) rather than falling back to text: a typo'd flag silently emitting unparseable prose on a zero exit is the same false-clean shape one layer up.

**Stated bound, recorded rather than hidden.** A consumer piping this under `set -e` still gets a non-zero exit on an unhealthy install and aborts before reading the document. The document carries `ok` so `$?` is never needed, and the contract doc says so **in the contract** rather than leaving it to be discovered in production. Two further bounds live there for the same reason: the fail-closed `--format` diagnostic goes to **stdout** (it is written before any format is in effect), so *unparseable stdout* is a state a consumer must handle — **stated, not fixed, because moving it changes how this command reports an error, which is gated**; and the `warn` ↔ `unvalidated` assignment is still imprecise, so **absence of `unvalidated` is not evidence a leg was measured** until card#5291 / card#5292 (stage 10) land. **[LANDED — DL-251. `severity: "unvalidated"` is now sound evidence that a leg could not measure; its ABSENCE still is not evidence of the reverse, for the narrower reason recorded there. The pre-disclosure is also what let `schema` stay at 1 — see `check-json-contract.md` §2.]** That imprecision is why `checks[].disposition` is a separate axis from `findings[].severity` at all.

**Evidence.** Text output **byte-identical: 33/33 goldens green, no regeneration** — stage 9 is the first gated row whose operator-visible column is purely additive, and a needed regen would have been a signal, not a chore. **Whole suite 1861/1861, 5316 assertions** — named deliberately, since the two cross-test defects above are exactly why a per-file list is not an evidence set. Within it: `CheckJsonContractTest` 13/13 · `EventConsumerReconcilerTest` 7/7 · `EventFollowsConsumerCheckTest` 19/19 · `CheckGoldenTest` 76/76. phpstan L7 0 · pint clean · `check-doc-refs` clean. **Real surface:** `php artisan bridge:check --format=json` against a live install — exit 0, one parseable document, 37 registered / 31 ran / 15 reported / 16 silent / 2 not-requested / 4 not-run, three reconciled scopes. **10/10 stage mutations witnessed** (one mutation, one named test, a restore and a compare between each), and **M9 came back GREEN on the first attempt: dropping per-agent result retention left the whole suite passing**, i.e. the document's `agent` attribution was asserted nowhere. Closed by `test_a_per_agent_check_is_one_entry_whose_findings_name_their_agent`, re-run RED — the stage's own instance of the rule that a green suite is evidence only where something could have gone red.

**The code half shipped RED, and the correction is the entry's sharpest lesson.** The stage-9 commit claimed *"code + tests complete and green"*; **it was not**, and the claim had no whole-suite run behind it (no CI has ever run on this branch — workflows fire on PRs). Two tests were failing, **both invisible to every per-file run the build used as evidence**, each passing in isolation and redding only where other tests follow it. Measured in a detached worktree at that exact commit with its own `composer install`, not inferred. **(a) `CheckJsonContractTest` leaked a pinned `PATH` into the rest of the process, redding 15 tests across three unrelated suites** (`PrTitleLintTest`, `GitHubTokenResolverTest`, `ReconcileCommandTest` — everything that shells out; symptom `sh: 1: bash: not found`, exit `127`, in files with nothing to do with `bridge:check`). `PinnedHost` saves the ambient environment **in its constructor**, and several tests in that class walk a list of install shapes, so the second `build()` constructs one while the first is still applied, **saves the PINNED `PATH` as ambient**, and restores the process to it. `CheckGoldenTest` had met this and guards it by tearing down between captures; the new class copied the pattern without the guard. **Fixed structurally — `build()` tears down first, so nesting is unrepresentable** rather than a thing each test must remember, which is decision (2) of DL-248 applied to a test harness. **(b) The skipped-advisory severity test had a stale premise:** it reached the fail-soft state by letting the check's own `WebhookEvent` query throw, and stage 9 moved that query into the reconciler, so the check correctly yielded nothing and the test asserted an advisory it had no way to emit. **Behaviour intact** — verified at the source *before* the test was touched — and every assertion is unchanged; the failure is now handed in as a value. **The generalisable rule: a `--filter` or per-file run is not evidence about the suite.** Both defects are cross-test — one is process state leaking forward, the other a premise the rest of the suite never exercised — so no amount of running the stage's own tests could surface either. A stage's evidence must name the whole-suite run that produced its "green".

**Three findings from the paper-trail half — and the first is a CODE defect that only writing the contract down exposed, which is the argument for an owning doc over a docblock.** **(1) `not_run_reason` was emitted for checks that RAN.** Stating in the doc *when* the field is non-null meant checking, and the live document disagreed with the sentence: `channel.server_snapshot` came back `disposition: "reported"`, with a finding, **carrying "every parsed agent aborted before this leg"**. `CheckRunner::noteNotRun()` attaches a reason to a whole **slot** before the run knows whether that slot will execute, so a per-agent check noted for the agents that aborted and then run for one that did not holds both. **A consumer keying on a non-null reason to mean *did not run* would have been precisely wrong on it — a false signal inside the write contract, in the stage whose entire subject is not shipping false signals.** Fixed at the renderer by gating the reason on the disposition, which is what `CheckInventory::notRunReasons()` and `unexplainedNotRun()` already do; **the JSON renderer was the one reader of the raw map that did not filter**, and the audit for siblings found no other field in the document reading an unfiltered map. **The existing assertion that a ran check carries no reason PASSED UNDER THE DEFECT** — its subject had no reason recorded at all, so it was null for the wrong cause, which is the "test pinned to a value rather than tied to the rule" shape. The replacement drives the renderer directly with an inventory whose *every* id carries a reason, so only the gate can make three of the four null; mutation-proven, reddening that test alone. **(2)** `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT` was justified by *"the fixtures under `tests/Fixtures/check-json` are read in a PR diff"* — **there is no such directory and no committed document fixture**; the guard builds its documents by running the command. A true decision resting on a false premise invites a later reversal that sounds correct, so the rationale is restated on the reason that survives inspection: two real documents get `diff`ed, and on one line that diff is the whole document. **(3)** The stage-7a docblock claim that `emitReport()`'s `@phpstan-impure` keeps the `unvalidated` tally's `> 0` guard from being called dead is **FALSE, and was already false before stage 9 touched the method** — re-measured on an unmodified `dev` checkout (a detached worktree with its own `composer install`, never a symlinked `vendor/`, since composer autoloads `app/` from the target and a symlink makes the experiment answer for the wrong checkout): removing the annotation leaves phpstan at **0 errors**, and it still does on this branch with the tally moved a hop deeper. **The annotation was KEPT** — it states a true fact, and deleting it on the strength of an unidentified substitute is how the guard comes back dead on an unrelated edit. Recorded in the plan's § Disproved claims as claim 9, whose lesson is sharper than claims 6 and 7's: **a docblock claim can cite a measurement and still be stale, because the measurement was true once and nothing re-runs it.**

**Also landed here, as its own class item rather than as a side effect (card#5687):** the plan doc's header **enumerated which stages are built** — a moving value its own § Staged execution table owns, 230 lines below — and drifted through six merged PRs, each of which updated the table and left the header behind. Every one of those PRs' review and doc-sync passes missed it, and a grep could not have caught it: `CLAUDE.md`'s index row was kept current the whole time, so the wording search returns a correct copy and a stale one with nothing distinguishing them. **The cure is DELETION, not re-synchronisation** — the header now points at the table, and `CLAUDE.md`'s row does the same, so neither can drift again. *"Stages marked HARD GATE stay gated"* is policy, not a measurement, and stays. Fixed with stage 9 because stage 9 is one of the two events that would otherwise have re-minted it.

## DL-250 — Every tie over this grammar reads one corpus: a shape absent from `CardTokenGrammar::VECTORS` was invisible to all of them at once, and read as independent greens

**Date:** 2026-07-31
**Context — the bug is one character, the finding is not.** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::warnCardTokenNearMiss()` probed `/\bcard(?:[_:.]|\s#)?\d/i`. `\bcard` matches inside `cards`, the optional separator group cannot consume the `s`, and `\d` then fails against it — with no second word boundary to retry from. So **every plural spelling was silent**: `cards #123`, `cards#123`, `cards-123`, `cards123`, `cards_123`, `cards:123`, `cards.123`. None of them correlate either, and the probe is consulted ONLY on the null-parse path (both call sites guarded `$dl === null && $cardToken === null`), so the whole family was the exact failure the probe exists to prevent: the branch publishes, the card never moves, nobody is told. **[card#6025:** there is no `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::warnCardTokenNearMiss()` in the tree today — the probe moved to `NearMissProbe` / `CardTokenGrammar::nearMissCardId()`; the entry records the code as it stood.**]**

**The finding is one layer up.** DL-239 built a lattice of guards over this grammar — the `good=` answer-set tie, the `looks=` superset check, the end-to-end warn-iff-rejected loop, the warning-text naming check, the case-fold leg, the require-step agreement, and `describe()`'s anti-snapshot assertion. Every one of them is sound, and **every one is keyed to the same single hand-authored corpus**, `CardTokenGrammar::VECTORS`: measured on `dev`, **eight legs across two files ask that one list and nothing else**. A shape absent from it is therefore invisible to all eight *simultaneously*, and the result presents as eight independent confirmations rather than as one measurement repeated eight times. That is worse than one guard, because the count reads as corroboration. **The fix is therefore a corpus edit plus closing the one site that does not react to a corpus edit at all** — the regex widening is the smallest part of it.

**Decision (1) — the near-miss probe moves onto `CardTokenGrammar`, and its separators become DATA.** `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` is the list; `looksLikeCardToken()` assembles the pattern from it; `probeVectors()` derives one text per cell of {singular, plural} × {no separator} ∪ that list. **One definition, two consumers** — the pattern and the corpus that covers it can no longer disagree, because neither is typed out beside the other. This **supersedes DL-239(h)** as a code-state claim (the probe is no longer inline and is no longer that literal), and deliberately does NOT reverse its reasoning: (h) refused to widen the probe **to the grammar**, which would make it stop detecting what it exists to catch. That refusal stands — the probe is still a *looks-like* predicate whose `! parses` half is the caller guard, and it is still not derivable from `PATTERN`. What (h) did not anticipate is that a second grammar over card tokens, maintained inside a consumer, is precisely the restatement shape DL-239 was about.

**Decision (2) — `VECTORS` stays the SENTENCE corpus and gains exactly ONE plural row.** It feeds `describe()`, which renders a human-facing log line; its rejected side is *exemplary*, never exhaustive (the set of non-parsing strings is infinite). Seven plural rows would make that line worse, not more honest. `cards #123` names the family; **separator coverage is the derived property's job**, and the const's docblock says so, because the obvious "fix" for the next person is to paste the other six in.

**Decision (3) — the classifier test is driven off the grammar, and this is the load-bearing change.** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` drove a hand-written three-element list. It is the only leg that exercises the **runtime** surface this whole mechanism is about, and it reacted to nothing: the corpus edit that reds three legs in `PrTitleLintTest` left it green (measured, both directions — see below). It now drives `VECTORS ∪ probeVectors()`, routing each shape to the surface it can actually OCCUR on — across printable ASCII `git check-ref-format` rejects **exactly** space, `*`, `:`, `?`, `[`, `\`, `^`, `~` (measured by running it over all 95, not recalled), so those spellings reach the probe only through a PR title — so **both** call sites are covered and both are asserted to have been reached. The routing predicate names **all eight** rather than the two today's separators happen to use: scoped to `[\s:]` it would route a future `card^123` to `classifyPush()` as `refs/heads/feat/card^123`, a ref git will never produce, and the leg would keep passing while asserting on an impossible input.

**Decision (4) — a SECOND bash tie, `looks=` against the runtime probe, answer set to answer set.** DL-239 tied `looks=` to the vector set (a superset check) and `good=` to `PATTERN`. Nothing tied `looks=` to the **runtime** probe, so the two could diverge on any shape outside the corpus. The concrete hazard is not hypothetical: `looks=` widened to catch `cards #123` and miss `cards#123` is the one-character version of the original defect, and it is exactly what a fix driven from a bug report rather than from the separator data would produce. Driven with negatives present, so the comparison cannot pass as `[all-true] === [all-true]`. **Measured: that mutation reds this leg and no other leg in the only file that reads the YAML** — the vector-set superset check beside it stays green, because `cards #123` is the one plural row in the sentence corpus and `s? #` still catches it.

**The tie's corpus is the UNION of both engines' separator domains, and that is what makes it bidirectional.** Driven off `probeVectors()` alone it is one-directional, which was measured rather than reasoned: **adding** a separator to `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` without the YAML reds it, **removing** one does not — the corpus shrinks with the data, so the bash side is simply never asked about the dropped separator. Removals survived on an accident: every **non-accepted** separator happens to carry a curated `VECTORS` row for the classifier leg to catch it by, and dropping one of the two **accepted** ones (`-`, `#`), whose rows parse, was caught by nothing in any of the three files (measured — 95/95 green on that mutant). That is a property of today's corpus, not of the design: **DL-250's own thesis — one corpus, N guards blind together — reproduced inside the guard DL-250 added to close it.** So `probeVectors()` supplies the PHP side's domain (multi-character members included) and `card<c>123` / `cards<c>123` for every printable-ASCII `c` supplies a superset of any single-character class the YAML can spell; a narrowing on either side leaves the other side's separator in the corpus and the two answer sets diverge. Derived by ASKING the engines rather than by parsing the YAML's bracket class — a parse would red on a cosmetic regex edit, which is the wrong failure for a behavioural tie. **The bound, stated because it is real:** single-character separators are covered exhaustively on both sides by construction; **multi-character** ones only as `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` declares them, so one added to the YAML class *alone* is outside the corpus. A two-character cross-product cannot close that — a non-digit second character (`cards-x123`) makes `looks=`'s legitimate looseness (it requires no digit after the separator) read as a disagreement, so the tie would red on correct code.

**Decision (5) — the probe's space separator becomes a literal ` #`, narrowing it from `\s#`.** A tab or newline before the `#` no longer reads as a near-miss. This is a deliberate, measured narrowing: the separator list has to be literal strings for the cross-product to be built by concatenation, and the bash `looks=` predicate has always used a literal space — so the two engines now **agree**, which is what makes decision (4)'s tie meaningful. A tab-separated card token in a PR title is not a shape anyone has produced.

**Decision (6) — the bare space stays out, permanently, and the reason is recorded on the data.** DL-201 ruled that prose ("supports card 2") stays silent. `card 123` / `cards 123` are therefore not near-misses, every consumer of these lists asserts warn-iff-not-parsed, and a bare-space member would demand a warning the ruling forbids. Recorded on `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` and on `VECTORS` rather than left to be re-derived — a separator-derived corpus **cannot** widen into it, which is one more reason to derive rather than list.

**A property, not a comment: the probe's accepted separators are inert on the singular arm.** `-` and `#` are in the separator set although they are the ACCEPTED separators, which looks like it should change singular behavior and does not — every text matching `\bcard[-#]\d` parses, so no such text reaches a probe consulted only where `parse()` returned null. Pinned as an assertion in `CardTokenGrammarTest`, because a comment cannot red when the pattern moves.

**Disclosed, not buried: the `looks=` widening adds CI warn-noise on legitimately-plural branches.** `looks='…card([-#_.:]|[0-9]| #)'` became `…cards?(…)`, so a subject carrying a plural word immediately followed by one of those separators and a digit now draws a `::warning::` where it drew none. Measured on this branch: `feat/cards-2-column-layout`, `board cards-12 layout`, `refactor the cards.2 view`, `cards_2_grid` and `cards2go` all newly warn. The shape is bounded and stateable — the word `cards` at a token boundary, then a separator, then a digit, in the title or the head branch — not a general regression: `reorder the cards later` still warns nowhere. It is the price of catching `cards-123`, which is the *same string shape* written by an author who did mean a card; the predicate cannot tell them apart, which is exactly why DL-234 made this leg emit `::warning::` rather than gate — its exit code is pinned to 0 in `PrTitleLintTest`, so the extra noise can never become a merge block. **No accept/reject change:** the require step and the correlation grammar are untouched, and nothing that merged before merges differently now.

**Stated bound, unchanged and not fixed here.** The probe's digit class is ASCII (DL-231), so a Unicode-digit token stays silent at runtime — the CI lint's warning text covers that class by name instead. The derived classifier leg counts that row OUT explicitly rather than skipping it, so every corpus row is accounted for and the expected-warning total stays exact.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) **Add the two spellings from the bug report to `VECTORS` and stop** — rejected on re-measurement: the widened probe warns on seven plural shapes, so five would have shipped with no tie of any kind, and both bash-side checks would still have passed because both are only ever asked about the corpus. Enumerated-from-the-bug-report against a rule-shaped regex is the same defect one level down. (b) **Paste all seven plural rows into `VECTORS`** — rejected per decision (2): it fixes the coverage by growing the operator sentence, and the next separator added to the class re-opens the identical gap. (c) **Leave the probe inline in the classifier and tie it from the test side** — rejected per decision (1); it is the half-hoist, and it leaves the separator set uninspectable as data. (d) **Derive the near-miss set from `PATTERN`** — impossible by construction and already refused as DL-239(h); the near-miss set is deliberately a different set. (e) **Fix the lint's `looks=` false positive on `card-layout-rework`** (it matches `looks` with no digit after the separator, so an ordinary `card-*` branch draws a CI warning) — declined on **scope**: it is a *different* defect, on the separator-with-no-digit arm, where this card's subject is the plural arm; it needs its own answer, and it is the reason `looks=` and the runtime probe are equal only on the separator cross-product rather than everywhere. **Explicitly NOT declined on the grounds first written here — *"it changes what a CI check reports"* — because that does not discriminate: this PR's own `looks=` widening changes what that same check reports** (measured, in the disclosure above). A stated discriminator that both sides satisfy licenses a later agent to skip the repo's hard gate on one `looks=` edit and demand it on the other, which is worse than having none. Surfaced, not fixed.

**Tests — every changed leg proven failable by mutation, run and read, each restored.** The probe loses `s?` → the assembly leg, the new bash tie, and the derived classifier leg all red (12 expected warnings, 5 observed). `looks=` reverts → 3 red, including the new tie. `looks=` widened for `cards #123` but not `cards#123` → **only** the new tie reds. One separator dropped from `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` → the probe measurably stops accepting it AND the derived classifier leg reds, through the curated `VECTORS` row that survives the drop — which is what shows the pattern and the corpus really are one source. `PATTERN`'s separated arm narrowed to ≥2 digits → the inertness property reds. **Four more once the union corpus landed, one per direction the tie has to catch, each run against BOTH the new and the pre-union test file so the delta is the measurement:** a separator ADDED to `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` alone (`~`) → the tie reds, naming `card~123`/`cards~123` (it already did); one REMOVED from it alone (`:`) → the tie now reds naming `card:123`/`cards:123`, where the same mutation left **all 17** legs of the pre-union `PrTitleLintTest` green; one removed from the YAML `looks=` class alone (`:`) → 3 legs red, the tie among them; and the sharpest — the ACCEPTED separator `-` removed from `NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` alone → the tie reds, where before it was caught by **nothing at all**: `PrTitleLintTest`, `CardTokenGrammarTest` and `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` ran 95/95 green on the mutant. The removal direction had been surviving on the accident that every **non-accepted** separator happens to carry a curated `VECTORS` row for the classifier leg to catch it by; the two accepted ones carry rows that PARSE, so nothing was asking. And the before/after this card exists for: with the probe reverted and the plural row present in the corpus, the **pre-change** hand-written classifier test passes 71/71 while three `PrTitleLintTest` legs red — the derived replacement reds on the identical state. Card#5691.

## DL-251 — `unvalidated` gets a RULE, not a re-assignment: the leg that did not answer its own question — and the three legs a warn-keyed sweep could never have found

**Date:** 2026-07-31 (UTC)

**Context.** DL-238 (d) deliberately left the `warn` ↔ `unvalidated` boundary unsettled and said so in `Severity`'s docblock rather than guessing, because the discriminator drafted there (*"unvalidated = the check did not run and nothing is wrong"*) failed on a live site: `CheckCommand`'s event-consumer fail-soft catch is a genuine anomaly that DL-236 had already assigned `unvalidated`. That left ~21 legs reporting `warn` *because they could not measure*, which is why every disclosure this program shipped — the closing tally, stage 8's inventory bound, the JSON contract's §4 note — had to carry the same caveat: **the absence of `unvalidated` is not evidence a leg was measured.** Stage 10 of the check-registry plan (`docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`) is the gated row that settles it. Cards **#5291** (the boundary) and **#5292** (a `type` key written at 3 sites, read at 0).

**Decision (1) — the rule is PER LEG and it is one sentence: `unvalidated` ⟺ the leg did not answer its own question.** It lives in `App\Bridge\Support\Severity`'s docblock, replacing the "not settled" paragraph, and every other surface points at it rather than restating it. Answered ⇒ `ok`/`warn`/`fail` by the answer. Not answered because of a fact about the **install** ⇒ `unvalidated`. Not answered because the operator did not **ask** ⇒ no finding; the `not-requested` disposition (the ruling in the plan's § Resolved design decision, unchanged and now composed with this as limb 3). A leg is unanswered when **(a)** the measurement did not complete, **(b)** it completed but the leg cannot stand behind it because it may have measured the wrong subject, or **(c)** a COMPARISON leg's comparand does not resolve to exactly one *comparable* value. Per LEG and not per check because several checks deliberately carry many legs — `WritebackBoardStateCheck` and `WritebackMappingConfigCheck` both say *ONE CHECK, NOT ONE PER LEG* in their own docblocks and give the reason (a per-leg split would reorder operator output on a multi-mapping install).

**Explicitly adjudicated, because each was contested in design review and an unrecorded adjudication is one that gets re-litigated:**
- **`sudo`-gated ssh is NOT an invocation fact.** It was argued that `SshTransportProbe`'s *"re-run as root"* legs are like a withheld `--probe-tools-ssh` and therefore belong on the disposition axis. **They are not.** A withheld flag is a request the operator DECLINED TO MAKE; an insufficient euid is a **capability the process lacks** while running a leg the operator DID ask for — that leg runs unconditionally on every `bridge:check`. Both are swept: `:93` under limb (a) (the read did not complete), `:106` under limb (b) (it completed against a file sshd may not consult).
- **World-ambiguity is not measurement-ambiguity.** *"The token sees 0 cards"* was measured; what it IMPLIES is ambiguous, and the finding says both. It stays `warn`. Same for its board-tools twin.
- **A skipped DOWNSTREAM leg rides the disposition axis, and the discriminator is ENVELOPE WIDTH** — a property of the code, not a judgement. An envelope wrapping one construction can name the cause (`warn` + a not-run reason); one wrapping construction AND the run cannot, and its own comment already said the reason is *pitched at the envelope* — that one is swept.
- **`ChannelSnapshotProbe`'s launch disclosure needs no special clause.** An earlier revision added a fourth limb for it; that was an epicycle *and* it contradicted the one-meaning ruling. "The bridge runs as a different OS user" is an install fact, so limb 2 reaches it.
- **`EventFollowsConsumerCheck`'s advisory stays `warn`** — the non-throw path answers its question. (The throw path over-claims for a different reason and belongs to card#5698, not here.)

**Decision (2) — the THREE SILENT legs, which is the half the row did not ask for.** Every method of finding the sweep's population starts from sites that *report* `warn`, so it is blind by construction to a leg that answers nothing and prints nothing. Three exist. **Two are comparison legs:** `WritebackBoardStateCheck`'s mapped-stage-id compare and `BoardToolsBoardStateCheck`'s `create_stage_id` compare, both guarded on a non-empty board-stage read. Not warning on an empty read was RIGHT — it is not evidence the ids are wrong. Saying nothing was not: **both legs are also silent when they succeed**, so silence meant "every id exists" AND "the ids were never compared to anything", at the two legs whose entire job is catching a silent 422. **The third is a shared `switch` arm:** `ReconcileRepoTokensCheck` fell through `GitHubRepoProbeKind::Ok` into `::Network` — *"could not reach GitHub (timeout/connection)"* — with one `break`, so a token proven good and a token this run never managed to probe produced identical output (nothing) from the leg whose whole subject is whether that token works. Staying out of the token-problem vocabulary was right (a blip is not a token-validity signal, and the new message says so); staying silent was not. **All three now emit `unvalidated`,** under limb (c) for the two comparands and limb (a) for the probe that did not complete. This ADDS output lines rather than re-assigning them, which is why it belongs inside the row's gate. **Measured at write time against the escape hatch the build spec left open:** 42 added lines across THREE production files — 24 for the two comparison legs (13 + 11, re-counted at write time from the diff hunks rather than inherited) and 18 for the `switch`-arm split plus the docblock paragraph that explains it (comment + code, including the `if`/`else` restructure and the `switch`-arm split; the severity flips in those same files are excluded — they belong to the sweep), plus 3 rewritten test methods. It did not materially widen the diff, so it was not dropped.

**⚠ Decision (2a) — the METHOD defect behind (2), recorded because it is the root cause and it is NOT fixed (canon #2).** The first pass of this stage found TWO silent legs and shipped "two exist" as a population; the third was found later, by re-reading, in a file the stage had never opened. **Every derivation in this repo keys on something a leg EMITTED** — `Finding::warn`, `Severity::Warn`, a message signature, a golden line — and a leg that emits nothing appears in none of them, so **no command enumerates this category and none was run**. The silent-leg set was produced by READING the check subsystem, which makes **three a FLOOR, not a set**, and that is written into the stage-10 result rather than left implied. The nearest available derivation is structural, not textual — enumerate every `switch` arm, `else`-less `if` and early `return` inside a `Check::run()`/`runFor()` generator and ask what each CONCLUDED — and it is a static-analysis job that does not exist. Naming it is the filing; it is not claimed as built, and the honest reading of decision (2) is "three found", never "three exist". **The sharpest part: the third leg's file was already flagged.** `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`'s stage-3a result says, three stages early, that `bin/check-golden-mutate.php` does not enumerate `switch` arms and that `reconcile.repo_tokens`'s four arms are *"absent from the disclosed-gap list entirely"*. That disclosure was correct and the sweep walked past it, because the disclosure is prose and the sweep was a grep. **A disclosed gap with no instrument behind it is still closed only by someone happening to re-read the file** — which is a finding about this whole program's method, not about this stage.

**Decision (3) — `severityMeansSetupIncomplete()` widened to `Unvalidated => true` IN THE SAME COMMIT, and the hazard it re-opens is recorded rather than absorbed.** That predicate has one caller (the DL-225 flipped-default advisory) and one input (`SshPinnedLineCheck`), whose two `warn`s are both in the sweep — so leaving it would have taken the advisory from flagging both to flagging neither and silently dropped it on the install shape it exists for. Witnessed, not reasoned: reverting the widening while keeping the sweep drops the advisory line out of the `board-tools-ssh-default-transport-advisory` golden and reds the suite.
**⚠ The widening makes the predicate EXTENSIONALLY `$severity !== Severity::Ok` — the proxy DL-236 (f) replaced — and exactly one thing still separates them: it is an exhaustive `match`, so a fifth severity is a phpstan error instead of being swept in silently.** It reds `CheckCommandSeverityContractTest`'s DL-238 (g) watch-item, which is **replaced, not deleted**: the predicate assertion now reads *"everything but `ok`"*, and a second test pins the severity SET the pinned-line leg can emit (derived from the method's source, not from a fixture corpus — a behavioural union is blind to an arm no fixture reaches). **DL-238 (g) is NARROWED, NOT CLOSED.** Post-sweep, `unvalidated` on this path means *"could not read authorized_keys"* (setup IS incomplete) and would mean the opposite for any future structurally-unmeasurable finding — **the same enum value**, which no severity assertion can separate. The replacement is a **tripwire**: it detects that the emitted set MOVED and forces a decision; it cannot classify what moved into it. **Root cause, named and OUT OF SCOPE (canon #2):** the advisory infers an install FACT from a SEVERITY. Having `probePinnedLine()` return the setup-incomplete fact directly removes the coupling instead of re-tuning a severity map, and that is the fix — deliberately not built here, because it changes what the ssh probe returns and belongs with its own evidence.
The slot-level argument for the widening being safe is separate and holds: a slot that never ran emits **no findings** (`CheckRunner` attaches a reason only), so *"told incomplete on the strength of a check nobody ran"* cannot occur at slot level.

**Decision (4) — `schema` stays `1`, on two independently checkable grounds, both written into the contract's bump table rather than asserted here.** (i) **No tagged release has ever carried the contract** — `git ls-tree v0.71.0 app/Bridge/Check/` is empty, verified at build time, so there is no consumer and the change IS the contract. It is worded as that command rather than as "it's the same release", which is a judgement about intent and not checkable. (ii) A **pre-disclosed precision correction** to which findings carry which severity is not a bump: §4 of the contract told consumers not to read the absence of `unvalidated` as *measured*, and named the landing. Delivering exactly the disclosed correction is the contract doing its job; the row explicitly does not cover an **undisclosed** re-assignment, which changes a key's meaning and bumps.

**Decision (5) — card#5292: the `type` key is DELETED, not migrated.** `BoardToolAgentResolver::problems()` typed each entry `bearer_unreadable | collision`, justified in three docblocks as letting `bridge:check` split severity. The split was decided the other way (both FAIL under default-ON, DL-217 v7), and the key was **read at zero call sites for its entire life**. An unused affordance is not free: it is a claim in the source about what a consumer can do, and it was false. `problems()` returns `list<string>`. Six source sites and two test comments carried the claim; the derivation found one the design pass had missed, which is why the build ran the grep instead of trusting the list.

**Decision (6) — the tripwire pins CALL SITES, and its exhaustiveness is structural.** `Finding`'s constructor was **public** and three checks used it to re-scope another probe's finding, so `Finding::unvalidated(` was never the only door and a text guard over it was never complete. The constructor is now **private**, and the three sites go through a new severity-preserving `Finding::scoped()` — canon #5 on three near-identical edits through one primitive. `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` pins the exact per-file construction set **and** asserts the constructor is private, because the second is what makes the first exhaustive. **It is stated as a tripwire and not as a proof:** it reds when the set moves and forces a human decision; it cannot say which severity is right, it constrains no `warn` site, and it says nothing about whether a site is reachable.

**Decision (7) — the disclosure NARROWS rather than dies, and the tally line survives a SECOND narrowing.** Stage 8 narrowed it once ("a floor, because the vocabulary is imprecise"). That sentence is now false, and deleting the line would have read as *"everything unmeasured is now counted"* — a stronger claim than this change earns. The rule is keyed on **what a leg concluded**, so it can only make DISCLOSED blindness precise. **The residual is what the line is NOT allowed to mis-describe, and the first draft of it did:** it said a leg that never notices it measured nothing *"still says nothing"*. That is false — such a leg may also report the conclusion it would have drawn had the measurement happened, which is a confidently WRONG finding rather than an absence (`EventFollowsConsumerCheck`'s undeclared-classifier advisory fires off `CheckCommand`'s swallowed classifier throw; card#5698 owns the class). Describing the residual as silence tells an operator that everything they DO see is precise — the same overclaim one narrowing up. The shipped line therefore says the residual **is not counted here** and names both shapes: *"it may say nothing, or say what it would have concluded."* It also drops the phrase *"the disclosed population"*, which collided with `emitInventory()`'s line printed immediately above it — that line discloses the NOT-RUN checks, which this count excludes, and two adjacent lines cannot both own the phrase. `check-json-contract.md` moved in step — `unvalidated` is sound evidence a leg could not measure; its **absence** is still not evidence everything was.

**Salience loss, recorded because it is a real cost and the gate is entitled to see it — and its FIRST statement was scoped too narrowly.** Five swept sites name an actionable coord-config defect (`WritebackBoardStateCheck`'s three terminal-compare arms, `WritebackMappingConfigCheck`'s two issue_population arms) and go from yellow to plain. **That cluster is not the whole cost, and saying only "coord-config" implied it was.** A pass over all 21 swept messages finds **seven that spell an explicit operator ACTION** and lose their yellow, and they are a set DISJOINT from those five (the five diagnose a coord-config defect without naming a command; their tails say only what will go wrong): the two *"Point `bridge.writeback.coord_config_path` (or `$COORD_CONFIG`) at coordination.config.json"* arms, the two `SshTransportProbe` pinned-line legs (*"re-run as root"*), and three `ChannelSnapshotProbe` arms — an unreadable/absent/malformed DEPLOYED `package.json` (*grant read access · repair the manifest · re-copy the directory*, one action per cause), an unreadable BUNDLED `package.json` (*restore or repair a tracked file*), and a path this user cannot traverse (*re-run as the agent's user, or grant it traversal*). Twelve of the 21 in total, then, carry either a named defect or a named action into plain text. Accepted, on the same argument for all of them: what those legs report is that the MEASUREMENT could not be made, not that anything was proven wrong, and presenting an unmade measurement in the colour reserved for a measured anomaly is the miscalibration rather than the fix for it. The line still prints, and it now enters the closing tally — a coverage statement the yellow never made. **It goes in the PR body and the release notes**, because an operator watching for yellow will see fewer of them.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Sweep and leave the rule unwritten** — rejected: the next leg re-mints the boundary question, which is the recurrence this whole program is funded to stop; a sweep without a rule is 21 local fixes. (b) **A fifth `Severity` case for "could not measure"** — rejected: it splits the one signal card#5170 created and breaks the exhaustive-`match` and exit-contract properties for a distinction the disposition axis already carries. (c) **Leave the silent legs silent** and note them — rejected per decision (2): they are the exact defect shape, inside the stage built to remove it. (d) **Bump `schema` to 2 to be safe** — rejected: it mints a version that existed only on a dev branch, and "to be safe" is what makes a version number stop meaning anything. (e) **Fix the DL-225 advisory's root cause here** (return the fact, not a severity) — rejected as scope: correct, named, and owed its own evidence. (f) **A phrase-ban tripwire on message text** — rejected: an earlier revision of it was red on landing (the messages share no phrase) and blind to four swept sites; message strings are operator prose and get reworded.

**Tests — the RED came first at every site, and where it could not, that is said.** The 7 swept sites with **no** severity assertion (`WritebackMappingConfigCheck:191,196`, `WritebackBoardStateCheck:244,264,278`, `ChannelSnapshotProbe:276`, `CheckCommand:384` — one more than the design pass had enumerated, found by re-deriving instead of transcribing) each got an assertion pinning `warn` **first**, seen green, then seen RED under the sweep, then flipped. The 14 that had one went red on the sweep directly. **23 tests were watched failing** in one run before any was updated. Four tripwire mutations on a **detached copy**: adding a site reds the pin, removing one reds it, **re-publicising the constructor plus a `new Finding(Severity::Unvalidated, …)` bypass leaves the pin GREEN and reds only the reachability guard** — which is precisely why that second assertion exists — and the same bypass against the private constructor is a fatal `Error`, i.e. unrepresentable. The §3 pairing was witnessed by reverting the widening on that copy and watching the advisory line disappear from a golden.

**The follow-up pass carried its own reds, each named with the mutation that produced it.** (i) The `Network` split: the pre-existing `assertSame([], …)` was watched failing against the new arm, printing the exact `unvalidated` finding, before the assertion was rewritten — then the new assertion was mutation-proven by deleting the `yield` and watching *"actual size 0 matches expected size 1"*. (ii) The call-site tripwire reds on the new site unprompted, which is the guard doing the job it was built for and is recorded rather than routed around. (iii) The `$targets === []` guard: mutated to `if (false)` and watched red at *"only the board-visibility line is owed"*. (iv) The board-tools `assertCount(2)`: a spurious third `Finding::warn` inserted into the empty-stage arm reds it at *"actual size 3 matches expected size 2"* — the mutation that its absence let through. **And one finding about the ORIGINAL evidence, which is the more useful half:** the §2b writeback test was built on the shared `mapping()` helper, whose `stages` is `[]` — so it asserted *"could NOT check the mapped stage ids"* for a mapping that mapped **no** stage ids, i.e. it stood on the exact false positive the guard now removes. A test written on a defect's own shape cannot see the defect; it now uses a mapping that targets a stage, and the empty-target case gets its own test asserting the absence of BOTH arms.

**The goldens cannot witness a severity, and the regeneration says so.** All 33 fixtures come from an undecorated buffer (DL-248), so the four channels write identical bytes. **Not one message line changed.** 8 fixtures changed and every delta is accounted for: 6 gain a tally line where none existed (0→1), one goes 1→2, and one changes only the tally's own wording. For those 7 the golden discriminates the site **through the count**; it is still not a severity witness. **A SECOND regeneration followed the tally's correction** — the same 8 files, one line each, every delta the tail of that sentence, no count moved (`8 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)`), which is the measurement that the wording is isolated from every other line. **The `Network` split reaches no fixture at all:** it needs a real connection failure to api.github.com, which an `Http::fake` corpus cannot produce, so `ReconcileRepoTokensCheckTest` is its only witness — the same shape as the other three arms of that `switch`, and the reason that test exists. The **JSON** consequence was witnessed by nothing at all — `CheckJsonContractTest` asserted only 4-value membership, true before and after — so a document-level assertion now pins one swept site on each side of the registry boundary.

**⚠ WHAT THIS SHIPS THAT IS STILL WRONG, disclosed rather than discovered (card#5698).** The §2b legs put an `unvalidated` — *"the board returned no workflow stages, so there was nothing to compare against"* — DIRECTLY BELOW a swimlane leg that convicts the operator's config off the SAME unresolved read (*"swimlane_id X is not on board Y — created cards will 422"*). Both board-state checks now carry that pair. The root cause is one level down and is NOT a call-site problem: `KanbanClient::idList()` — and `preloadStages()` with it — collapses *genuinely empty*, *key absent from the response*, and *rows present but malformed* into a single `[]`, so no caller can distinguish "this board has no swimlanes" from "the read did not resolve". Guarding each leg would be N downstream patches over one upstream defect (canon #2/#5); the fix is for the client to return a result that keeps the three apart. **Filed on card#5698 with that analysis, and named here so the contradiction does not ship silently.** The §2b legs still go in: replacing silence with a disclosure is strictly better than the swimlane leg's status quo, and the asymmetry is now visible instead of being two different kinds of invisible.

**Out of scope, and NOT claimed:** card#5698's overclaim class (which now also carries the `idList()` collapse above); card#5701; and the **`fail` and `ok` populations — 41 and 32 construction sites respectively, counted at write time — which were not audited against the rule**. Nothing here claims the vocabulary is precise everywhere.

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, and NO exit-code change** — `emitFinding()` returns false only for `fail`, asserted as a property, so re-assigning `warn` → `unvalidated` cannot move an exit code by construction. **Operator-visible: yes** — 21 findings render plain instead of yellow, 3 new lines appear (one of them only on an install that cannot reach api.github.com), and the closing tally counts more.

## DL-252 — A `from:` label is evidence of who OPENED a thread, never of who acted on it: the coord Intent splits actor from author, and says "unattributable" out loud

**Date:** 2026-07-31
**Context — the field was right on the common case and confidently wrong on the rest, and a reader who was not looking was misled.** `CoordinationClassifier::reattribute()` recovered one name — `scope_author_map`, else the `from:<agent>` label, else the body `FROM:` line — and placed it in the Intent's **`Actor`** and in the rendered summary's `from <name>` slot. On `issue_comment.created` that is correct (the actor wrote the comment). On `issues.opened` it is correct (the actor opened the thread). On every OTHER handled action — `reopened`, `ready_for_review`, and anything an install adds via `coord_extra_actions` — the label is the *frozen thread-opener* (DL-035) and the body is the opening post, so the classifier reported the thread's author as the agent that acted. Its own docblock said "the from: label is the frozen thread-opener" and the method was NAMED for recovering the author; the conflation was encoded in the naming, not hidden in a branch. **Three sightings in two days (not offered as a rate), and the third is the one that settles severity:** a seat that had never heard of the defect read `coord issue #439 from moodle …` on a bodyless `reopened`, formed a belief about who reopened it, and wrote that belief into a coordination post as fact. The bound on the damage was that the seat declined to act on it — a discipline, not a property of the channel. Reported via roundtable #209 (finding + measurement credited to AIMLA's platform seat, AIMLA #464 R16); card#5721. **[card#6025:** there is no `CoordinationClassifier::reattribute()` in the tree today — the entry records the code as it stood.**]**

**Decision — emit the actor as UNATTRIBUTABLE on those actions, carry the thread author in its own field, and make the state explicit on BOTH surfaces.** `reattribute()` becomes `attribute()`, which returns the three facts the one value was standing in for: `actor` (who performed THIS event, or null), `thread_author` (whose subject it is), and `echo_author` (the pre-change union, unchanged, read by exactly one caller — see (f)). The Intent's `actor` is the first; `payload` gains `actor_attribution` (always present: `resolved` / `unresolved` / `unattributable`) and `thread_author`; `payload.from` is null exactly on `unattributable`; and the summary renders `by an unattributable actor (thread opened by <name>)` in the slot that used to read `from <name>`.

- **(a) Why not resolve the real actor.** Unrecoverable, not unimplemented. Under `github.shared_identity` every seat posts as one account, so the webhook `sender` is identical for all of them (the reporter took the distinct actor set across a whole thread timeline and got a single login). No field in a bodyless payload discriminates. "Try harder" is not an option on the table; the only honest remedies are to stop implying an actor, or to say who the author is *as the author*. This does both, which is the option the requester endorsed over their own two.
- **(b) Why the marker is not optional polish, argued twice and the second argument is the stronger.** First: an absent key and a null one read identically to a careless consumer, and "the field is missing" is the shape that later gets papered over with a read-time fallback (canon #5). Second, and decisive: **the exposed consumer is a naive reader, not a script.** An absent field renders as *nothing at all*, and nothing-at-all is indistinguishable from a summary that simply did not mention who acted — which is precisely the gap the misled seat filled from context. Dropping the name only stops telling the reader something false; the marker gets them to the right belief. Note the shape: `actor.name` was ALREADY nullable with null meaning "the registry could not resolve it", so reusing null for "no actor exists to resolve" would have re-minted, in the payload, the exact could-not-distinguish defect of DL-236 and DL-251 — the joke writing itself.
- **(c) Three states, not two.** `resolved` / `unresolved` / `unattributable`. Collapsing the last two would say "nobody wrote it down" and "nothing could ever be written down" with one word, and only the second is a property of the event class. `unattributable` is the accurate word by DL-236 (c)'s own test — name what is known about the MEASUREMENT, not the decision — and its bound is stated in the consumer guide: it is a claim about this event under this install's config (a `scope_author_map` entry, or a non-shared account, still resolves), not a universal one.
- **(d) The affected set is DERIVED, not hand-listed.** `AUTHORING_ACTIONS` names the ONE action per prefix that creates the text the classifier reads (`issues.opened`, `issue_comment.created`, `pull_request.opened`); `subject()` computes `authored_by_actor` from the same `$prefix`/`$action` pair that selects the subject, so the flag cannot drift from the event it describes. Two gates fall out of it and they are NOT the same predicate: the body `FROM:` line attributes the actor iff the actor **wrote that body**, while the `from:` label attributes the actor iff the actor **opened the labelled subject** (`authored_by_actor && ! comment`) — which is why a *comment* never takes its actor from the thread's label. It is an ALLOW-list: an action nobody enumerated — a future GitHub action, or one an install adds via `coord_extra_actions` — is non-authoring, so a widening can only lose a name, never invent one. `pull_request.ready_for_review` lands on the non-authoring side deliberately: anyone with write access can mark a PR ready, so the opener is not evidence, and fail-safe beats usually-right. A test pins the two constants to the same key set (the derivation fatals loudly on a missing key rather than defaulting — verified by mutation).
- **(e) `issues.opened` is NOT part of the defect and is byte-identical.** There the author IS the actor. Every pre-existing assertion on that path passes unchanged — including the summary, which is asserted whole (`coord issue #4 from other to me: T`) and not by substring, so a formatting drift on the attributable branch reds.
- **(f) WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIX, and why that is a scope call rather than an oversight.** `ClassifyResult::reattributedActor` still carries the **union** — actor if known, else the thread author — because it is not a rendering: the dispatcher re-runs the per-agent echo check on it (DL-005) and **drops the dispatch** when it matches the serving agent. So the same conflation has a *delivery* consequence that this change leaves standing: on a thread the serving agent opened (`from:<me>`), a **counterparty's** `reopened`/`closed` is attributed to that agent and suppressed as "echo: own write" — and so is a **bare** reply with no `FROM:` line, which is exactly the case DL-235's `bare_reply_to_own_thread` grant was built to wake (the classifier grants it; the dispatcher then drops it). Narrowing the echo input would make previously-dropped events start being delivered — a change to what the system delivers, which is hard-gated and was not approved here. It is pinned by two tests so it cannot drift silently, and it is filed for its own decision. **Read this bullet as the honest bound on the fix: the misleading RENDERING is closed; the mis-SUPPRESSION is not.**
- **(g) The sibling the audit found in the same primitive.** A comment *preferred* the body `FROM:` line but **fell back** to the frozen label, so a bare reply by anyone on someone else's thread reported the thread's opener as its author — the same conflation, on the one kind the brief for this work described as unaffected. Fixed here (the comment's own body is a comment's only actor evidence), and it reports `unresolved`, not `unattributable`, because that action *could* have carried the evidence.
- **(h) Not fixed, reported: the FROM-line parse exists twice.** `attribute()` uses an inline `preg_match('/^\s*FROM:\s*(\S+)/mi')` while the same file already calls the shipped `RecipientAddressing::author()` (DL-035) for DL-235's echo guard — two implementations of one parse, and they DIVERGE (`FROM: alice, bob` yields `alice,` from the inline one and `alice` from the helper). Consolidating changes which name gets attributed on real bodies, so it is a behavior change and not this change's business. Extracted to `fromBodyLine()` so there is now exactly one copy of each parse *inside* the classifier, which is what makes the divergence a two-site question instead of an N-site one. **Three things the honest version of this bullet has to add, because leaving them out is what made the copy look cheap.** (1) **A shipped doc forbids the copy that was kept:** `docs/customization.md` § Per-agent echo tells a classifier author to parse the `FROM:` line "via the shipped `RecipientAddressing::author()` helper — no hand-rolled regex", which is exactly what DL-035 replaced in that same example — so the flagship shipped classifier now does what its own customization guide tells operators not to. (2) **This change put a THIRD read on the divergent copy, and it is consumer-facing:** on an issue/PR subject `payload.thread_author` falls back to `fromBodyLine()`, so `FROM: alice, bob` in an opening post surfaces `alice,` in a newly documented field — before this change the divergence reached only the (internal) echo input and the summary. (3) **The two parses read the same body inside ONE `classify()` call and can name different people:** on a comment, `RecipientAddressing::author()` decides the DL-235 bare-reply wake grant (its echo clause compares that name against the serving agent) while `fromBodyLine()` decides `payload.from` — so a comment reading `FROM: alice, bob` is written by `alice` for the grant and by `alice,` for attribution, in one event. Verified at source, not assumed. The consolidation is still a behavior change and still gated — this bullet is the disclosure, not a discharge.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) render the label-derived name as the author and keep it in `Actor` — rejected with the requester: it keeps a real datum in a lying field. (b) emit the actor as unknown and drop the name — rejected: it makes the type honest by destroying information, and (b) above says why silence is not enough. (c) put the marker on `Actor` itself rather than in `payload` — rejected: `actor` is a **closed** object in `docs/event-schema.json` (`additionalProperties: false`, three required keys) shared by every classifier, so a new field there is a schema-version question for surfaces that have no attribution problem, while `payload` is per-`kind` and open. (d) omit the key on the attributable path so consumers can test presence — rejected: that is (b)'s absent-key shape re-introduced as an optimization. (e) name the third state `unknown` — rejected: `unknown` describes the reader's state, and `unresolved` is also unknown; the distinction being drawn is whether evidence CAN exist.

**Tests — 14 new, all 14 watched RED against the pre-change classifier** (production file reverted, suite re-run, restored): 7 assertion failures + 7 missing-payload-key errors (`Undefined array key` — an `E_WARNING` promoted to `ErrorException`, so PHPUnit reports them as errors rather than assertion failures, and the receiver would record them as dispatch errors; see the correction at the end of this paragraph), including the two that print the defect verbatim — `'coord issue #4 from other to me: T'` where the expectation is `'coord issue #4 by an unattributable actor (thread opened by other) to me: T'`. Three assertions are GREEN under revert by design and are labelled here rather than banked as revert coverage, each proven failable by a named mutation: the two echo-input pins (green because they assert a NON-change; red when `reattributedActor` is narrowed to `attribute()['actor']`), and the back-compat `issues.opened` summary (red when `AUTHORING_ACTIONS['issues.']` is flipped to `reopened`). The constant-coverage guard reds on deleting a family key — and a family added to `HANDLED` with no `AUTHORING_ACTIONS` entry raises `Undefined array key` on the derivation rather than silently treating the family as non-authoring. **Stated at the weakest true strength, because the first draft of this line overstated both halves:** it is NOT a fatal — PHP 8 emits an `E_WARNING`, the framework's registered error handler promotes it to `ErrorException`, and `DispatchService`'s classify `catch (Throwable)` records it via `recordError()`, so it surfaces as that one agent's errored (replayable) dispatch under treatment A, not as a dead receiver. And no docblock claims fail-loud for it: `AUTHORING_ACTIONS`'s own docblock claims the opposite property — a fail-SAFE allow-list ("a widening can only lose a name, never invent one"). The loudness is a property of the array read, not a documented contract, which is exactly why the constant-coverage test is the thing keeping it unreached.

**Doc-sync:** `docs/consumer-guide.md` gains § *Coordination intents: who acted vs. whose thread* (the per-`kind` field contract, the three states, the explicit "do not fall back to `thread_author`", the THREE evidence paths behind `resolved`, and the per-path bound on it — two of the three are operator-writable text and are not authentication, the third is the upstream sender identity); `docs/config-schema.md` `scope_author_map` (under a shared upstream identity it is the only path that survives a non-authoring action — so setting it on a multi-author repo mis-reports every actor) and `coord_extra_actions` (what an added action's attribution will be); `docs/customization.md` + `ClassifyResult`'s own docblock, which both claimed **"every shipped classifier leaves `reattributedActor` null"** — false since `CoordinationClassifier` shipped, corrected at both sites (DL-005's own text stays frozen; it was true when written).

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no exit-code change, no token-scope change, and no correlation change** (`CardTokenGrammar` / `DlTokenGrammar` / the PR-title and branch grammars are untouched — DL-201/DL-233/DL-250 are not in this diff). **Additive on the wire:** `payload` is open and per-`kind` in `docs/event-schema.json`, so no schema-version bump; `actor`'s closed shape is unchanged. **⚠ CONSUMER-VISIBLE ON TWO SHAPES, not one** — the sibling in (g) changes the wire on an AUTHORING action too, and an earlier draft of this line covered only the first: **(1) non-authoring action** (`reopened` / `ready_for_review` / any `coord_extra_actions` addition) — `payload.from` is now `null` where it carried the thread author, `actor_attribution` is `unattributable`, and the summary's `from <name>` becomes `by an unattributable actor (…)`. **(2) authoring action, bare comment** — an `issue_comment.created` with no body `FROM:` line on a `from:<opener>`-labelled thread no longer falls back to the label: `payload.from` goes from the opener's name to the actor's raw upstream id (`'99'` in the tests; `'?'` when the event carried no id), `actor_attribution` is `unresolved`, and the summary goes from `coord comment #9 from <opener>: T` to `coord comment #9 from 99: T`. In both shapes every key stays PRESENT — `from` carries null or a value, never absence, and `actor_attribution` names which. The requester's own pre-ship audit found their three consumers immune BY MECHANISM (`wake_membership` reads the `from:` label off the issue; `coord-thread-read` and `coord_attribution.py` parse the body `FROM:` line) — none reads the Intent's actor. 1885/1885 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs.php` clean. Card#5721.
