## DL-253 — A drop is a claim that THIS AGENT WROTE THIS EVENT: the echo input narrows to the actor, and "nobody can be named" starts DELIVERING instead of dropping

**Date:** 2026-08-01

**Context — DL-252 fixed how the event READ and left how it was DELIVERED, and the delivery half was the one silently costing messages.** That entry's bullet (f) is the whole context and it was written as a scope call, not an oversight: `attribute()` returned a third value, `echo_author`, the pre-DL-252 UNION of *who acted* and *whose thread it is*, and `ClassifyResult::reattributedActor` carried it because the dispatcher DROPS on that value (DL-005). On a thread the serving agent had opened (`from:<me>`, frozen at open per DL-035), a **counterparty's** bodyless action — `reopened`, `closed`, `ready_for_review`, anything an install adds via `coord_extra_actions` — carried that agent's own name into `DispatchService`'s post-classify echo recheck, matched, and was dropped as `echo: own write (reattributed author)`. **The seat never saw it, at all.** The same held for a **bare reply with no `FROM:` line**, whose only recoverable name is that same frozen label — which is precisely the population DL-235's `bare_reply_to_own_thread` grant was built to wake (aimla-pm measured **112 dropped coordination comments per impl agent**). **The guard's own comment stated the assumption that made it wrong** — *"re-run the SAME per-agent echo check now that attribution is better"* — when on these actions attribution was not better, it was the thread's author wearing the actor's slot. Filed as card#5738 rather than folded into card#5721, deliberately: a delivery defect inside a rendering-fix bundle inherits that bundle's priority and goes quiet (canon #18).

**Decision — `reattributedActor` carries `attribute()`'s `actor`, and `echo_author` is DELETED rather than narrowed.** One fact, one place: the value the dispatcher drops on is now the same value the Intent reports, and the union that produced two answers to "who is this?" no longer exists to be re-read by a future caller. `null` is therefore a real answer and it **delivers**.

- **(a) Why null must deliver rather than drop.** Under `github.shared_identity` (DL-002) a bodyless event carries no evidence of who acted — that is DL-252 (a) and it has not changed. So the choice is not "correct vs. incorrect" but **which error to make when the system cannot tell**: drop, and every counterparty action on your own threads disappears (measured, live, and invisible — a drop leaves no inbox row to notice); or deliver, and you occasionally see your own evidence-free action. **The cost of a wrong delivery is one read; the cost of a wrong drop is the message.** Asymmetric, so it decides.
- **(b) What is PRESERVED, and it is the whole of DL-005's purpose.** Every path that genuinely evidences the actor still suppresses the agent's own write: `scope_author_map` (which survives even a bodyless action — one agent does everything on that repo), the `from:` label on the action that OPENED the labelled subject, and the body `FROM:` line on the action that WROTE that body. A **different** shared-id agent's write still carries a non-self name and still surfaces. Pinned by a test per evidence path, each proven failable by mutation (below).
- **(c) The residual cost, stated rather than discovered later: an agent's own evidence-free action on its own thread now wakes it.** Its own `reopened`/`closed`, and its own **bare** comment carrying no `FROM:` line. Bounded and small in practice — the coordination protocol mandates `FROM:` on every comment, so a conformant own post still names its author and is still suppressed — and it is **not** a loop: a coordination intent produces a `channel_push`, a wake, never a write (`CoordinationClassifier` is `InboxOnly`; the writeback path is a different classifier and untouched). An install that finds it noisy has the honest lever: name yourself in what you post.
- **(d) Why NOT a config knob.** A `coord_echo_input: actor|union` flag would ship both behaviours forever and make every operator adjudicate a question they have no evidence to answer — and one of the two settings is the defect. The pre-DL-253 behaviour is not a preference somebody might reasonably hold; it drops other people's mail. Deciding is the fix (canon #3: a new need gets a dedicated path, but a *wrong* behaviour gets removed, not made optional).
- **(e) The test debt this closes, and it is the more general lesson.** Every assertion that a coordination event WAKES an agent had stopped at the `ClassifyResult` — including DL-235's own grant test, which passed on the day it shipped while the dispatcher dropped the very event it certified. **A grant asserted at the classifier is not evidence of delivery; only dispatch can witness delivery.** Three end-to-end tests now drive the real `CoordinationClassifier` through `DispatchService` under a shared identity and assert the dispatch OUTCOME plus the wake actually leaving the box. Standing rule: a wake/grant claim gets a `DispatchServiceTest` counterpart, not only a classifier unit.
- **(f) The doc siblings — the shipped guides taught the defect to anyone writing a classifier.** `docs/customization.md` and `docs/multi-agent.md` both told a classifier author to "recover the true **author**" and return it, and customization.md's bullet went further, citing this repo's own union as a deliberate pattern to copy. That is canon #5's shape one level up: the primitive was fixed here, but the instruction to re-mint it shipped in two guides. Both now state the contract as *this agent performed this event*, with the explicit "return null when you cannot evidence the actor". `docs/consumer-guide.md` § Echo-suppression semantics gains the bound its flat claim — *consumers will never see the agent's own writes* — no longer supports under a shared identity.
- **(g) Not fixed, carried forward unchanged: the two `FROM:`-line parses in one classifier** (DL-252 (h)). Untouched by this change and still divergent; this entry neither discharges nor worsens it.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) keep the union and special-case bodyless actions — rejected: that is the union defended by a branch, and the bare-comment sibling would still drop. (b) Null `reattributedActor` outright for the coord classifier — rejected: it discards genuine own-write suppression (b), and DL-005's own-write drop is load-bearing. (c) Gate on `wake_membership` membership so only `bare_reply_to_own_thread` events escape the echo check — rejected: it makes an attribution question depend on a recipient-gate setting, coupling two unrelated axes, and leaves bodyless actions dropped. (d) A config knob — (d) above.

**Consumer/operator impact — DELIVERED VOLUME GOES UP, and the discriminator is one grep.** A channel is affected iff it **inherits the `wake_membership` default** AND **opens its own threads**; a channel that sets `wake_membership` explicitly cannot be reached by this (an explicit key is a named mechanism, not an absence of symptoms). Measured on the reporting operator's install: 2 PM channels explicitly configured → unaffected; 3 impl seats inheriting the default → affected; 5 utility channels inherit but open no threads → no population. That install audited its own state/design docs for any baseline keyed on delivered comment volume and found **none**, so the volume-anomaly risk is zero *there* — not generalised to other installs. Notice was given to aimla-pm on roundtable #209 before this shipped, on the same terms as the `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` agreement (card#5734).

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no exit-code change, no token-scope change, no correlation change, and no wire-shape change** — `Intent`, `payload`, and `docs/event-schema.json` are untouched; this changes only WHICH events are dispatched, never how one reads.

**Tests — 4 new + 2 rewritten; every one watched fail.** The two DL-252 pins that existed to make this change loud (`test_echo_input_still_carries_the_thread_author_*`) did exactly their job — they went red on the first run — and are rewritten to pin the new contract rather than deleted. The two delivery tests were watched RED against the pre-change classifier (`'delivered'` vs actual `'dropped'`, the defect printed verbatim). The three **preservation** tests are green under revert by construction — they assert a NON-change — so they were proven failable by a named mutation instead (`reattributedActor: null`), which reds all three, restored byte-identically after. **Whole suite 1890/1890 (5584 assertions), phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs.php` clean.** Card#5738; roundtable #209; supersedes DL-252 (f) (that entry stays as written — the log is append-only).

## DL-254 — A stat that could not SEE is not a stat that found nothing: the absence guard is hoisted out of one class and adopted where the two worlds actually differ

**Context — one class, ten-plus members, and the guard that already solved it had been sitting private in one file since DL-230.** `is_dir()` and `is_file()` return false for `EACCES` exactly as they do for `ENOENT`. A leg that reads that bare `false` as ABSENCE states a definite fact about the install on evidence that cannot tell the fact apart from its own blindness — and then hands out the remediation for the wrong world: *"run bridge:provision"* for a secret already provisioned, *"Repoint channel.socket"* for a correct config, *"place a least-privilege token"* for a token already placed. This is routine rather than exotic: the bridge commonly runs as a different OS user than the agent (DL-227's same-box topology), and an agent's own directories are commonly `0700`. `ChannelSnapshotProbe` reasoned this through for the snapshot legs and built `visibleOrUnverified()` — then kept it **private**, so nothing else adopted it and every new stat re-minted the defect. That is canon #5 read backwards: not N call sites needing one fix, but one fix that never reached its N call sites. Filed as the class item **card#5698**.

**Decision — hoist the guard to `App\Bridge\Support\PathVisibility` and adopt it at the sites where the two worlds lead to DIFFERENT consequences; correct the claim, not the severity, where they do not.**

- **(a) The discriminator, and it is not "is the message wrong".** Every member's message was wrong. What decides the fix is whether *absent* and *could-not-see* imply the same thing for THIS RUN. Where they diverge, the leg did not answer its own question and reports `unvalidated` (the `Severity` rule's limb 2 — a capability **this process** lacks). Where they converge, the verdict is earned in both worlds and only the CLAIM gets fixed. Applying one blanket rewrite to all members — which is what the card originally prescribed — would have been wrong twice, in opposite directions.
- **(b) Five adopters, and one of them moved an exit code.** `ChannelSnapshotProbe` (2 populations, now a consumer of the guard it authored), `ChannelTransportCheck`, `WritebackAlertChannelCheck`, `AgentWebhookSecretCheck`, `WritebackTokenCheck` — all previously `warn`. The consequential one is **`BoardToolAgentResolver`**, previously `fail`: `bridge:check` runs as the operator, while the resolver that actually serves board tools is built by `AgentToolsController` as the **web** user and may read the token fine. That `fail` therefore convicted a healthy install of a missing bearer *and flipped the exit code* — a claim about a runtime the checking process never observed.
- **(c) `InstallConfigDirCheck` KEEPS its `fail`, and this is the interesting negative.** It looks like the most severe member — an unreadable ancestor turning into a non-zero exit — and the reflex fix is to downgrade it. That would have been canon #3: loosening a check to make a failure go away. `CheckCommand` gates its entire agent loop on the **same** `is_dir()`, so in both worlds this run loaded no agent config and every per-agent leg below it is MISSING rather than clean. That is a fact about the RUN, known with certainty, so the exit is earned. Only the message was wrong, and it now names both causes plus the run's own degradation. **Verified at the source before deciding, not assumed** — had the loop reported its own failure independently, the answer would have been the opposite.
- **(d) `AgentApiTokenCheck` was never a member.** The card listed it; reading it settled otherwise. Its message says *"API token not readable at …"*, which is TRUE under `EACCES` and `ENOENT` alike — a claim its evidence supports. Removed from the class with the reasoning recorded, rather than "fixed" into a change with no defect behind it.
- **(e) The board-tools problem list carries `Finding`s now, which restores a discrimination DL-251 removed — without reopening it.** card#5292 deleted a `type` tag from `BoardToolAgentResolver::problems()` because it was written at three sites and read at zero, and left the explicit invitation *"restore it if and when a caller genuinely needs to discriminate"*. One now does. **DL-251's ruling is untouched:** it settled `bearer_unreadable` vs `collision` — two MEASURED faults that both still `fail`. What is new is a THIRD situation that ruling never covered, where the build could not measure at all. **[DL-262 adds a FOURTH on the same ground and, in doing so, SPLITS the `bearer_unreadable` label this sentence treats as atomic:** a bearer that is present and unreadable by this process is `unvalidated`, not `fail`. The perms half is what still carries the measured `fail`.**]** Carrying the severity itself (rather than a tag the consumer must interpret) is also strictly better than what was removed.
- **(f) What the hoist COST, disclosed rather than discovered later.** `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` pins where the severity is CONSTRUCTED; centralising construction collapsed five call sites into one entry, so a check **dropping** its guard and going back to asserting absence now moves no number there — the exact regression this class exists to prevent. A second pin, `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest`, counts adopters over comment-stripped source and closes it. Its own bound is stated in its docblock and is real: **it cannot see a NEW stat that never adopted the guard.** No test can; that judgment is prose in `PathVisibility`.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) share only the predicate and let each site write its own message — rejected: seven spellings of one concept is the drift the class documents. (b) Downgrade every member to `unvalidated` uniformly — rejected by (c). (c) A per-stat guard everywhere including paths that cannot be affected — rejected: canon #6, and `ChannelSnapshotProbe`'s existing comment already bounds where its gate applies and why one deliberately-unguarded stat stays unguarded.

**Consumer/operator impact — one exit-code change, in the safe direction, on one install shape.** An install where `bridge:check` cannot traverse to a board-tools bearer previously exited non-zero and now does not; that install was being told something false. No other severity moves. Two operator-facing messages change wording (`InstallConfigDirCheck`, and the six guarded legs' not-visible text). `message` strings are explicitly not part of the `--format=json` contract (`docs/check-json-contract.md`), and `schema` stays **1**.

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, no wire-shape change.**

**Tests — 11 new across 4 files; every not-visible arm watched RED against the pre-change tree.** `app/` was reverted to `HEAD` with the new tests in place and all five `cannot_be_SEEN` arms failed, then restored and re-verified green — the arms measure the fix, not themselves. `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest` was proven failable by dropping a real guard (it named the exact file), restored byte-identically. `WritebackTokenCheck` had **no test file at all** and gained one covering all four arms, not just the one this change touched. One golden fixture moved (`config-dir-missing`), one line, `exit: 1` preserved — and the harness's own subject guard caught that the fixture had drifted off the string it is named for, which is why the subject map moved with it. Card#5698 (class item — **still open**; this closes its stat-conflation sub-shape only).

## DL-255 — An agent the run could not READ is not an agent that is not THERE: the three scope maps get one coverage fact, and the legs that read them stop accusing through it

**Context — one root cause, four consumers, and a defect that gets WORSE the more agents an install runs.** `CheckCommand::handle()`'s per-agent loop derives three maps onto `CheckContext` — `writebackEmittingScopes` (which github scopes have a writeback-emitting classifier), `coordCardMoveScopes` (which enable the coord-card-move family) and `githubScopeConsumers` (which classifiers consume which event types). All three are accumulated **inside** that loop and **after** both of its aborts: a `catch` on `AgentConfig::load`, and the classifier-resolution gate. So an agent whose YAML did not parse, or whose classifier did not resolve, is in none of them — and every consumer reads "this scope is absent from the map" as "the operator did not enable it". The operator is then told to *add an agent* for an agent they already have, or to *edit a families list* that may already be correct in the config that failed to load, while a line further up already named the real fault. This is the same shape as DL-254 one layer in: a definite claim resting on evidence that cannot distinguish the fact from the run's own blindness. Filed on the class item **card#5698**, which named this root cause explicitly and named the fix as ONE fact rather than N call-site patches (canon #5).

**Decision — record `CheckContext::$agentScopeCoverage`: which agents were not read to completion, and which github scopes each is KNOWN to subscribe to; every leg reading a map NEGATIVE consults it first.**

- **(a) The ledger stores a SCOPE SET, not a count — and that is the whole design, not an optimisation.** The two aborts know different amounts. A config-load abort knows only a filename, so *which* scopes that agent covers is itself unknown and every scope is in doubt (`scopes: null`). A classifier-gate abort happens with `$cfg` already parsed, so its github subscriptions are a real answer and an unrelated mapping's finding must survive it **untouched**. A bare abort count — the obvious implementation — would have softened every writeback finding on the install for one broken YAML, which is a second false claim replacing the first. `scopes: []` (a kanban-only agent) is kept distinct from `null` for the same reason: it rules that agent out of every github scope rather than shrugging.
- **(b) Three legs disclose; a fourth stops skipping in silence.** The orphaned-mapping accusation and the coord-card-move family gate in the direction that ACCUSES (`WritebackMappingConfigCheck`), and the dropped-arrival warn (`EventFollowsConsumerCheck`), all report `unvalidated` naming the unread agent instead of the claim. The fourth is `WritebackBoardStateCheck`'s gate on the **DL-200 coord-terminal preflight** — the read that makes it legitimate for the bridge to own a terminal stage id at all, and which that check's own docblock calls MANDATORY with a binding condition that a missing input must never read as agreement. An unread agent made that gate false and skipped the preflight silently; it now says so, and only where the compare would otherwise have run (the two inner conditions mirror `coordTerminalAgreement()`'s own early return).
- **(c) ONE map-fed arm deliberately gets NO disclosure, and the omission is a ruling.** `WritebackMappingConfigCheck`'s `family-on, terminal-missing` warn is the only one of the four that asserts **nothing** when the scope is absent: it is scoped to family-enabled scopes precisely so a pure PR-writeback mapping stays quiet. An unread agent therefore costs it no false claim — only the same silence it already keeps for every install that does not use coord cards — while a disclosure there would print on EVERY mapping of every run with an unreadable agent config, including the majority carrying no coord-card config at all. That is the silent-LEG class DL-251 stage 10 handled, whose members had answering siblings; this arm has none.
- **(d) The asymmetry that bounds the event-consumer disclosure.** An unread consumer can only ADD to a scope's `consumed` set, never remove from it. So an EMPTY `unconsumed` is sound whether or not the roster is complete, and only a non-empty one is unprovable. The check discloses on the warn path only, which is why a healthy-but-incomplete run does not grow a line per scope.
- **(e) It cannot move an exit code, by construction rather than by care.** Both abort sites set `$ok = false` *before* recording coverage, so a run with an incomplete roster has already failed; and `unvalidated` never flips the exit in the first place. There is no install shape where this disclosure is the difference between 0 and non-zero — which is what makes an operator-facing output change on the always-failing path a safe one.
- **(f) The JSON document carries the fact at TOP LEVEL, not under `event_consumers`.** The gap is about the run, and it short-changes three maps of which the document exposes one. `agent_scope_coverage.{complete, unread_agents[]}` is what lets a machine consumer reach the same conclusion the prose legs reached without parsing messages — `event_consumers.scopes[].unconsumed` being the one derived value it can inflate. `schema` stays **1** on two independently sufficient grounds: an added key is not a bump, and the three severity re-assignments are exactly the precision correction §4 of `docs/check-json-contract.md` pre-disclosed (that row names card#5698 by number).

**Alternatives considered:** (a) Guard each call site locally against a "did anything abort" boolean — rejected: it is the N-patches shape the card names, and it loses (a)'s precision. (b) Hoist the `coordCardMoveScopes` derivation ABOVE the classifier abort, since it is a raw-config family test that needs no classifier — genuinely appealing, and it would shrink how often coverage is short, but it changes what that map MEANS for an agent that cannot classify at all, and it does nothing for the config-load abort. Recorded on `CheckContext` as a finding and left for its own item rather than smuggled in here. (c) Suppress the affected findings entirely instead of disclosing — rejected: silence is what the `unvalidated` vocabulary exists to replace.

**Consumer/operator impact — additive on the JSON side; on the text side, three findings change severity and wording, and one previously-silent skip starts printing. All four are reachable only on a run that is already exiting non-zero.**

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, no exit-code change.**

**Tests — 8 new for the ledger, 3 for the event-consumer arms, 2 JSON-contract cases, and 2 golden fixtures, because the corpus could not witness any of this.** Not one of the 33 existing golden files combined an aborted agent with a writeback mapping, so all four call sites were invisible to it — `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrote every fixture and **zero** existing captures moved, which is the measurement that says so. `writeback-move-leg-agent-unread` fires all three disclosures at the real command surface; `writeback-orphan-survives-unrelated-unread-agent` is the precision control, where the abort must be REACHED and the ORPHANED accusation must SURVIVE it — both halves are declared subjects, because either alone passes under a wrong ledger. Card#5698 (class item — **still open**; this closes its three-maps root cause only, and corrects two of its own filings: the swallowed-throw member is NOT map-fed, and neither are two of its four round-3 members).

## DL-256 — An empty list and an absent one are different answers: `KanbanClient`'s collection projections stop manufacturing "not there" out of "could not read"

**Context — the parser, not the endpoint, was the liar, and that is what makes this fixable at one place.** `KanbanClient::idList()` reduced a decoded kanban collection to `list<int>`, mapping a **non-array** input to the same `[]` it produces for a genuinely empty list. Three public reads project through it — `findCardsByRef`, `cardsByTag`, `boardSwimlaneIds` — and `boardCustomFieldKeys` does the same thing one type over, for `key` strings. `->json('data.swimlanes')` returns `null` for an absent key exactly as `->json()` returns `null` for a body that is not the promised shape, so four `bridge:check` legs were issuing definite config verdicts — *"swimlane_id 4 not found on board 8 (a deleted lane, or a lane on a different board)"*, *"board 8 is MISSING the custom field(s) …"* — whose only evidence was this run's inability to parse the response. Filed on the class item **card#5698**, whose `idList()` slice named the primitive, the four routing methods, and `WritebackByRefCheck`'s `byRefAvailable()` registration preflight as the in-tree precedent for the fix shape.

**Decision — `idList()` (and `boardCustomFieldKeys()`, on the same rule) returns `null` when the decoded value is not a collection at all, and every caller decides explicitly what that means for it.**

- **(a) `[]` deliberately stays a real answer, and this is the measurement that forced the design.** Read live against the three production boards before writing any code, `preload.json` answers `data.swimlanes: []` — key present, list empty — on **all three**. Empty is therefore the *ordinary* state of every board this fleet runs, and the naive reading of the card ("an empty lane list means we could not see") would have printed a cannot-verify line on every healthy install while fixing nothing. The distinction that carries the class is **present-and-empty vs. absent**, which is narrower than the card claimed and is the only one the evidence supports.
- **(b) The two RUNTIME callers keep degrading to a no-op — but stop doing it silently.** `findCardsByRef` / `cardsByTag` still answer `[]`, because a throw on a deterministic body would retry-storm an unfixable event for ~11 days (the DL-020 anti-pattern) and both contracts already make an empty result a graceful no-op. What changes is that the degradation is now logged at the shared choke point, which is exactly the DL-026 treatment `correlationCards` already applies to the board scan: *"the endpoint answered a body with no card collection"* and *"no card matched"* are different facts, and only the first is a bug to chase. **No request-path behaviour moves.**
- **(c) Three `bridge:check` legs move `warn` → `unvalidated`; the fail-closed one stays `fail`.** The two swimlane lookups and the dependabot custom-field lookup did not answer their own question — limb (c) of the `Severity` rule, the unresolved comparand being the board's own lane / field list. The `issue_population=all` `issue_number` leg does **not** move: an unverifiable board could silently double-card, so cannot-verify is still a failure there. Its message alone was wrong. This is DL-254's `InstallConfigDirCheck` ruling applied again — fix the claim, keep the earned exit code — and downgrading it to match its three siblings would have been canon #3, loosening a check to make a failure go away.
- **(d) The exit code cannot move anywhere in this change, by construction rather than by care.** `unvalidated` never flips the exit; and on the one `fail` leg, a null read already reached the `! in_array` arm and failed there, so the outcome is identical in both worlds. The test that pins it asserts the **message** changed while the severity did **not**, which is the assertion that actually distinguishes the two.
- **(e) Partiality is deliberately NOT represented, and the bound is stated in the primitive.** A row the projection skips is not reflected in the return: the question answered is *"did the response carry a collection"*, never *"was it complete"*. Signalling completeness would have to either withhold the ids that did parse — breaking the two correlation callers, whose whole job is to use them — or add a third state no caller has a use for. A kanban row always carries its primary key.
- **(f) One unreachable guard was removed rather than shipped.** The board-tools leg first grew a `configuredLanes !== []` arm; `BoardToolsConfig` requires `swimlane_id` for an enabled block and the two constructions that leave it null also null `boardId`, which the check's own guard already returns on. The arm could not fire for any loadable config, so it is gone and the reason is a comment.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) Return a small result object separating `empty` from `unreadable` — rejected as more mechanism than two states need, and it would have rippled a new type through two request-path callers for a diagnostic-only benefit. (b) Guard at the four check call sites and leave the primitive alone — rejected outright: that is the N-patches shape card#5698 exists to stop, and it leaves the fifth caller to re-mint the defect. (c) Make the runtime callers throw on an unreadable body — rejected under DL-020: a deterministic 5xx is a retry storm, and the log makes the condition visible without one.

**Consumer/operator impact — text side only: three findings change severity and wording, one `fail` keeps its severity and changes its diagnosis, and two runtime log lines are new. No JSON `schema` bump (no key added or removed).**

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, no exit-code change.**

**Tests — 6 new client cases, 5 new check cases, and 1 golden fixture, plus a corrected call-site tripwire.** The corpus could not witness this class either: `moveLegInstall`'s preload already omits `data.swimlanes`, but its mapping declares no `swimlane_id`, so the leg that would have lied never ran — the same blindness DL-255 recorded. `writeback-swimlane-collection-absent` is the witness, and it declares **both** the disclosure that must appear and the accusation that must not, because pinning only the first stays green if the fix regresses into printing both. Every leg was driven RED before being trusted: collapsing `null` back into `[]` takes exactly the three severity assertions, the one message assertion, and the golden fixture red, and no others. `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest`'s pinned set moved 8 → 10 and 2 → 3, updated deliberately with the fourth member's absence from it recorded as a ruling. Card#5698 (class item — **still open**; this closes its `idList()` slice only).

## DL-257 — A classifier the run could not ASK is not a classifier that declares nothing: the consumed-events catch gets a third state and stops asserting through it

**Context — the `catch` arm was the whole defect, and it was one assignment.** `CheckCommand`'s per-agent loop probes whether an agent's classifier implements `DeclaresConsumedEvents` (out of process, DL-025) and then asks the resolved instance what it consumes. That call is wrapped in `catch (Throwable)`, which wrote `$declares = false` — **the same value a classifier that does not implement the interface gets**. So *"it declares, and this run could not ask it"* and *"it does not declare"* were one state, and two definite claims followed from it: `EventFollowsConsumerCheck::undeclaredDisclosure()` told the operator the classifier **does not declare its consumed events** (false — the out-of-process probe had just said it does), and the emptied `consumed` made `EventConsumerScope::unconsumed()` over-inclusive, so the **silently dropped on arrival** warn could accuse a scope whose arrivals that very classifier consumes. Filed on the class item **card#5698** as the swallowed-throw half of its partial-map pair, and explicitly NOT closed by DL-255 — the coverage ledger that fixed the map-fed half cannot reach a throw inside the derivation.

**Decision — `declared` becomes `?bool`, with `null` written ONLY in the `catch`, and every consumer decides explicitly what it means.**

- **(a) The third state, not a widened guard.** `null` routes to a new `EventConsumerScope::$unreadable` bucket, keyed `class|agent` exactly as `undeclared` is; `false` still routes to `undeclared`, unchanged. `EventConsumerReconciler::declarations()` tests `=== null` FIRST and separately, because the `! $c['declared']` it used to run is true for both values — that identity IS the defect. Same shape as DL-255's null scope set and DL-256's null id list, and the third time this repo has answered "could not read" with a third state rather than a sentinel.
- **(b) The dominant reachable throw is `consumedEventTypes()`, and the fixture had to prove it.** `ClassifierResolver::for()`'s three throws are pre-validated by `probeLoadable` in `AgentClassifierResolvableCheck` (same three failure modes), so the arm that actually survives is the call INTO classifier code — a custom impl that throws on a malformed config key, or any impl breaking the interface's pure-map contract. `tests/Fixtures/UnreadableDeclarationClassifier` does exactly that. The existing `ThrowingClassifier` was the wrong witness: it throws from `classify()`, which `bridge:check` never calls.
- **(c) Path (C) is deliberately untouched and stays `false`.** `probeImplements` true + `for()` OK + the instance nonetheless not `instanceof` is a MEASURED in-process fact (the bare probe process and the booted one disagreed), not an inability to measure. Only the `catch` arm moved.
- **(d) The disclosure is a `warn` and the verdict is `unvalidated`, and the split is the point.** *The declaration could not be read* is measured — the run caught the throw — and it is the operator's actual defect, so it warns and names the classifier and the pure-map contract. *Whether these arrivals are dropped* is what could not be measured, so the unconsumed lines collapse into one `unvalidated` finding, mirroring the `agentScopeCoverage->mayCover()` arm directly above it, which is the same treatment for the same reason. The asymmetry that bounds this to the warn path is that arm's too: an unread declaration can only ADD to `consumed`, so an EMPTY `unconsumed` stays sound and stays silent.
- **(e) The action-inventory caveat had to be EXTENDED or this change would have silently deleted it.** That caveat was gated on `undeclared !== []`, and a throwing classifier used to be IN `undeclared` — so moving it out drops a line that used to print, invisible to every test (the finding is `ok`, so no severity assertion sees it) and to the golden corpus (no fixture reached it). It now carries a SECOND clause in its own wording rather than widening the first, because calling a classifier that does declare "undeclared" would re-mint this card's defect at the caveat. **That preserves reach and adjudicates nothing:** whether an `ok` finding may carry a could-not-measure disclosure at all is card#5698's own 41-fail / 32-ok severity audit, which the card says must not be shipped one site at a time.
- **(f) `--format=json` gains `event_consumers.scopes[].unreadable`; `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1.** An added key is deliberately not a bump (the const's own docblock), and the contract doc now tells a consumer to read this alongside `agent_scope_coverage.complete` before trusting `unconsumed` — both bound it the same way and in the same direction.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) Keep per-type warns and merely re-word them — rejected: the count/last-seen sentence's whole claim is that nothing consumes the type, which is precisely what this run cannot say; re-wording it would have kept a definite verdict at `warn` severity. (b) Fold `unreadable` into `undeclared` and disclose in prose only — rejected: the JSON surface exists so consumers stop parsing prose, and a machine reading `undeclared` would inherit the exact conflation. (c) Emit the throwing-classifier warn unconditionally, even when nothing is unconsumed — rejected as scope creep beyond the correction: the empty-`unconsumed` case is genuinely robust here (see (d)), so an unconditional line would be a new capability, not a false claim removed.

**Consumer/operator impact — text side only, plus one additive JSON key. No exit-code change:** the lines that moved were `warn`, the lines replacing them are `warn` + `unvalidated`, and neither flips the exit (`emitFinding()` returns false only for `fail`).

**No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.**

**Tests — 4 new unit cases, 1 new feature case through the command, 1 new golden fixture, 1 new test classifier, plus the pinned `Finding::unvalidated(` count 2 → 3.** The command-level case is the one that exercises the `catch` that mints the state at all — every unit test around it builds `CheckContext::$githubScopeConsumers` by hand — and it was watched go RED against the reverted `$declares = false` before being trusted. The golden fixture is the DISCRIMINATING PAIR for `event-consumer-unconsumed-type`: same scope, same arrival, same unconsumed type, differing only in whether the declaration could be read. **No existing golden file changed**, which is the evidence that the tri-state is inert on every install shape the corpus already covers. Card#5698 (class item — **still open**; this closes its swallowed-throw slice only: the bundled-cause catch, the PATH-proxy leg, the two `WritebackBoardStateCheck` round-3 members and the 41/32 severity audit remain).

## DL-258 — A board this token cannot SEE is not a board whose cards are all fine: the source-coverage all-clear stops being minted out of an empty read

**Context — the first `Finding::ok` site the stage-10 bound reserved, and it was a live defect, not untidiness.** DL-251 (stage 10) swept the legs that REPORT `warn` on a failed measurement and disclosed a population it did not reach: its **32 `Finding::ok` construction sites were never audited** against the severity rule. `WritebackSourceCoverageCheck` is the first of them read, and it fails the rule outright. `KanbanClient::readBoardCards()` returns `cards: []` with `truncated: false` for a `200` carrying no rows — **exactly what a token whose user is not a member of the board receives**. With no cards the per-card loop never runs, `$flagged` stays `0`, `truncated` is false, and the leg certified **green**: *"writeback: dl_number cards on board N all have a mapped source (self-move-eligible)"*. It examined nothing and reported a pass. `Severity::Ok`'s own docblock states the invariant this breaks in the vocabulary itself — Ok *"MUST NEVER carry a not-measured finding"* — and it is the precise failure (green-because-never-looked) the whole DL-242 programme exists to kill, surviving at an `ok` site because every sweep to date was keyed on `warn`. Filed as card#5701, and deliberately NOT filed inside the class item card#5698: canon #18 keeps a live correctness defect out of a consolidation bundle, where it would inherit the bundle's priority and go quiet.

**The tell was that one run contradicted itself.** On a blind token `WritebackBoardStateCheck`'s DL-029 probe prints *"writeback: token sees 0 cards on board N — EITHER the board is empty … OR the token's user isn't a member …"* in the **same output** as this green line. One leg disclosed that the population was unknown; its neighbour certified it clean.

**Decision — the leg WITHHOLDS the all-clear on an empty read, because nothing available to it can disambiguate one.**

- **(a) Withhold, do not re-measure.** No second read buys discrimination: `visibility()` reports `total === 0` for both worlds and its own comment documents that ambiguity; `byRefAvailable()` folds *"board isn't accessible to the token"* together with *"this kanban predates by-ref"* into one `false`, and probes only the FIRST mapped board while this leg walks all of them. So the honest severity is `unvalidated` — the leg did not answer its own question — and a `Finding::ok` there would be unsupported in every world consistent with the evidence.
- **(b) The discriminator is the EMPTY READ, never "no DL cards found".** A board whose cards were all read and none of which carry a `dl_number` **was measured**: the population is known and the claim over it is true, so it keeps its `ok`. Keying the new branch on the DL count instead would print a cannot-verify line on every healthy board that simply has no DL cards yet. `test_a_card_with_no_dl_number_is_not_examined` pins that direction and reds if the predicate is keyed wrong.
- **(c) Ordering is unchanged and the truncation leg still wins.** `truncated` is tested first; a truncated read is non-empty in every non-pathological case, and where both hold the more specific cause is the right one to name. Both are `unvalidated`, so no verdict is lost either way.
- **(d) This is NOT in tension with DL-256, though the two rulings point opposite ways on the word "empty".** There, an empty `data.swimlanes` was a REAL answer — measured present-and-empty on all three production boards — and only an ABSENT collection was could-not-see, because the payload carried the distinction. Here it carries none: a member's empty board and a non-member's invisible board produce byte-identical rows. **Empty is an answer only when the response can still say which empty it is.** That sentence is the rule the two decisions share.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) Consult `visibility()` from this leg and green only when `total > 0` — rejected: `total === 0` is ambiguous for the same reason the card read is, so it swaps one unsupported claim for another while adding a network round-trip per board. (b) Hoist the DL-029 0-card signal onto `CheckContext` and gate on it — rejected for this slice: it shares a fact that *is itself ambiguous*, so it cannot license the `ok` either; the sharing is worth doing only if some future probe can actually distinguish membership, and building the plumbing now would imply a discrimination that does not exist. (c) Leave `ok` and append a caveat to it — rejected: that is the shape card#5698 reserves for its 41-fail / 32-ok audit, and it would keep a green line as the operator's headline for a board nobody looked at.

**Consumer/operator impact — text side only. No exit-code change:** the line that moved was `ok`, the line replacing it is `unvalidated`, and neither flips the exit (`emitFinding()` returns false only for `fail`). No JSON key added or removed; `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1. **No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.**

**Tests — 1 new unit case carrying its control in the same run, plus the pinned `Finding::unvalidated(` count 2 → 3 for this file.** The golden corpus **cannot witness this leg at all** — every fixture holding a writeback client runs `scan` correlation and the check is a no-op outside `ref` — which was re-verified here by a positive-controlled grep rather than taken from the existing docblock: the leg's messages appear in **zero** fixtures while `writeback` appears in many. So the witness is a unit test faking **two boards behind one stub in one loop** (one read empty, one not), which makes the control structural rather than a second scenario: a check that had simply stopped emitting `ok` would fail the control half. Mutation-proven — reverting the branch to the pre-fix fall-through reds exactly that test and nothing else, and the file was restored byte-identically (`cmp`). **No golden file changed.**

**Correction to DL-257's closing line, recorded here rather than by editing an append-only entry.** That line says the class's remaining members include *"the two `WritebackBoardStateCheck` round-3 members"*. They were already closed by **DL-256**, which landed in the commit immediately preceding it — so the claim was wrong when written, not merely stale. `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`'s parallel copy carried the same error and is corrected in this change. **Root cause, and the reason this correction is not just a re-sync:** the class's open list is RESTATED in three places (card#5698, the plan doc's per-slice `Still open on the class` lines, and each DL's closing sentence) while only the card owns it, and it has now drifted in both directions — the card was missing DL-257 entirely, and the two doc copies were wrong about DL-256. Retiring those restatements in favour of a pointer to card#5698 is filed on that card; this change adds no fourth copy, pointing instead.


## DL-259 — A green line may disclose what a fact implies, but never that it could not look: the reserved `fail`/`ok` severity audit, run whole

**Context — the last population stage 10 disclosed and did not sweep.** DL-251 settled the `warn` ↔ `unvalidated` boundary and said so explicitly: it swept only legs that already REPORTED `warn` on a failed measurement, leaving the `fail` and `ok` construction sites unaudited against its own rule. card#5698 held that as its standing bound, and required it be run **whole** — the card is explicit that shipping it site-by-site is how the class re-minted itself in the first place. Populations re-derived live rather than recalled: **45 `fail` · 33 `ok`**, up from the 41/32 the card recorded, because DL-254…258 added sites. All 78 were read against the rule.

**Result first: the rule needed no amendment. It needed two corollaries written down**, because both were already being decided ad hoc in per-site prose, in two directions, with each site arguing a general principle that contradicted its sibling's. They now live in `Severity`'s docblock, which owns the vocabulary and is the only place they belong:

- **(A) An `ok` may disclose ambiguity about what a measured fact IMPLIES, but never its own blindness.** The discriminator is the same one the "world-ambiguity is not measurement-ambiguity" clause already draws, applied to a finding that has concluded: doubt about the CONSEQUENCE of a measurement keeps the finding and carries a disclosure; doubt about whether the measurement HAPPENED is limb (a) and takes the whole finding to `unvalidated`. **A disclosure therefore splits by its CAUSE, never by its presence** — which is what stops the corollary from degenerating into "any caveat ⇒ unvalidated".
- **(B) A vacuous universal claim is SILENT when its emptiness is the operator's own config, and `ok` when only this run's measurement could establish it.** Who else holds the fact is the discriminator.

**Corollary (B) closed a live divergence and deliberately changed NO behaviour.** `WritebackBoardStateCheck`'s mapped-stage-ids leg falls silent when the mapping targets no stage ("silence is the honest answer for a vacuous question"); `WritebackSourceCoverageCheck` emits `ok` when it read the board and found nothing to flag ("the witness that the check read the board"). Both are correct: the first empty set is the operator's own `writeback.json`, which they can read and which no line would inform them about; the second is a fact only the read establishes, and its `ok` is load-bearing precisely because the empty READ beside it is `unvalidated` (DL-258). Recording the discriminator was the entire fix. **Changing either site to match the other would have destroyed a correct output** — the temptation to make an audit look productive by converging two sites is exactly what canon #3 warns about.

**Four sites disagreed with the rule, and only two moved severity. That split is the main result.**

- `EventFollowsConsumerCheck::actionInventory()` — rendered **green** while appending *"a classifier … did not answer what it consumes … (possible false inventory)"*. The inventory may list actions that ARE consumed, and the finding said so in an `ok`. Now `unvalidated` when the run could not obtain a declaration — by EITHER shortener: a classifier that was asked and threw (DL-257), or an agent this run never finished reading (DL-255). **Fixing only the first would have been a half-fix at one site, not a smaller scope:** `unlistedActions()` reads `consumed`/`bare`/`qualified` unioned across the scope's consumers, so an unread agent can make an action look unlisted, and a BARE declaration from it would have removed the whole type. The class docblock had deferred exactly that gating to this audit, and the audit is what discharges it. The `undeclared` caveat on the same line **keeps its `ok`** and is the control — an `instanceof` returning false is a measured in-process fact (DL-257's own ruling), so only its consequence is open. This is also the first site converted **out of** `ok` by corollary (A), and the code comment that deferred the question here ("adjudicates nothing … the audit … must not be shipped one site at a time") is discharged.
- `SharedIdentitiesCheck` — certified `0 shared account(s)` in green for a file it **could not read** and for one that **is not JSON**. `AgentRegistry::loadSharedIdentities()` is fail-soft **by design** (its other caller is the runtime, which must not 5xx over a bad optional file) and answers `[]` for all three states, so the count alone could never carry the signal the check's own docblock claimed it carried. The primitive keeps its contract; the discrimination moves to the check, where a verdict is pronounced. Unreadable ⇒ `unvalidated` (nothing measured); malformed ⇒ **`warn`**, not `unvalidated` — those bytes WERE read, so it is a measured fault, and a real one: the loader ignores the file and every agent sharing an account loses attribution silently.
- `SshTransportProbe` — hard-failed *"board_tools.ssh_account 'X' does not resolve to an OS account on this host"* whenever `homeForUser()` returned `''`, which `SystemSshProbeEnvironment` also returns when **`posix_getpwnam` does not exist**. On any PHP build without the `posix` extension (optional, and commonly absent or disabled on hardened/shared hosts — this codebase already guards `posix_getuid` with `function_exists` for the same reason) that convicted a perfectly valid account and flipped the exit. **Fixed at the primitive, not the call site** (canon #5): `SshProbeEnvironment::homeForUser()` is now `?string`, with `null` = this process cannot look accounts up and `''` = the database answered and has no such account. The no-such-account arm **keeps its `fail`**.
- `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheck` — accused *"no bearer at <path> — run bridge:provision-tools"* off `SecretFile::read()` ⇒ `TokenFile::readTrimmed()` ⇒ `! is_file()`, false for EACCES exactly as for ENOENT. A missed member of DL-254's stat-conflation sweep, reading the **same file** its sibling `BoardToolAgentResolver` guards. **Keeps its `fail`; only the claim changed.**

**Why two of the four keep an exit-code-bearing `fail` — the `InstallConfigDirCheck` precedent, applied twice.** DL-254 kept that check's `fail` because `CheckCommand` gates its whole agent loop on the same `is_dir()`, so in BOTH worlds THIS RUN certainly loaded no agent config — a fact about the run, known with certainty, so the exit code is earned and only the message was wrong. The same test decides both here. The board-tools probe asserts about **its own certification**, which the operator explicitly requested with `--probe-tools`: absent or unseeable, this probe presented no bearer and certified nothing. The ssh no-such-account arm likewise blocks certification on a measured answer. **This is where the audit differs from `BoardToolAgentResolver`, which DID downgrade** (DL-254): that finding asserts about the RUNTIME's enablement while running as the wrong OS user, so an unseeable token makes its claim false rather than merely unhelpful. Subject, not shape, decides. **The audit moved a severity only where the run had genuinely measured nothing.**

**Also corrected, because encountering a false claim makes it yours (canon #16).** `Severity`'s docblock cited `EventFollowsConsumerCheck` advising off a swallowed throw as a LIVE example of a leg that fails to notice it did not measure — **DL-257 closed that** by giving the derivation a third state, two slices before this one. The example was stale in the doc that owns the rule.

**Consumer/operator impact — text and severity only. No exit code moved in either direction.** The two `fail`s that stayed `fail` changed message only; the sites that moved went `ok` → `unvalidated`/`warn`, and neither flips the exit (`emitFinding()` returns false only for `fail`). The one **new** `warn` (malformed shared-identities.json) replaces a green line on an install that was already broken. No JSON key added or removed; `SCHEMA_VERSION` **stays 1**, on the contract's pre-disclosed-precision row. **No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.**

**Tests — 5 new cases, every one watched go RED against the un-fixed code before being trusted, plus the `Finding::unvalidated(` construction-site pin updated deliberately at 3 files.** `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` fired exactly as designed and is the reason the pin is a tripwire rather than a formality. One existing test was **re-pinned rather than worked around**: `test_the_inventory_caveat_survives_the_move_of_a_throwing_classifier_out_of_undeclared` asserted `Severity::Ok` for the pre-adjudication state the code itself flagged as undecided — this is the adjudication, so the assertion moves and the test keeps its original regression guarantee (the caveat must still print). A control case was added beside it so "any caveat ⇒ unvalidated" cannot pass. **The golden corpus witnessed none of this** — no fixture carries an unreadable shared-identities file, a posix-less host, or an unreadable declaration alongside an unlisted action — so **all 33 fixtures are unchanged**, which is the evidence the re-assignments are inert on every install shape the corpus covers, and equally the reason each arm needed its own mutation-proven unit test. 1951/1951 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs.php` clean.

**Doc-sync, including a retirement this change owed rather than deferred.** `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`'s three `Still open on the class` enumerations are **retired** here in favour of a pointer to card#5698, which owns that list. They were filed for retirement on the card by DL-258, and this change is what forced it: closing the audit invalidates all three the moment it lands, so re-syncing a third copy would have been the defect (canon #16 — delete the restatement, point at the owner). What each slice CLOSED stays; only the forward-looking copies go. The `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md` copies are left alone — this log is append-only, so a later DL corrects an earlier one in place of an edit. `docs/config-schema.md`'s `ssh_account` row and `docs/check-json-contract.md`'s schema-stability paragraph updated in lockstep.

**Two findings surfaced by this audit and deliberately NOT fixed here (canon #6), filed rather than folded.** `DirectoryPermissions::warnIfInsecure()` returns `null` — indistinguishable from "secure" — when `fileperms()` cannot stat the directory, which is reachable via `InstallSecretDirCheck` (it never existence-checks the dir), so an absent or unseeable `BRIDGE_SECRET_DIR` prints a green line and a silent perms leg. That is the **silent-leg** class (DL-251 stage 10, card#5291), not this one, and its `ok` is NOT a member here — the `ok` claims only that the value is a configured absolute path, a claim its evidence supports, which is the same test that ruled `AgentApiTokenCheck` out of the class in DL-254. Separately, `CheckCommand`'s per-agent not-run REASON says the config dir *"is not a directory"* on the same EACCES/ENOENT conflation, but it rides the disposition axis, not the severity vocabulary this audit bounds. **[card#6025:** there is no `DirectoryPermissions::warnIfInsecure()` in the tree today — the entry records the code as it stood.**]**

## DL-260 — A token this process cannot read is not a token the receiver cannot read: the channel-token catch stops convicting the push on a proxy read

**Card:** #5698 (sub-shape 2 of the class — the bundled-cause catch) · **PR:** #460

**Context.** `ChannelTokenPathCheck` did the real read — deliberately, so a preflight could not drift from `ChannelToken::read`'s contract — and reported whatever it threw as one `warn` ending *"channel_push will FAIL until fixed"*. One `catch`, three causes, one verdict. Two of those causes earn that verdict and one does not, and the difference is not which rule broke but **who the broken rule is broken for**: `bridge:check` reads the token as the operator, while `channel_push` and `WritebackAlertNotifier` read it inside the receiver request as the OS user the receiver runs as. A group/world-readable mode and a blank file are the same for every reader. A file this process cannot read is not.

**Decision — the causes are kept apart at the THROW site, not re-derived at the consumer.** `ChannelTokenException` now carries a `ChannelTokenFault`, decided inside `ChannelToken::read` off the same stat that failed. Five cases, split on one question — is the fault uid-independent?

- **`Missing` / `InsecurePerms` / `EmptyFile` keep the `warn` and the definite verdict.** The receiver hits each of them identically.
- **`NotReadable`** (a regular file is there, this process cannot read it) and **`NotVisible`** (a directory above it denies this process traversal) report **`unvalidated`** and make no claim about the push. Limb (b) of the rule in `Severity` — the measurement completed, but on the wrong subject.

**The three-way split of the first gate is the part that keeps the check useful, and it is why this is not simply "downgrade the unreadable arm".** Collapsing all of `! is_file($path) || ! is_readable($path)` into `unvalidated` would have stopped warning on a **genuinely absent** token — overwhelmingly the real case, and one this process CAN establish whenever it can traverse to the path. Trading a false accusation for a false silence is not a fix. So `unreadableFault()` asks traversability FIRST (without it `is_file()` cannot answer at all and its `false` would read as an absence never established), then splits on `is_file()`: present ⇒ `NotReadable`, absent ⇒ `Missing`.

**Why the classification lives in the primitive.** A check re-deriving it from the path afterwards would be a second copy of `ChannelToken`'s rules — the copy this leg's design notes were explicit about not creating — and it would stat a file that can change between the read and the re-derivation, so the two copies could disagree about one throw.

**The exception MESSAGES are deliberately unsplit, and the runtime is byte-identical.** At runtime the reader IS the subject, so *"channel auth token not readable at &lt;path&gt;"* is true and useful on all three paths of the first gate; only the proxy reader needs the split, and it takes it from the enum rather than from prose. `ChannelPushHandler` and `WritebackAlertNotifier` are untouched.

**`PathVisibility` gains a second door rather than a paraphrase.** `notVisibleFinding()` is the message without the stat, for a caller whose failed read already established non-visibility. Re-statting through `unverifiedUnlessVisible()` was the alternative and it would measure a second time. `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest` now counts **both** doors and says why: the pin is about the verdict, not the stat, and counting only the statting door would have let this adopter drop its guard — and go back to convicting the push off a read made as the wrong OS user — without moving a number anywhere.

**Tests — both new arms watched go RED against the un-fixed code before being trusted.** Killing the traversability gate reds the two `NotVisible` cases; collapsing `NotReadable` into `Missing` reds the two `NotReadable` cases. `ChannelToken`'s five faults are asserted separately, because a test asserting merely "it threw" passes against the bundled shape this replaced. Both construction-site pins updated deliberately (`UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` +1 at the check; `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest` +1 through the message door). **No golden fixture reaches any of this** — every fixture that declares a `token_path` writes a readable 0600 file — so all 33 captures are unchanged and each arm carries its own mutation-proven unit test. **No exit code moves in either direction**; `--format=json` is untouched; schema stays 1. 1959/1959 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean.

**A sibling audit finding, filed rather than folded (canon #7/#18) — card#5778.** Auditing the same shape across the other secret readers found a live defect that is NOT a member of card#5698's class: `SecretFile::read()` delegates to `TokenFile::readTrimmed()`, which gates on `! is_file` and then calls `file_get_contents` with no `is_readable` check, so a present-but-unreadable secret raises an **undocumented `ErrorException`** — measured live, with `is_file` true, `is_readable` false and `isInsecure` false, i.e. both pre-gates a caller would use pass. Four of its seven call sites do not handle it (`AgentToolsController` returns 500 where its own comment says the caller must never be able to distinguish that case from a 401; `CheckCommand`'s unwrapped resolver construction aborts `bridge:check` on a healthy install), and the three that do each invented a separate workaround. `ChannelToken` is the only reader that pre-checks `is_readable`, which is why this change is unaffected by it. One card, not two: the live defect and the divergent workarounds share one root and one fix.

## DL-261 — A php-fpm binary this process cannot find is not a receiver without `fastcgi_finish_request()`: the retention preflight stops convicting an install on a PATH read

**Card:** #5698 (sub-shape 3 of the class — the PATH-proxy; **the last member, so the class closes here**) · **PR:** #461

**Context.** `RetentionPostureCheck` closed with a definite claim — *"retention: this PHP install has no `fastcgi_finish_request()`"* — and prescribed the cure for it (*"Serve the receiver under PHP-FPM"*). The evidence behind it was `ExecutableFinder->find('php-fpm…')`, which asks one question and it is not that one: **is a php-fpm binary findable on the PATH THIS process sees.** `bridge:check` is a console command, and the CLI SAPI never defines `fastcgi_finish_request()` regardless of how the receiver is served, so the function-existence limb can never carry the answer either. The subject that matters is the **receiver's** process, and this command never runs as it — the same discriminator DL-260 applied to the channel token and DL-254 to the board-tools resolver.

**It is false on a healthy install, and that was measured rather than argued.** The reference host keeps `/usr/sbin/php-fpm8.5` and serves the receiver under Apache + PHP-FPM. Run from a login shell whose PATH includes `/usr/sbin`, the leg is silent. Run from one without it — an ordinary non-root PATH on several distributions — the same box, same install, same healthy receiver produces the definite claim and tells the operator to adopt the thing they are already using.

**The method's own docblock had been describing a probe that does not exist.** It said php-fpm ships the function iff the FPM SAPI is built, *"so probe the fpm binary's own module list"*. No module list has ever been read — by that method or any other. **DL-199 carried the same inversion** (*"`bridge:check` now warns, probing the receiver's SAPI rather than the CLI's"*), which is corrected in place at that entry rather than left to be re-read as history. Two independent restatements of a capability the code never had is the shape canon #16 exists for, and it is why the method is **renamed** — `receiverSapiFinishesEarly()` → `earlyFinishIndicated()` — rather than merely re-commented: the old name asserted the answer in every call site and every doc that pointed at it.

**Decision — the leg reports `unvalidated` and narrows the claim to what was actually read.** It now says it could NOT determine whether the receiver ends the request early, names both reasons (this process is CLI; no php-fpm binary was findable on the PATH it sees), states outright that *a healthy FPM install can keep the binary in `/usr/sbin`, off a non-root PATH*, and **keeps the whole operator consequence and remedy** — the latency degradation is still described, and the two cures are still offered, now conditioned on *"if the receiver is NOT served under PHP-FPM"*. Limb (b) of the rule in `Severity`: the measurement completed, on the wrong subject.

**Why the sibling state stays SILENT and did not become an `ok`.** Finding a binary does not establish the receiver's SAPI any more than missing one refutes it — the proxy is weak in both directions, since the receiver may be served by mod_php, or by a different PHP install, on a box that has the binary. A green *"retention: the receiver finishes early"* would therefore be a line that measured nothing, which is exactly what corollary (A) forbids. Emitting `unvalidated` on **both** states was considered and rejected for the opposite reason: it would print a permanent disclosure on every run of every install, including the majority where nothing is suspected, and a signal that fires unconditionally carries no information. So the leg raises the possibility only where the cheap indicator is absent, and the severity says the possibility is unconfirmed.

**The `function_exists()` limb is KEPT although it is unreachable today, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight.** Every caller is `bridge:check`, so it is dead. It is also the only limb whose subject is correct — the process asking is the process answering — so a check ever run inside the receiver's own SAPI is answered rightly by it and wrongly by the other. Deleting it would remove the one correct measurement in the method and leave only the proxy.

**The root-cause alternative is NAMED AND NOT BUILT.** The only process that can answer this authoritatively is the receiver, and it already writes to the cache: `RetentionGate` could record `function_exists('fastcgi_finish_request')` from inside the request and let the preflight read a fact measured by the subject. It is not built here because it does not fit the leg's job — the marker exists only **after** a webhook has arrived and a pass has run, so on a fresh install (precisely when a preflight is read) it is absent, and DL-199 wanted a preflight line rather than a post-hoc one. Recorded on card#5698 as the standing option if the disclosure ever proves insufficient.

**Tests — the severity assertion was watched go RED against the un-fixed code before being trusted.** It reds with exactly `Warn` vs `Unvalidated` and greens with the fix. This mattered more than usual here: **the golden corpus pins this leg's line on 34 of 37 fixtures, and a golden capture is plain text**, so it witnesses no severity at all — `warn` and `unvalidated` differ only in the renderer's colour and the closing tally. Without a severity assertion the leg could be flipped back to convicting the receiver and every golden file would stay byte-identical. The tally **does** move (each affected fixture's `unvalidated` count goes up by one), which is the corpus's only view of the change and is now a second, independent witness. Its discriminating control — a findable stub binary leaves the leg silent — guards the opposite failure, an unconditional disclosure. `minimal` / `minimal-fpm-present` remain the pin-potency pair; that test is re-pointed at the new text **and** now asserts the retired claim appears in neither half, which is the assertion that would catch the old wording surviving a partial regen. `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` fired as designed and its `RetentionPostureCheck` entry is deliberately raised 1 → 2.

**No exit code moves, in either direction, by construction** — `emitFinding()` returns false only for `fail`, and this leg has never emitted one. `--format=json` `schema` stays **1** (`message` strings are explicitly not part of that contract, and no key is added). No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change; the receiver runtime is untouched.

**Doc-sync.** `RetentionGate`'s environment-constraints docblock said *"`bridge:check` warns"* and now records that it cannot and never could. `PinnedHost`'s pin-1 description and its `$fpmPresent` param both described the PATH read as *"whether the receiver's SAPI can finish early"* — the same conflation, in the harness that exists to control it. `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` referenced the old method name in five places including two mutation lists; all are re-pointed, with the rename noted once at the stage-2 result so the history stays readable. `docs/check-golden-coverage.md` needs no regen — it is bounded to `handle()` predicates and this leg migrated out at stage 2.

## DL-262 — A secret this process cannot READ is not a secret that is absent: `SecretFile::read`'s undocumented third outcome becomes part of the contract

**Card:** #5778 · **PR:** #462

**Context.** `SecretFile::read()`'s docblock named exactly two outcomes — *"null when the file is absent or blank … throws `InsecureSecretPermsException` when it is present but group/world-readable"*. There was a third. It delegates to `TokenFile::readTrimmed()`, which gates on `! is_file()` and then calls `file_get_contents()` with nothing between the two: on a file that is PRESENT and unreadable by this process, the early return never fires and the read's warning becomes an uncaught `ErrorException`. Four of the primitive's seven callers never expected it.

**Measured on the real surface, and the first attempt to measure it was itself the trap.** Bootstrapped against a present `0600` file owned by another OS user: `is_file` true · `is_readable` false · `SecretFile::isInsecure` **false** · `read()` throws `ErrorException`. Both pre-gates a caller would reasonably reach for PASS in that state, so guarding with them is no protection. **`tinker` is not a valid harness for this and would have disproved the card:** psysh installs its own error handler, so the same call returns `null` there. One input, two contradictory outcomes decided by ambient state — which is a second defect hiding inside the first, and is why the fix does not depend on any handler.

**Why the state is ordinary rather than exotic.** It is the topology `PathVisibility` and DL-227 already describe: the bridge runs as a different OS user than the agent, and a `0600` secret owned by the other user is exactly what correct provisioning produces. `bridge:check` reads these files as the OPERATOR; the receiver reads them as the web user.

**The blast radius, and the split IS the diagnosis (canon #5).** Three callers had each independently invented a private `catch (Throwable)` for a behaviour the primitive never documented; four had not. The two unhandled sites that matter: `BoardToolAgentResolver` is constructed by `AgentToolsController` with no wrapper, so `POST /agent-tools/call` answered **500** — breaking that controller's own stated contract, written eight lines below the construction: *"Do not distinguish 'unknown token' from 'collided/unreadable token' to the caller."* A 500 tells an **unauthenticated** caller that another agent's bearer file exists and is unreadable, which is precisely the distinction the design refuses to draw, on the one door reachable with no credential. And `CheckCommand:498` builds the same resolver ABOVE the third fail-soft envelope, so a **healthy** install — bearer readable by the web user that actually serves board tools — aborted `bridge:check` when the operator ran it.

**Decision — one primitive change, not seven guards.** `TokenFile::readTrimmed()` classifies the failed open itself and throws `UnreadableSecretException`; `SecretFile::read()` documents all three outcomes. **The authority is the open's own return value, not `is_readable()`** — that predicate answers for the real uid (wrong under setuid) and cannot see an ACL or a filesystem that refuses the open, so it both misses failures and invites the caller to read its `false` as absence. The warning suppression is load-bearing rather than hygiene: it is what makes the outcome a **type** instead of the ambient handler's choice.

**The obvious cheap fix was rejected as the defect itself.** An `is_readable()` gate returning `null` would have made every symptom disappear in one line — and it converts an unreadable secret into a confident *"no secret here"*, which is card#5698's assert-absence-off-a-permission-denial defect minted into the primitive every secret reader shares. The point is to make the third state REACH the caller, not to hide it.

**Per-caller dispositions, decided on one question: is the read that failed the read that matters?** `BoardToolAgentResolver` → **`unvalidated`**, not `fail`: it is built both by `bridge:check` as the operator and by the controller as the web user, so a mode that stopped one is no evidence about the other — the same ground as its not-visible arm (DL-254) and as DL-260's channel-token split. This **narrows** DL-222's *"an unreadable bearer FAILs"* and DL-251(e)'s *"`bearer_unreadable` … still FAILs"*: the perms half stays a measured `fail`, the uid-relative half does not. `WritebackClientFactory` → `ConfigException`, the channel its callers and its own docblock already promise. `bridge:provision` / `bridge:provision-tools` → **`fail`**, and the asymmetry is the point: those commands act AS the operator and present the token themselves, so there the failed read IS the read that matters.

**Caller-facing effect.** `POST /agent-tools/call` returns **401** where it returned 500 — a refusal that no longer discloses anything, restoring the controller's stated contract. `bridge:check` completes instead of aborting, reporting `unvalidated`. **No exit code moves in the fixed direction:** `unvalidated` never flips it, and the run that previously ABORTED had no exit contract at all.

**Two consumers found by the self-review, after the falsification run rather than before it.** (1) `ChannelToken::read` pre-gates on `is_readable()` and then calls the same primitive — but that predicate is a PREDICTION and the open is the measurement, so they can disagree (an ACL, a network filesystem, `is_readable`'s real-vs-effective-uid split under setuid, or an unlink in the window). The new type would then have escaped a method whose every caller is written against `ChannelTokenException`; it is now mapped onto `ChannelTokenFault::NotReadable`, which already existed for exactly this state (DL-260). **This arm is NOT covered by a test and that is a real gap, not an oversight:** reaching it requires making `is_readable()` lie, which this suite cannot do deterministically. It is not a regression — the same state escaped as an `ErrorException` before — and it is recorded here rather than left to look covered. (2) `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheck` caught `Throwable` into a message ending *"(chmod 600)"*. That remedy is right for the perms fault it was written for and **wrong** for this one, where the mode is already correct and the fault is ownership — it would send the operator to loosen permissions on a healthy bearer. Split into its own arm, `fail` preserved.

**Tests — every new assertion was watched go RED against the un-fixed code before being trusted.** Six of them, each failing for the right reason: the door test returned **500** with a stack trace through `AgentToolsController:41 → readToken → SecretFile::read → TokenFile → HandleExceptions`, and the rest surfaced the raw `ErrorException`. Each unreadable-state test carries a **skip-if-still-readable** guard rather than a silent pass, because root reads through mode bits and a test that cannot fail must not report as one. Discriminating controls pair every new arm — a genuinely absent bearer still `fail`s, an absent writeback token keeps its own distinct message — so the change cannot be satisfied by collapsing states onto one answer (canon #3). `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` fired as designed; its `BoardToolAgentResolver` entry is deliberately added.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — the shape is NOT confined to this primitive, and the rest is filed, not folded.** *(Corrected by DL-263: the class has **five** members, not four. `BridgePaths::readJsonl` uses `file()` instead of `file_get_contents()`, so the grep behind this list could not reach it — it was found by re-reading the subsystem while landing the consolidation.)* Four more reads use the same `is_file()`-gate-then-unguarded-read shape and were measured to throw `ErrorException` on a present-but-unreadable file: `BridgePaths::readSeen` (docblock: *"missing/garbage → []"*), `AgentRegistry::loadSharedIdentities` (**fail-soft by design** — its own recorded reason is that the runtime *"must not 5xx over a bad optional file"*, and `SharedIdentitiesCheck` already models this exact state as `unvalidated`, so the check and the loader it certifies disagree), `WritebackConfig::load` (on the receiver's dispatch path, and it already has a typed channel it does not use here), and `WebhookProvisioner`'s reconcile read (caught, but rendered as *"API error"* — a local permission fault attributed to the upstream). **Filed as ONE class card (#5789), not four, and deliberately not fixed here:** folding a four-site consolidation into this PR would bundle a live correctness defect with it, where canon #18 says it goes quiet.

**Doc-sync.** `WritebackClientFactory`'s docblock claimed it throws `ConfigException` on an *insecure* token; it never did (that is `InsecureSecretPermsException`, DL-010) — corrected, since this change adds a third channel and would have compounded a false claim. `BoardToolAgentResolver`'s `problems` list is re-grouped by the question the severity actually splits on. `docs/config-schema.md`'s board-tools bearer row named only ONE `unvalidated` case; it now names both, matching the channel-token row two sections above, which DL-260 had already brought to that shape. `docs/board-tools.md`'s 401 row records the indistinguishability as the deliberate property it is. `ProvisionCommand`'s null arm said *"token unreadable"* — the wrong half of the split even before this change, and provably so after it.
