**Decision 2 — the near-miss id comes from the EXISTING probe, as a capturing sibling; never a fourth pattern.** `NearMissProbe::id()` captures the digit run `matches()` already had to match, and `matches()` is now DERIVED from it (`id($text) !== null`), so the two cannot disagree about what a near-miss is. `CardTokenGrammar::nearMissCardId()` binds it to the card stem beside `looksLikeCardToken()`. DL-239(h) / DL-250(1) stand: the near-miss SET is unchanged, and a fourth hand-written regex was the alternative that mints the drift those entries exist to remove.

**Decision 3 — an unreadable token that names one of the DL's own cards is REDUNDANT, not a refusal.** This is the leg that separates the shipped rule from "refuse on the bare shape" (candidate B, rejected): B refuses on SPELLING, so a prose-ish `card_4811` mention in a title would block an otherwise-correct DL move **even where it names the DL's own card**, and recovery would need `bridge:replay` (a title edit re-fires nothing). The redundant arm logs `info` and lets the DL win, mirroring the agreeing-arm precedent the parsed token already had. Everything else — a differing id, or an id the probe cannot pin to a resolved card — refuses. **What the redundant arm rescues is bounded, and stating it as "the leg that keeps ordinary prose citations working" OVERSTATES the separation from B:** it keeps a prose citation of **the DL's own card** working, and nothing wider. A near-miss-spelled citation of a DIFFERENT card — the ordinary "see also `card_4811`" in a title whose DL resolves elsewhere — is refused by the SHIPPED rule too, identically to B, so B's own cost statement above (`bridge:replay` is the recovery; a title edit re-fires nothing) applies unchanged to the shipped rule for that input class. The two rules differ over WHICH citations survive, not over whether prose citations survive at all; the shipped one is narrower than B by exactly the redundant set.

**Decision 4 — the refusal is HANDLER plumbing over the classifier's predicate, so it ALERTS.** The classifier emits its move target(s) carrying `card_token_near_miss: true` and `KanbanMoveCardHandler` refuses them through `WritebackAlertNotifier::warnAndNotify` — the one primitive every permanent refusal uses (DL-274 / DL-285). Dropping the target at classify time was the alternative and was rejected on exactly that ground: it would be a third **log-only** refusal branch, the shape DL-274 spent a card removing. The gate sits before the client is built — a refused move needs no card read, and a missing/insecure token must not 5xx-retry an event that is permanently refused. It carries no stamp refs: a refused move writes nothing at all.

**Decision 5 — HARD BOUND, written into the code: the recovered id may REFUSE or WARN, never SELECT.** It is read only as a member test against ids the DL resolved on its own. The precedent is `refCorroborates` / DL-270(b'): corroboration is deliberately wider than selection, and a bare id can confirm a token but never produce one. Same rule here — otherwise every spelling the grammar rejects becomes a correlation channel through the back door, which is what `CardTokenGrammar::PATTERN` decides against. The redundancy arm is written as the narrow POSITIVE test, so anything the probe cannot pin to a resolved card lands on the refusing side rather than the permissive one.

**OPERATOR GATE — the refuse half was APPROVED (2026-08-13), asked before any code was written.** Refusing changes what the bridge accepts, so it is a hard gate (canon #14). The ask carried the blast radius below and a recommendation to approve; the ruling approved refusing a move when a DL resolves beside an UNREADABLE card token naming a different card. The warn half needed no gate and would have shipped either way.

**BLAST RADIUS — 0 of 1,118 historical PRs, measured through the shipped grammars via the dev autoloader (never a re-implemented regex), with a positive control.** 520 PRs on this repo + 598 on the kanban repo: card-shaped-but-unparsed = **0**, so this refuses nothing that has ever happened here. Control: 3 synthetic rows including the repro were all caught while the historical count stayed 0, so the instrument could see one. **Bounds, stated rather than left implied:** "a DL RESOLVES" was approximated by "a DL PARSES" (an upper bound, and it measured 0, so it is exact); deleted branch names are un-enumerable, so the push surface is only partially covered (9 live branches, 0 hits); and only the 2 writeback-mapped repos were measured.

**STATED BOUNDS — recorded, deliberately not "fixed".** (a) A malformed TITLE token beside a PARSING BRANCH token stays invisible: the branch is authoritative (DL-270), so the question of which card is named is already settled and a misspelling beside it changes nothing. (b) A pure-overlay event (`converted_to_draft` / `ready_for_review`) inherits the refusal through the shared predicate, with **no** diagnostic — the same no-double-log split DL-218 made for its own conflict, on the lower-harm surface that ruling was about. **It suppresses BOTH directions, and the one-directional wording this bound originally carried ("no `block_reason` lands on the DL's card") hid the second:** `correlatedCardIds()` returns `ids: []` for `ready_for_review` exactly as for `converted_to_draft`, so a marker SET under an earlier title is also never CLEARED. Reachable, on a `draft_overlay` mapping: a PR opened-as-draft titled `DL-9 fix` sets `PR is in draft` on the DL's card; the title is then edited to `DL-9 fix (card_4811)`; `ready_for_review` now reads NearMissRefusal and emits no overlay target, so the card keeps the marker for as long as that title stands. The residual is not inert — `PinGuard::isPinned()` reads a non-empty `block_reason` as a human pin, so a later `started` promotion of that card is refused (loudly, `pinned_no_automove`) on a pin the PR left behind; the refusal is signalled, its cause is not. **Disclosed, not fixed:** giving the overlay a diagnostic here re-opens the DL-218 double-log ruling, and the harm is a stale marker rather than a wrong write. (c) The digit class stays ASCII (DL-231 is not reopened); a Unicode-digit near-miss is invisible to the probe and covered by name in the CI PR-title lint. (d) The design's "or no recoverable id" arm was **not built**: with the capturing sibling, a probe match implies a captured digit run, so an unreadable-token-with-no-id state is unreachable and a branch for it would be defending against a state that cannot happen (canon #6). The refusing side is the negation of the redundancy test, so if that ever became reachable it would refuse, not select. (e) **The BARE-SPACE spelling is a live residual of exactly the harm this entry closes, one separator away from the shipped repro.** `NearMissProbe::SEPARATORS` excludes `' '` deliberately — DL-201 ruled prose ("supports card 2") warns nowhere and DL-250(6) recorded that ruling ON the data so no later stem could widen into it — so for `Guard against DL-9 (card 4811)` on head `fix/4811-guard` the probe answers null: `token=null`, `nearMissId=null`, verdict `DlWins`, and DL-9's card moves and is stamped with this PR's refs with no warning of any kind, which is the defect at the top of this entry with a space where the underscore was. Measured through the shipped grammars rather than inferred (`CardTokenGrammar::parse()` and `nearMissCardId()` both return null on that subject; the `card_4811` spelling recovers `4811` as the positive control). It is left open because closing it means adding the bare space to the ONE shared separator list, which reopens DL-201/DL-250(6) for every stem and widens the warn surface far beyond anything this card measured — a ruling-level change, not a bound this entry may take. `docs/writeback.md` discloses the bare-space near-miss silence where the near-miss set is written for operators; this bound is what that silence now costs at the DL-win sites.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — one open instance of the same shape, NOT fixed here, because closing it is a separate gate.** The shape is *"a card-shaped token that does not parse is invisible to the guard that would have used it."* Re-read rather than grepped: a malformed token in the **head branch** beside a **parsing title** token — `Fix card#5287` on `fix/card_4811-slug` — is the reverse of bound (a) and is NOT covered. The authoritative surface is the unreadable one there, and the title's card is selected (marked uncorroborated, so DL-270's handler gate is the only thing between it and a move). Refusing it would be a NEW validation change beyond the approved gate, and its shape is not the one that was measured, so it is disclosed here and reported to the card rather than widened in silently.

**Adjacent honesty fix, shipped with this.** The FR-7 **no-move** arms (a DL that resolves to nothing with no `card#` fallback, on both the move and push paths) now call `warnTokenNearMiss()`. Nothing moves on those arms, so the near-miss line's own "no move" clause is TRUE about them — which is the DL-234(e) whole-subject condition, satisfied, not widened. To make that safe the probe helper now asks each grammar's `parse()` before probing its stem: at the both-null call site that is implied by the caller's guard (byte-identical answer), and at the new call sites it is what keeps the line from telling an operator that a DL which parsed does not parse.

**Tests — every leg was watched fail, and each states HOW.** **10 new legs:** 7 in `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` (the repro end-to-end with a TOTAL-warning-count assert; the push mirror through the shared predicate; the redundant arm on each surface — `info`, no warning, no flag; the pure-overlay inheritance; and both no-move arms) and 3 in `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` (refused before any read; the refusal ALERTS with `reason=card_token_near_miss`; and an unflagged target unaffected). **8 were written first and observed red against the unfixed code**, each on the defect's own signature — `Undefined array key "card_token_near_miss"`, the DL's card emitted clean, the missing `info`, `Requests were recorded`. The other **2 were green when written and were made to fail by mutation instead**, which is the same evidence obtained the other way round and is stated rather than glossed: the push-surface redundant leg (its arm removed ⇒ red) and the unflagged-target negative control (the gate made unconditional ⇒ red). **11 mutations, each applied singly and restored by `cp`+`cmp` (never `git checkout --`), measured over the subset that can see them** (`tests/Feature/{Classifiers,Handlers,Support,Writeback,Workflows}` — 796/796 green as the control): the recovered id SELECTS the card ⇒ **10 red**, including DL-250's grammar-driven corpus leg (`'card4' must not correlate`) — the hard bound is enforced by the suite, not by this prose; the predicate reads unreadable as absent again (the shipped defect) ⇒ 4 red; the push consumer left unfixed ⇒ 1 red; the overlay consumer left unfixed ⇒ 1 red; the handler ignoring the flag ⇒ 2 red; refuse on the bare SHAPE (candidate B) ⇒ 1 red — the redundant arm, which is exactly the leg that should object; each no-move probe removed ⇒ 1 red each; the push redundant arm removed ⇒ 1 red; dropping the per-stem `parse()` check ⇒ 3 red, one of them the DL-corpus leg's exact warning COUNT; and the refusal gate made unconditional ⇒ **58 red**, the negative control among them. **Pins re-run and green:** the DL-234(e) whole-subject suppression, the DL-201/DL-250(6) prose silence (`card 2` warns nowhere), the DL-218 conflict legs' single warning, the overlay silence legs, and `PrTitleLintTest` (untouched — no grammar and no lint changed). **2223/2223 phpunit (6819 assertions)** — 2213 before, +10 — phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs` clean.

**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Writeback/CardTokenVerdict.php`; `NearMissProbe` (capturing sibling, `matches()` derived from it); `CardTokenGrammar` (`nearMissCardId()`); `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` (three-state resolution, the verdict predicate at all three consumers, the refusal warning + flag, the honest no-move arms, the per-stem probe guard); `KanbanMoveCardHandler` (the `card_token_near_miss` refusal arm); `docs/writeback.md`; `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **No config key, no migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change** — the only behaviour change is that a move which today happens onto the wrong card is refused and alerted. Card #6027; DL-218, DL-231, DL-234, DL-250, DL-270, DL-273, DL-274, DL-285.

## DL-288 — the changelog gate's CI half takes composer.json, composer.lock and .env.example; the npm pair beside them is DISCLOSED, not inherited (card#6137)

- **Date:** 2026-08-17
- **Status:** implemented (card#6137). **Extends DL-280/DL-282; supersedes neither.** The CI-half criterion at `changelog-gate.yml` — *what CI ACCEPTS OR REJECTS, which is shipped behaviour for a contributor* — is unchanged; what changes is which files are measured against it. **No claim of criterion-completeness is made here either**, and DL-282's withdrawal of that claim stands.

**What DL-282 left, and why it could not stay.** It recorded three files as DISCLOSED ACCEPTED GAPS rather than verified exclusions, because their real mechanisms were named rather than denied. One of the two reasons offered for `composer.json` — *"no CI step runs a composer script"* — was **already withdrawn as false in the same commit that shipped the entry**; that half was never in force. The surviving reason — *a dependency change alters the subject under test rather than the gate's own rule* — is not an application of the criterion but a proposed **amendment** to it, and the operator ruled against the amendment: `composer.json:14-23` pins `larastan/larastan`, `laravel/pint` and `phpunit/phpunit`, which ARE the analysers `laravel-tests.yml` runs, and `composer.json:9`'s platform constraint fails `composer install` outright. A change to those changes what CI accepts, directly and by four independent mechanisms.

**Decision 1 — three members join the anchored group; the branch exemption is untouched.** `composer.json`, `composer.lock`, `.env.example`, anchored `^…$` like every other root-file member. `changelog-gate.yml`'s `dependabot/*|release/*|sync/*|revert-*` exemption is deliberately not touched and is what keeps the cost at one PR shape.

**BLAST RADIUS — one commit in 125, re-derived independently by the reviewer rather than trusted.** Over `v0.70.0..dev` (125 first-parent): `composer.json` **0** commits, `.env.example` **0**, `composer.lock` **12**, of which **11** are `dependabot[bot]` on `dependabot/*` branches and therefore already exempt. The single human-authored one is `a864bd9` — a `league/commonmark` **GHSA** bump touching `composer.lock` and nothing else, with no card/DL token in its title and no `docs/CHANGELOG.md` change — i.e. the one PR this catches is a security bump that shipped undocumented. A premise the measurement silently rests on was checked separately: `.github/dependabot.yml` sets no `pull-request-branch-name` prefix override, so all 11 really are on `dependabot/*`. Independently confirmed: **0 of those 11 touches `docs/CHANGELOG.md`**, which is why the branch exemption is load-bearing rather than incidental — that fact is now pinned by a test instead of living in prose.

**⛔ Decision 2 — the npm manifest pair is recorded as a NEWLY DISCLOSED CI-half gap, in this same change, and is NOT inherited from DL-282.** `examples/channel-servers/package.json` and `examples/channel-servers/package-lock.json` meet the CI-half criterion on the identical mechanism used to justify `composer.lock`: `channel-server-supply-chain.yml:66` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (failing the PR on manifest/lock drift), `:72` runs `npm audit --audit-level=high` reading the lockfile as **that gate's own rule input**, `:102`/`:108` run a version-bump guard reading the `version` field of **both** files and failing on disagreement, and `provision-tools-python.yml:88` runs a second `npm ci` against the same lockfile.

⚠ **This is the defect shape DL-282 itself named** — *"fixing 2 of 5 IS the guard-reads-a-proper-subset defect shape … re-minted one directory down"* — and without this disclosure the change would have discharged a card-owned gap list while the repo demonstrably knew of another gap, leaving the CI half's recorded gap set empty and false. **The exposure is not theoretical and this repo has already measured it:** `.github/dependabot.yml`'s header records that security updates are disabled here, that **17 of 19 lifetime alerts (89%) were npm on that exact lockfile**, and that the surviving path is *"anything urgent is hand-cut as a PR to `dev`"* — a human, hand-cut, lockfile-only security bump on a non-exempt branch, which is `a864bd9`'s shape exactly, one directory over.

⭐ **Recorded because it is the more useful lesson: DL-282 HAD the evidence and used it in the other direction.** Its *Verified exclusions* paragraph disposes of the ROOT `package.json` with *"the two `npm ci` steps run with `working-directory: examples/channel-servers`, against that directory's own manifest, not the root one."* The sentence is still literally true and is annotated rather than contradicted — but it points straight at the nested pair and never turns the question around on it. **An exclusion argument that names the file it is not about is where the next gap hides.** Widening to reach the pair is a separate operator ruling and is deliberately NOT taken here.

**Controls — four, each observed RED, each restored by snapshot + `cmp`, never `git checkout --`.** Dropping `composer.lock` from `VERSIONING.md`'s scope row → 38/39 naming it (the one that mattered: the round's own rewording of that cell could have broken the leg's field extraction and made it vacuous — it did not, the failure message shows the cell isolated at 317 chars). Deleting the `composer.lock` row from the `PATH SCOPE` table → 38/39. Moving `pint.json` into the prefix alternation, and `bin/` into the anchored alternation → each reds the new regime assertion. ⚠ **A fifth attempt silently DID NOT APPLY and the suite came back green at 39/39** — caught by the harness's per-replacement applied-check, not by the result. A mutation that does not apply reports as a passing control; only the applied-check separates the two.

**Decision 3 — the scope's two-regime invariant is now DERIVED, not counted.** The surfaces previously carried the numeral *"seven root files"*, the only scope fact `test_every_scope_enumeration_is_derived_from_the_predicate` did not cover — a future widening would have left it false at green, and this change had to hand-edit it. Both surfaces now state the **rule** (every prefix-group member ends in `/`, every anchored-group member does not), and the derivation leg asserts it (+11 assertions, so provably non-vacuous), pinning the invariant DL-282 Decision 2 rests on and nothing previously covered.

**Log annotations — three, all ADDITIVE, zero words removed (`git diff --word-diff` verified).** Appended to DL-282's *surviving argument* paragraph (scoped to the whole DISCLOSED ACCEPTED GAPS block: records the discharge, withdraws the surviving argument, carries the npm gap forward), a standalone supersession line after the fenced predicate literal (which deliberately does NOT restate the current predicate — a fifth hand-maintained copy is the defect DL-282 closed), and a count-only supersession on *Decision 2 — the four root files*. ⚠ **Correction to the precedent as it was briefed:** two of the three prior annotations (DL-280 *Stated bound*, DL-281 *Consequences*) close with the frozen-original formula attributed to DL-277; the third (DL-276 Decision 4) carries no such formula and states the opposite — that rewriting in place was *"a convention set HERE, not one this log already had."* All three blocks here are original prose and take the additive form.

**Tests — one stale pointer repaired by re-pointing, per DL-276 Decision 4.** DL-282's *Controls* paragraph names `dl282InScopeMemberProvider` and *"5 of 8, as fixture paths"*. That provider is renamed `rootCiConfigMemberProvider` (ruling-specific names go stale, which is the reason for the rename) and the figures are now **8 of 11**. Recorded here rather than as a fourth annotation.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **The rename escape is still open and untouched:** the gate reads `git diff --name-only`, so its verdict depends on git's rename detection — a file moved into or out of an in-scope path can be recorded as delete+add. Real, on this same card, deliberately out of scope. (b) The MariaDB matrix leg was not run locally (SQLite only here). (c) No criterion-completeness claim is made or reintroduced; every `complete`/`exhaust` in the new prose is a negation, and the npm pair is cited by name as the live instance of the difference.

## DL-289 — the PR-title gate inspects every branch that NAMES a card id, and one regex both decides and extracts it (card#6822)

- **Date:** 2026-08-18
- **Status:** implemented (card#6822). **Corrects DL-182 in exactly one clause — its accept-set — and supersedes nothing.** The token grammar, the `edited` trigger, the unconditional near-miss warning (DL-234) and the digit-class narrowing (DL-272) are all untouched and re-confirmed.

**What DL-182 established, and the half that stopped being true.** DL-182 made a card-id branch's PR title carry a `card#<id>` / `DL-NNNN` token, because that token is the ONLY key the writeback has. It defined "card-id branch" as `^[a-z-]+/[0-9]+-`. **The rule survives; the accept-set does not.** The house branch style drifted to the `card`-prefixed spellings, and a guard whose accept-set no longer describes the population it guards **passes green having enforced nothing** — the same silent-success shape DL-182 was written to abolish, re-minted one layer up, in the classifier instead of the token arm.

**Decision 1 — the accept-set is "a run of ASCII digits followed by a hyphen, optionally prefixed `card`/`card-`, optionally preceded by a `<type>/` segment."** So `fix/6100-slug` (DL-182's shape, unchanged), `card6027-slug`, `card-5538-slug`, `fix/card6371-slug` and `chore/card-5913-slug` all name a card id. **⚠ This is an accept/reject change:** a PR on either newly-reached spelling whose title carries no token now REDS where it passed.

**Decision 2 — the predicate and the id EXTRACTION become one regex (`BASH_REMATCH`), and this is not a tidy-up.** The extraction was a second parse — `${branch_lc#*/}` then a `%%-*` chop — that agreed with the predicate on exactly the one shape the predicate accepted. **Widening the predicate alone would have yielded `card6371` for the prefixed shape and the WHOLE BRANCH NAME for the segment-less one**, i.e. a gate that fires and then compares against a malformed id: loudly wrong instead of quietly absent, which is worse than the defect being fixed. Two copies of one decision is DL-182's real residue here (canon #5). Side effect worth naming: the old chop could place arbitrary branch text into the token arm's regex; `([0-9]+)` structurally cannot.

**MEASUREMENT — and ⚠ the two derivations disagree for a reason that was MEASURED, not assumed.** Over the merged subset of the newest 100 closed PRs, minus `dependabot/*`/`release/*`/`sync/*`/`revert-*`: on the newest **60 merged**, 35 branches — 16 old-reached, 6 segment-less, 7 prefixed, 6 card-less ⇒ **13 of 29 card-bearing PRs (45%) merged with nothing enforcing the writeback's only key**; over the full **96 merged** refs, **33** branches move skipped→enforced. card#6822 recorded 18/7/7/6 over a **different** window: `gh pr list --state merged --limit 60` orders by MERGE recency (oldest merge `2026-08-04`), while the derivation above is ordered by PR number and reaches back to a merge of `2026-07-29`. **Both reproduce exactly over the population each names — re-running the card's command returns the card's figures unchanged.** This is not window drift and was not left as one; ⇒ **any future re-count must state which window it used.** The shapes and the conclusion are identical either way.

**⛔ The prefixed shape is the finding, not the segment-less one.** `fix/card6371-…` and `chore/card-5913-…` DO follow the `<type>/…-slug` convention and read as compliant to a human reviewer. Only the literal `card` sitting between the slash and the digits put them outside the regex. A convention violation you can see is not the dangerous kind.

**Decision 3 — the guard moved, the branch names did not.** Renaming the offending branches would satisfy the old regex and leave the next `fix/card<NNNN>-` branch free to re-mint the silence (canon #2/#5). The header no longer restates WHICH spellings qualify — that set is owned by the require step's own predicate, for the same reason the token grammar is not restated there, and now with the same measured history: the set this header used to name is precisely the one that went stale while nothing noticed.

**Controls — 7 mutations of the real workflow, each applied, measured, and restored by snapshot.** The pre-fix predicate+extraction pair (6 legs red); **the named trap — predicate widened with the old extraction kept (5 legs red, exactly the `card`-prefixed rows)**; the `tr` case-fold removed (2); the exemption `case` removed (2); the trailing `-` dropped (3); the `^` anchor dropped (4); `BASH_REMATCH[3]`→`[2]` (9). Assertions read the **extracted id out of the step's own output**, so a malformed id cannot pass a leg that merely fired: the desync leg pins `card6371`/`card`/`card6027`/`card` against `6371`/`5913`/`6027`/`5538`.

⚠ **Two of the builder's own premises were falsified by its own checks and corrected before ship**, which is why they are recorded rather than the conclusions alone: (a) the trailing `-` was claimed to exclude `feat/oauth2-login` — measurement showed the `^` anchor does, and the leg is now split into two axes each paired with rows it actually flips; (b) the digitless rows were claimed as negative controls — they cannot flip under ANY widening, so they are population coverage, not controls. The real negative controls are `fix/cards-123-thing` (plural), `feat/oauth2-login` and `fix/2fa-enrollment`, each swallowed by a specific over-widening. Separately, *"every real exempt branch fails the predicate anyway"* is now **measured** (0 of 29) rather than asserted, which is why the `skip:exempt` rows are synthetic.

**Case-folding is preserved and now PINNED.** DL-182's `branch_lc`/`title_lc` fold (bridge #4384 — the classifier's regexes are `/i`, so a title the classifier correlates must never red here on case alone) is a real divergence from the co-vendored kanban-board copy. A leg removes the `tr` and watches an upper-case card branch go unreachable; `FIX/CARD6371-Stage-Aware-…` → `6371` and `Card-5538-…` → `5538` are asserted.

**⛔ DISCLOSED NEW FALSE RED, characterized rather than discovered later.** With both optionals empty the shape is a bare leading `<digits>-`, so `2026-08-18-notes` is enforced as card 2026. Absent from the corpus, as is a bare `5538-slug`. **Taken deliberately: the failure it risks is LOUD and the defect it closes is SILENT**, and that trade only runs one direction. Pinned as a test row so the choice is legible rather than latent.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **Nothing ran on a GitHub runner** — the require step's bash was executed by the repo's own harness against the real `run:` body; per the repo's testing doc nothing local validates Actions YAML *as* a workflow. The first real exercise is this PR's own run, and ⚠ **that run cannot exercise the NEW shapes**: the branch `fix/6822-…` satisfies the OLD accept-set too, so a green there proves no-regression, not the widening. **The new shapes' first real exercise is the next `card<NNNN>-` PR on this repo.** (b) The kanban-board copy is the same class (kanban card#6820, DL-244, shipped) and is a separate repo, board and gate — deliberately not touched here. (c) `[a-z-]+` still excludes digits in the type segment, so `v2/6822-slug` skips; pre-existing, unchanged, absent from the corpus. (d) The exemption glob set remains duplicated across `pr-title-lint.yml` and `changelog-gate.yml` — pre-existing canon #5 residue, consciously accepted with cross-references in both files, not introduced here.

**Log annotations — additive, no words removed.** DL-182's accept-set clause, DL-234's near-miss residue description, and DL-272's collation note each carry a forward pointer to this entry; the originals stay frozen per this log's append-only contract.

## DL-290 — a coord card's lane is resolved by ONE primitive for all three writes, and the label-after-open gap closes as an opt-in MOVE (card#6393)

- **Date:** 2026-08-20
- **Status:** implemented (card#6393). **Closes both residual instances DL-286's sibling audit filed as one class item**; supersedes nothing. DL-198's create-set, DL-200's correlation key and close leg, DL-204's fleet default, and DL-286's mirrored lane rule (`CoordLaneStages`, incl. the anchored-`[TASK]` gate and the skip-and-continue scan) are all untouched and re-confirmed.

**The class, restated from DL-286's audit:** *a coord-card stage minted or kept with NO lane input*. On a lane-model board the consumer's `kanban-writeback` pass runs BEFORE its issues-sync and maps the card's lane back onto the issue's `stage:*` label, so a bridge write that ignores the lane does not merely place a card — it REWRITES a written sequencing ruling on the issue. DL-286 fixed the create write and named two survivors: the **revive** arm (reopen → the fixed `coord_card_stage_id`) and the **label-after-open** create gap.

**Decision 1 — the resolution is ONE primitive with three call sites, not three derivations.** `CoordCardLanePlacement::resolve()` is extracted behaviour-preserving from `KanbanCoordCardHandler::createStage()` and returns `{stage, lane, unmapped}`. `lane` is the DISCRIMINATOR and is why it returns a shape rather than an int: **null** means no lane governs this card (no lane map configured, or a non-`[TASK]` title) and `stage` is then the caller's fixed stage — byte-identical DL-198/DL-200; **non-null** means the answer was derived. The relane leg acts only on a derived answer, so it needs no second copy of the "is the lane model live here" question. Three near-identical derivations of one rule is precisely how the movers come to disagree about where a `[TASK]` belongs (canon #5).

**Decision 2 — the primitive is PURE and carries NO logging, and that constraint came from the test suite, not from taste.** `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` (DL-285) holds **set-equality** over the bare `Log::warning`/`Log::error` call sites in `app/Bridge/Handlers/Kanban*Handler.php`. The unmapped-lane diagnostic hoisted into `app/Bridge/Writeback/` would have moved out from under that guard, which would then report clean over a population it no longer covers — the exact defect DL-285 exists to prevent, committed by a refactor rather than by a new arm. So `resolve()` returns `unmapped` as the caller's warn MATERIAL and each handler logs at its own call site, where the message can also name what that leg was doing. The move handler's new line is added to that test's ALLOWED map **with its reason** (a config-gap diagnostic on a move that SUCCEEDS — nothing was refused, so there is no failure to signal), which is the mechanism the guard is built around; the guard itself is not loosened.

**Decision 3 — the revive arm becomes lane-aware, and the classifier wire DL-286 named as the blocker is the whole cost.** DL-286 recorded the true reason the revive was deferred: the move family's target payload carried only `repo`/`issue_number`/`sid`/`disposition`. It now carries `title` + `labels` too, from the same family-wide `labels()` reader the create family uses — `issues.reopened` and `issues.closed` both deliver `issue.title` and `issue.labels`, so this costs no API read. Stamped on EVERY move target rather than only the revive one, because the family emits one payload shape; the terminal leg ignores both (a close is unconditional over lanes, ruled on roundtable #18). **Default-ON, but only for the population that already has BOTH `move_coord_cards` and `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` live.**

**Decision 4 — the label-after-open gap needs a MOVE, and card#6393's own stated fix would have shipped a no-op.** The card prescribed *"extending the create family (`issues.labeled`, redelivery-safe via the tag pre-check)"*. The create family already fires unconditionally at `issues.opened`, so the card EXISTS by the time any `labeled` event arrives; re-running create on it hits the `id:<sid>` tag pre-check, finds the card and skips. The pre-check that makes create redelivery-safe is exactly what makes it inert here. So the fix is a new `relane` disposition on the existing move handler, driven by a new `coord-card-relane` family.

**Decision 5 — the family is OPT-IN and never a default.** It is the only family that reacts to a label edit, and `issues.labeled` is a high-volume action on a live coordination repo: **641** such deliveries had already arrived on the reference install and been dropped as action-undeclared (operator measurement, last delivery 2026-08-20 15:31:53 UTC). That measurement cuts both ways and both are recorded: **no webhook-subscription change is needed** (enabling the family turns a stream that already arrives into board writes), and **a filter wrong in the permissive direction does not misfire once — it misfires across a live stream.** Gated additionally on the mapping's `move_coord_cards` (a relane IS the bridge moving a coord card) and on a `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` lane model existing at all — **both tested at the CLASSIFIER, not left to the handler**, and the reason is this same measurement. A target emitted for an inert leg is not free: the handler pays a `cardsByTag` search plus a `getCard` per correlated card before it can discover there is no lane to write, so leaving the lane test to it would buy two kanban reads per `issues.labeled` delivery, permanently, for zero board writes. The mapping is already in hand at the classifier. The handler keeps its own lane test (it does not author the targets it is handed — `kanban_coord_card_move` is registered unconditionally); what the classifier gate removes is the common path reaching it.

**Decision 6 — the trigger is the LANE VOCABULARY, not the `stage:` namespace, and the difference is a measured behaviour difference.** The first implementation filtered on `str_starts_with($name, 'stage:')`. That accepts every label an install invents in that namespace (`stage:done`, `stage:blocked`); `CoordLaneStages::resolveLane` recognizes none of them, the placement falls back to `DEFAULT_LANE`, and the handler MOVES the card there. **Measured, not reasoned:** with the prefix-only predicate in place, a real `issues.labeled` body announcing `stage:done` on a `[TASK]` whose card sits in lane `now` (stage 40) PATCHes that card to stage 42 (`later`) — a demotion on a label that expressed no sequencing at all, handing the consumer's lane→label pass a `stage:later` to write onto the issue. That is this card's own defect, minted by the fix for it, and on an already-arriving stream it is not one instance. The predicate is now `CoordLaneStages::isLaneLabel()` — the vocabulary's one owner, beside `LANES` and the prefix, so no caller re-spells either. The same reasoning is why **`unlabeled` is deliberately not consumed**: removing a `stage:*` label states no lane, and re-deriving on it would invent a sequencing decision nobody made.

**Decision 7 — the announced label is read from the delivery's own top-level `label.name`, and UNIONED into the lane inputs.** Filtering on "the issue HAS a `stage:*` label" instead of "this delivery ANNOUNCED one" would relane on every unrelated label edit to any already-sequenced issue — the bulk of the stream. Whether `issue.labels` on a `labeled` delivery already reflects the just-added label is **UNVERIFIED**: no delivery corpus was reachable from this branch to measure it on, and nothing was read that states it either way. Rather than depend on an unpinned snapshot ordering, the announced label is unioned into the label set the handler derives from — the trigger label is already in hand from the filter, so it costs nothing — and BOTH shapes (present in `issue.labels`, absent from it) are driven through the classifier with the same expected lane inputs. **The union settles the ADD direction and ONLY that one — a BOUND, not a closure.** A union cannot subtract, so the opposite shape still rides the same unpinned snapshot: a relabel (`stage:now` removed, `stage:later` added) arrives as an `unlabeled` delivery this family deliberately does not consume plus a `labeled` one, and if that `labeled` delivery's `issue.labels` still lists the removed `stage:now`, the set resolves to `now` by `LANES` order and the operator's explicit demotion is silently dropped. **Accepted, not fixed.** Deriving from the announced label ALONE would close it and is refused for AGREEMENT: the consumer's `_task_lane` resolves over the issue's whole label set in `LANES` order, so an announced-only derivation would disagree with it on any issue carrying two lane labels (`stage:maybe` added to an issue already labelled `stage:now` resolves to `now` there and would resolve to `maybe` here) — and mirroring that rule rather than inventing a better one is DL-286's whole posture. Consuming `unlabeled` to learn of the removal is the invented-sequencing arm Decision 6 rules out. What closes this direction is pinning the snapshot's ordering against a real delivery corpus — the same UNVERIFIED measurement this decision names — not more logic here.

**Decision 8 — the relane leg has THREE gates, and the third is the one that keeps it from re-minting this card in reverse.** (1) The answer must be lane-DERIVED (Decision 1's discriminator) — this is what makes an install with no `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` byte-identical. Its two causes are logged apart (no lane model configured — a config gap the operator can close; versus a title the lane model does not govern — the design working, nothing to do), because one line for both tells the reader which it was: nothing. (2) The card must currently BE in one of the mapped lanes: relane is a lane→lane move, so a card someone advanced to a working column, or one the close leg parked in `coord_card_terminal_stage_id`, is never yanked back by a label edit (the terminal is disjoint from the lanes by config, so this subsumes it). (3) The card's current stage must be **service-set** — `last_stage_move.actor_type === "service"`, the SAME allow-list the revive arm already carried, reused rather than paralleled. Without (3) a label would override a human's deliberate board re-lane: instead of the writeback overwriting a label, the label would overwrite a board move. **Two movers disagreeing is what this card IS; a fix that adds a third mover is not a fix.**

**Decision 9 — `bridge:check` gains the family's silent-inert advisory, mirroring DL-204's, in ONE direction and not two.** With Decision 5's classifier gate in place, an operator who enables `coord-card-relane` without `move_coord_cards` or without `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` gets no config error (a lane-less mapping is valid for every other leg), no board write, and now nothing classified either — silent in a way no existing leg reports. `CheckContext` gains `coordCardRelaneScopes` beside `coordCardMoveScopes` (separate maps: the two families are independently enabled, and one map would make each family's advisory speak for the other's absence), and `writeback.mapping_config` warns naming whichever key is missing, both collected into one line (the DL-195 shape). **The DL-204 pair's SECOND direction is deliberately not mirrored, and that is a ruling:** `coord_card_terminal_stage_id` means the move leg and nothing else, so setting it declares an intent a missing family contradicts. `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` carries no such meaning — it is the CREATE leg's key (required alongside `create_coord_cards`, and read by the revive leg since this entry), so a lane model with no relane family is the normal shape of *every* lane-model install, including the reference one. A "lane ids set but no relane family" warn would fire on all of them for a family that is opt-in by design. **`docs/check-golden-coverage.md` is NOT regenerated, and the disposition is measured rather than assumed:** the new `handle()` accumulation predicate was flipped to `if (false)` and the golden suite re-run — **84/84 green**, so it would be an UNOBSERVED row (the fixture set enables no relane family), while the same mutant reds both new `BridgeCommandsTest` legs. Regenerating rewrites every line-keyed id in that file for one row known in advance to be a disclosed gap; the measurement is recorded here instead.

**Scope — instance 3 was SPLIT OUT, not silently dropped.** The card's third instance (product-board routing: the consumer routes a routing-labelled `[TASK]` to a different board with a different lane model, and the bridge has no per-issue board routing at all) is architecturally disjoint from one shared lane-placement primitive and is tracked as **card#7098**.

**Tests — the permissive direction is pinned by mutation, in both places it can fail.** New: `CoordinationCardRelaneClassifierTest` (family emit, the lane-model config gate, the three declining shapes — a non-`stage` label, a `stage:*` the issue merely carries, and a `stage:`-prefixed label outside the vocabulary — plus the four lane labels that DO trigger, the union leg, case folding, `unlabeled`, opt-in-ness, the `move_coord_cards` gate, the population gate, and `consumedEventTypes`); `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandlerTest`'s lane section (lane-aware revive incl. the unmapped-lane warn and the unchanged human-terminal refusal; relane's idempotent no-op, the human-lane refusal, the null-`actor_type` fail-closed, the terminal card, the unmapped-stage card, the no-lane-map inertness, the non-`[TASK]` title) and three full-dispatch legs that drive a real webhook body through classify→registry→handle; `BridgeCommandsTest` gains Decision 9's four legs (each missing key, both missing at once, the family-scoping negative, and the fully-configured silence), whose three predicates were each seen to fail by mutation — the arm off reds the two warn legs, an unconditional warn reds the silence leg, and dropping the family scoping reds the negative. **The vector is `stage:now` and never `stage:later` throughout: `later` is the no-label default, so a broken wire would land the card in the same stage as a working one and the leg could not fail** (DL-286's own lesson, re-applied). **Decision 6 was seen to fail:** replacing `isLaneLabel()` with the prefix-only predicate (restored by `cp`+`cmp`, never `git checkout --`) reds **5 of 2277** — the classifier's out-of-vocabulary leg, the full-dispatch leg that asserts NO board write, and three of the predicate's own vector legs in `CoordLaneStagesTest` (the prefix-alone set, the contains-a-lane-name set `stage:no`/`stage:nowish`, and the stray-whitespace set, whose trailing-space `stage:now ` the prefix accepts) — and swapping the dispatch leg's assertion to `assertMovedTo(42)` under the same mutant passes, which is how the `later` demotion above is a measurement rather than a claim. *(It reddened exactly 2 of 2266 while the predicate had no direct vectors; the review that added them moved both numbers.)* **`isLaneLabel` is vectored in `CoordLaneStagesTest`** — 6 new methods, taking that file from 10 to **16** — because `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` names it as where the lane agreement's re-ported vectors live, and the trigger reads the same vocabulary from the other end. Its vectors are adversarial rather than ported, and the file says so: the consumer has no such predicate, because it only ever resolves a whole label SET. **2277/2277 phpunit (7087 assertions)** — 2266 before this review's legs, +11 — phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs` clean.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **Nothing was exercised against a live coordination repo or a live kanban board** — every leg is `Http::fake`d, and the first real exercise is an operator enabling the family on an install. (b) **The 641-delivery figure and its timestamp are the operator's measurement, carried here as sourced; no delivery corpus was reachable from this branch**, so neither the share of those deliveries announcing a `stage:*` label nor the `issue.labels` snapshot question (Decision 7) was measured here. The design does not depend on the first at all; it depends on the second in ONE direction only, and that is Decision 7's stated bound rather than a closure — the union covers a snapshot MISSING the announced label, and a snapshot still listing a just-REMOVED lane label drops the removal. (c) The `bridge:check` event-follows-consumer advisory will stop reporting `issues.labeled` as arrived-and-unconsumed on any install that enables the family; that is the check working, and that leg's code is untouched. Check code DOES change, for Decision 9's new advisory only — no existing finding's text or ordering moves, which is what leaves the golden byte-contract intact (`CheckGoldenTest` 84/84 with the arm live).

**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Writeback/CoordCardLanePlacement.php`; `CoordLaneStages` (`isLaneLabel()`); `CoordinationClassifier` (the `coord-card-relane` family + its action const + `consumedEventTypes` arm; the move family's payload gains `title`/`labels`); `KanbanCoordCardHandler` (`createStage()` routes through the primitive; its private `labels()` reader moves onto it); `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandler` (the `DISPOSITIONS` allow-list gains `relane`, `moveOne()` takes the payload, new `relaneOne()`/`serviceSet()`/`warnUnmappedLanes()`, the revive write is lane-derived); `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` ALLOWED gains the new line with its reason; `CheckContext` (`coordCardRelaneScopes`), `CheckCommand` (its accumulation) and `WritebackMappingConfigCheck` (Decision 9's advisory); `docs/writeback.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`, `docs/customization.md`, `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, and additive annotations on DL-286's precondition + sibling-audit paragraphs. **No migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change, no new webhook subscription.** Byte-identical for any install without `coord_card_lane_stage_ids`; the relane leg is additionally inert until an operator adds the family. Cards #6393, #7098; DL-198, DL-200, DL-204, DL-285, DL-286.

## DL-291 — rule 1's two escape hatches read an annotation at ONE scope, that scope is the sentence, and the sentence boundary is not `[.!?]\s` (card#7127)

- **Date:** 2026-08-21
- **Status:** implemented (card#7127). **Corrects DL-013 in exactly one clause — the reach of the removed-marker — and supersedes nothing.** The vocabulary is untouched, the surfaces scanned are untouched, and the rule DL-013 established stands: prose naming a since-deleted construct fails CI unless it is annotated as deliberately historical.

**Context — two answers to one question, in one file.** `bin/check-doc-refs.php` carries two escape hatches for rule 1, and both answer *"does this annotation cover this citation?"*. The removed-marker answered it over the whole **line**; `citedAsRejected()` answered it over the **sentence**, and its own docblock says why — a decision-log entry is one enormous line whose alternatives sit beside the consequences, so a line-scoped read of "rejected" would exempt the built constructs cited two clauses away. That is the same argument, and it was only ever applied to one of the two. Two formats for one thing inside a single file is the shape canon #5 names, and it left a third hatch free to arrive at a third granularity.

**⛔ The cost was not hypothetical, and it grew.** `docs/CHANGELOG.md` entries are single lines that narrate a removal **and** cite the live members that replaced it — the speech act a release note makes by construction. One truthful *"X was removed"* therefore switched the member leg off for every other citation on that line. card#6025's review measured the loss at one citation and called it *"small now; it grows with each annotation"*; widening the marker vocabulary in that same change took it to nineteen, and every subsequent release note added more. **Disclosed rather than silent** — the per-run unexamined tally has always printed the bucket — which is why card#6025 filed it instead of folding it in.

**Decision 1 — the scope is hoisted into one helper, `annotationCovers($line, $tok, $marker)`, and both hatches consume it.** The granularity is decided in one place and a caller supplies only the words it accepts. This is deliberately not a second sentence-splitter retrofitted into the marker leg: two implementations of one scope is the defect being fixed, and fixing it by adding a copy would re-mint it. `citedAsRejected()` survives as the named predicate holding the *rejected* vocabulary, implemented over the shared helper; the splitter itself is `sentencesOf()`, which rule 3 already shipped.

**⚑ Decision 2 — the sentence boundary is NOT `[.!?]\s`, and this was found by review after the first implementation shipped it wrong.** Recorded prominently because the fix was one character from inert. `sentencesOf()` split on a terminator followed by whitespace; but a terminator in these documents is usually **not** followed by whitespace — the sentence closes with markdown emphasis, a quote or a bracket first (`.**`, `.*`, `."`, `.)`, and the `.**]**` an appended annotation ends on). Under the naive pattern *"…was removed.** `Foo::bar()` is live"* is ONE fragment, the whole line goes back to the marker, and the line scope is restored **at green**. The exposure is not an edge: `docs/CHANGELOG.md` and `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md` — the two surfaces this decision exists for — carry **hundreds** of the bold form each (re-derive with `grep -o '\.\*\*' <file> | wc -l`). Closing punctuation is therefore part of the terminator. **The bound lives on the SPLITTER's docblock, not on a caller** — it hid precisely because `annotationCovers()` documented a different bound and the splitter documented none.

**Decision 3 — the splitter is byte-oriented, not `/u`, and that is measured rather than assumed.** The closer class carries three multi-byte characters, so `/u` is the reflex. But `preg_split` with `/u` returns `false` on input that is not valid UTF-8, and this function's fallback is the WHOLE text — silently restoring the widest possible scope on exactly the file nobody inspects. Without `/u`, the same five inputs (`’`, `”`, `»`, `…`, an em-dash mid-prose) split identically and every fragment is valid UTF-8, because each closer's bytes are consumed whole or not at all. The fallback stays fail-open on purpose — a fragment the splitter cannot compute must never invent a finding — and this bound is what keeps that path unreachable for real input.

**Decision 4 — the file/FQCN leg is moved too, not only the member leg the card measured.** The marker is one variable read by both legs. Sentence-scoping one of them would have left the same word meaning "this line" in one place and "this sentence" in another — the split being closed, re-opened one level up. **Cost, stated at the size that is actually load-bearing:** of the 128 backtick tokens in the six current-state docs that stop being line-skipped, only **4** are things the path leg can resolve at all (`app/Bridge/Support/SubscriptionRegistry.php`, `AgentConfig.php`, `AgentRegistry.php`, `config/bridge.php`) — the other 124 are prose the leg returns nothing for either way. All four resolve, so the leg gains **zero** findings. ⚠ The token count is the wrong unit and quoting it as the benefit overstates this by more than thirty-fold; the reason to move this leg is the consistency argument above, not a number.

**Decision 5 — an appended annotation must NAME the citation it discharges, and that is a real cost accepted in the open.** The freeze rule (DL-277) forbids editing a merged sentence, so the discharge is an annotation appended after it — and an appended annotation is a different sentence. It therefore has to repeat the citation in backticks instead of a bare *"removed in v0.60"*. **The trade is accepted because the shorter form is not actually an annotation of anything**: at the foot of a forty-sentence entry it names none of that entry's citations, and the reader cannot tell which construct went. Exactly **one** entry in the tree needed the token added when this landed — DL-237's SUPERSEDED note on the `_deploy_snapshot` conformance, which named the deleted member bare — and it was discharged by appending a further annotation, never by editing either frozen sentence.

**MEASUREMENT — stated as a reconciliation, with the method, and deliberately not as a before/after table of totals.** A totals table is a quoted authority: it is read at whatever tree the author happened to be standing on, and the first version of this entry proved the point by recording an "after" column taken at an intermediate state that reproduces at no shipped commit. What is recomputable is the **shape of the movement at a fixed corpus**, so that is what is recorded, together with how to re-derive it:

> Place the pre-change script and the post-change script side by side in a directory no rule scans (`harness/`, per `DocRefGateHarness`'s reasoning — the script resolves its root as `dirname(__DIR__)`), run each with `--census` over the same tree, and difference the buckets. At a fixed corpus the deltas MUST sum to zero; a non-zero sum means the two runs did not see the same corpus and the reading is void.

Run that way over the tree this entry ships in: **80 citations leave the removed-marker bucket. 50 of them become EXAMINED — all 50 resolve, and `reported` does not move. The remaining 30 land in a different NOT-examined bucket: 26 `class_not_under_app`, 2 `unverifiable_ancestry`, 2 `rejected_alternative`.** ⚠ **This entry's own prose is part of the corpus those figures are taken over**, so they moved while it was being written and will move again with the next doc edit — which is the whole reason the method above is the durable half and these five numbers are a dated reading. What does not move is the invariant: the deltas sum to zero, and the marker bucket's exodus splits into examined versus still-unexamined with `class_not_under_app` the largest non-`resolved` destination. ⚠ **That last group is the part a "coverage recovered" headline hides**, and `class_not_under_app` — a citation the leg examines and then cannot answer for — is the largest destination after `resolved`. Releasing a citation from the marker is not the same as answering it.

**`reported` went 0 → 1 → 0, and the 1 is re-derivable rather than recalled.** Strip the `card#7127` annotation from DL-237's SUPERSEDED note and re-run: the gate reports `ChannelSnapshotProbe::referenceFileSet()` — a member DL-237 removed — and exits 1. It is declared nowhere under `app/`, `tests/` or `bin/`, so the finding is true and the fix was to the **document**, never to the scope.

**Controls.** Every acceptance is paired with the same prose one character different, so a moved verdict is attributable. The recovered coverage is witnessed by making the recovered citation a PHANTOM and watching it red — an acceptance alone cannot distinguish *"the marker is scoped correctly"* from *"nothing is checked at all"*, which is exactly the pre-fix state. The terminator vector of Decision 2 was watched RED against the shipped-wrong splitter before it was fixed, with the other vectors in the same file staying green, so the failure was attributable to the boundary and not to the change around it. The negative is pinned beside them: a citation genuinely inside the removal sentence is still discharged, paired against the same sentence with the marker word swapped out.

**⚠ DISCLOSED NARROWING, characterized rather than discovered later.** The `~~` alternative in the vocabulary narrowed along with the prose markers: a struck-through block that spans several sentences on one line now discharges only the fragment carrying the `~~`, not the whole line. **Zero live instances** — every `~~` in this tree today strikes a heading that is one fragment — so this is disclosed, not measured as a cost, and it is named because the rest of this entry describes the change purely in terms of prose markers and a reader would not infer it.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Retrofit sentence-scoping into the marker leg and leave `citedAsRejected()` as it is** — rejected: it fixes the measured symptom and keeps the two implementations, so the next hatch picks its own granularity again. (b) **Widen the marker vocabulary instead** — rejected, and it is what caused the growth: more words on a line-scoped read is more blindness, not less. (c) **A rule that lets an unnamed marker reach the sentence it follows** — rejected on the corpus: the one real annotation needing it sits many sentences from the citation it discharges, so adjacency would not have covered it. (d) **Leave it and rely on the disclosed tally** — that was card#6025's ruling and was correct for that change; it stops being correct once the loss is the largest unexamined bucket and grows with every release note.

**Not fixed here, and the reason FIRST RECORDED IN THIS ENTRY WAS FALSE — corrected in place before merge.** This entry originally said `CLAUDE_CONVENTIONS.md:141` survives because *"the marker and the citation share a sentence."* **They do not.** Run the splitter on that line: `Class::member` sits in the bold lead-in fragment, which carries no marker word at all, and the marker words sit in two later fragments that cite nothing. The two only merged under the **broken** boundary of Decision 2 — so the case was never an instance of *prose about the vocabulary discharging itself*; it was an instance of the terminator defect, and fixing the splitter reaches it. With the boundary corrected that line's citation is EXAMINED, landing in `class_not_under_app` for an unrelated reason (`Class` is a placeholder naming no file under `app/`). ⇒ **The sub-shape card#7127's second comment describes remains mechanically live** — a sentence that both names a marker word and carries a citation does discharge that citation — **but its measured cost on this tree is now zero citations, not one**, and this document no longer records a cause that would have sent the next maintainer looking in the wrong place. The disposition on card#7127 (accepted, not fixed — every proposed fix is a special case in a vocabulary whose virtue is being dumb and predictable) stands for the mechanism.

**Consequences:** `bin/check-doc-refs.php` (new `annotationCovers()`; `sentencesOf()` gains the closing-punctuation terminator and the docblock that owns that bound; `citedAsRejected()` reimplemented over the helper; `$skip` renamed `$removedMarker`; both rule-1 legs call the helper per TOKEN rather than per line; census bucket `removed_marker_line` → `removed_marker_sentence` and the run line's wording with it; the rule-1 remediation string now states the sentence scope and the repeat-the-citation requirement, since a guard's remediation string is a doc surface); `tests/Support/DocRefGateHarness.php` gains the `assertAccepted`/`assertRejected` pair hoisted at its second real caller; new `tests/Feature/Workflows/DocRefMarkerScopeTest.php`; `tests/Feature/Workflows/DocRefMemberLintTest.php`; `CLAUDE_CONVENTIONS.md`; additive annotations on DL-013's scope clause and on DL-237's SUPERSEDED note; `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **No `app/` change, no migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change** — the executable surface is one CI script and its tests. ⚠ **UPGRADING (contributors, not installs): CI is STRICTER.** A doc line whose removed-marker sits in a different sentence from a dangling citation now reds where it passed; the fix is to move the marker into that citation's sentence, or to repeat the citation inside the annotation. Cards #7127, #6025; DL-013, DL-237, DL-277.
## DL-292 — the belongs-to-mapped-board guard is ONE primitive owning the compare AND the refusal report, and the canonical predicate is `is_numeric` + `(int)` (card#7138)

- **Date:** 2026-08-21
- **Status:** implemented (card#7138). **Closes the CLASS card#7133 split out** — DL-009's authz model and DL-020's transient/permanent split are untouched and re-confirmed; DL-274/DL-285's paired log-then-push primitive is the channel this routes through, unchanged. **⛔ Predicate change on two arms, hard-gate approved by the user 2026-08-21** (it changes what `kanban_move_card` and `kanban_block_reason` accept).

**The class.** The DL-009 belongs-to-mapped-board rule was written out three times, in three non-equivalent spellings: `$boardId !== $mapping->boardId` (`KanbanMoveCardHandler`), `($card['board_id'] ?? null) !== $mapping->boardId` (`KanbanBlockReasonHandler`), and `! is_numeric($card['board_id'] ?? null) || (int) $card['board_id'] !== $mapping->boardId` (`KanbanCoordCardMoveHandler`). One behaviour, three implementations, so a change to the rule had to be made three times and correctly each time — and it demonstrably did not happen: card#7133 found the same guard carrying two different report severities, the coord copy sitting at `Log::info` while its twins pushed an alert. **Two defects, one cause** (canon #7): the severity split, and the duplication that let it diverge.

**Decision 1 — one primitive owns the compare AND the report, not just the compare.** `MappedBoardGuard::refuses()` runs the predicate and, on a refusal, emits the `warnAndNotify` itself; the three call sites are reduced to `if (MappedBoardGuard::refuses(…)) { return; }`. Hoisting only the predicate and leaving three hand-written reports behind would have left the severity half of the class exactly where it was. What varies per arm is passed in — the message's reaction prefix, the `$outcome` that keeps the three off each other's dedup markers (DL-274(3)), and the optional `$issueNumber` (DL-285) that adds the `issue` log-context key on the coord arm. The reason code `card_not_on_mapped_board` and the message body are now constants of the primitive, so all three refusals cannot drift apart again.

⚑ This is the OPPOSITE constraint to DL-290 Decision 2, and deliberately. There, a diagnostic was kept at the call sites so it stayed inside `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest`'s bare-log population. Here the report is a routed `warnAndNotify`, which was never in that population, so moving it costs that guard nothing — and Decision 4 replaces what it does cost with a stronger, level-independent leg.

**Decision 2 — the canonical predicate is the coord copy's `is_numeric` + `(int)` form, which WIDENS what the two twins accept.** `WritebackMapping::$boardId` is a `readonly int` and `!==` does no type juggling, so both twins refused ANY non-int `board_id` — including the numeric string `"8"` and the JSON float `8.0`, which name the very board that is mapped. Measured over one vector set rather than reasoned about:

| `board_id` | twin `!==` | coord `is_numeric` + `(int)` |
|---|---|---|
| `8` | ACT | ACT |
| `"8"` · `8.0` · `"08"` · `"+8"` · `" 8"` · `"8e0"` | **REFUSE** | **ACT** |
| `8.9` · `"8.9"` · `"8.00"` · `"8.0000001"` · `8.999999` | **REFUSE** | **ACT** — see the truncation note below |
| `"8abc"` · `"0x8"` · `null` · `"abc"` · `""` · `true` · `9` · `7.9` | REFUSE | REFUSE |

**⚑ The accepted set is an INTERVAL, not a value, and the minute says so because the code does.** `is_numeric($v) && (int) $v === 8` accepts every numeric spelling of a value in the half-open interval **`[8, 9)`** — `(int)` TRUNCATES toward zero, it does not round or reject a fraction. So `8.9` and `"8.0000001"` name board 8 to this guard, while `7.9` (→ `7`) does not: truncation can only reach the mapped board from ABOVE. **This is inherent to the approved form** — there is no version of `is_numeric` + `(int)` that accepts `"8"` and rejects `8.9`, so it was not a separate choice available to be made — and the ⚠ UPGRADING prose that scoped the widening to a value *"naming the mapped board"* under-described it. Recorded here so the minuted approved set EQUALS the shipped set.

**⛔ Ruled: keep the truncation, do NOT make the compare lossless.** Operator ruling, 2026-08-21, taken on this enumeration rather than on the narrower one this entry first carried. Three reasons, in the order they carry weight: (a) it is **unreachable on any current install** — `board_id` is a JSON integer from this API, which is already STATED BOUND (a) below, so a fractional `board_id` is not a value this guard can be handed today; (b) a lossless compare (`(float) $v === (float) $mapping->boardId`, or an `is_int`-after-`is_numeric` gate) would be a SECOND predicate change on the same two arms, re-opening a gate that was just closed, to refuse a value no install emits; and (c) it opens no hole the guard exists to close — every accepted value still truncates onto the mapped board, and `"8abc"`, the one input a bare cast would wave through, is still refused by the `is_numeric` leg. **No new reason code**: a fractional `board_id` is not a distinct operator hypothesis, it is a kanban contract change, and inventing a slug for it would put a reason in the vocabulary that no install can produce. `docs/writeback.md` already words the rule as *"must equal the mapped `board_id` when cast to an int"*, which is exactly what ships — that sentence needs no correction, only the example row it now carries.

⇒ The coord refusal set is a strict **SUBSET** of the twins'. **The coord copy is the most PERMISSIVE of the three and the most CORRECT; it is not the strictest.** `is_numeric` is not what makes it strict — it is what stops `(int)` coercing a NON-numeric value into the mapped id (`(int) "8abc" === 8`), which is the one hole that tolerating numeric strings would otherwise open. ⛔ Recorded in this direction because the inverse was asserted once, on card#7133, and reached a code comment and a commit message before it was measured and corrected (comment 1014 on that card).

**Why widen rather than narrow.** A numeric-string board id names the same board (and, per the truncation note above, so does any numeric value in `[8, 9)` for a mapped board of 8 — the widening is an interval, not a spelling); refusing it is a FALSE refusal that no-ops a legitimate move and pushes a `card_not_on_mapped_board` alert on correct work — an availability defect, and a security signal spent on a non-event. Narrowing the coord arm to `!==` instead would have made all three brittle in the same way and would have deleted the `is_numeric` leg that is doing real work. **There is no fail-open in either direction, before or after:** every value that does not name the mapped board is still refused, and `"8abc"` — the one input a bare `(int)` compare would wave through — is refused by the `is_numeric` leg, which is now load-bearing on all three arms instead of one.

**⚑ LATENT, not live, and the distinction is the whole severity.** `board_id` comes back as a JSON **integer** from this API today (verified live against a board-8 card, 2026-08-21), so no install is currently mis-refusing anything and the accepted set changes in theory before it changes in practice. This is a behaviour change to a security guard nonetheless, which is why it is gated, minuted here, and stated in `docs/CHANGELOG.md` rather than folded in as a refactor.

**Decision 3 — the widening is pinned on both twins by tests that FAIL against the old spelling.** `"8"` (an array fixture) and `8.0` (a **raw JSON body**, because `json_encode(8.0)` emits `8` and an array fixture would silently round-trip to the int case and test nothing) must now ACT on both twin paths; `"8abc"` must still refuse on both. Reverting the predicate in the primitive reds exactly the four new acting legs and nothing else.

**Decision 4 — the class guard is re-pointed at the primitive, by KIND, and the LEVEL bound it already carried is left standing rather than widened.** `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` exists to catch a refusal that does not alert, and it was **green over card#7133's defect for the defect's entire life**: its population is every `Log::warning(`/`Log::error(` site, so a security refusal written at `Log::info` was structurally outside it. Widening that population by LEVEL is not the fix — `Log::info` is also ~34 not-tracked / success / policy sites, and pulling them in would drown the signal. The closure is by KIND: a second leg re-derives, every run, every non-comment line in `app/Bridge/Handlers/Kanban*Handler.php` naming the card field `'board_id'` or the reason literal `'card_not_on_mapped_board'`, and requires that set to be **empty** — a membership decision cannot be written without one of the two. A fourth copy therefore reds at any log level, or at none. The empty expectation is a measurement rather than a decoration because two things make failure possible: a scanner control on a fixture whose answer is known, and a positive assertion that the primitive still holds the rule, so a deleted guard cannot read as a clean repo. **Proven by firing it:** a fourth copy planted in `KanbanBlockReasonHandler` reporting at `Log::info` reds the new leg while the level-keyed leg stays green — which is the original defect, reproduced and now caught.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Align the two twins in place, keep three copies** — rejected: it is the same behaviour change to the same two paths, buys none of the consolidation, and leaves the N+1th copy free to mint the divergence again. (b) **Hoist the predicate only, leave the three reports** — rejected per Decision 1: the severity split lived in the reports. (c) **Narrow the coord arm to `!==`** — rejected per Decision 2: it makes all three wrong together and deletes a leg that is doing work. (d) **Widen the coverage guard to `Log::info`** — rejected per Decision 4: it converts one blind spot into an unreadable one. (e) **Key the new leg on `$mapping->boardId` instead of the card's `board_id`** — rejected: ~21 legitimate read-scoping uses of `$mapping->boardId` live in those handlers, so the population would be an allow-list of unrelated call sites that reds on every unrelated edit; the card's board field has exactly one honest reason to be read in a handler, and that reason now lives in the primitive.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **Nothing was exercised against a live kanban instance** — every leg is `Http::fake`d; the live check is the operator's, and the `board_id`-is-an-integer observation above is a read of one live card, not a contract kanban publishes. (b) **The new guard's population is the same `app/Bridge/Handlers/Kanban*Handler.php` glob the level-keyed leg carries**, so a membership compare minted outside those six files — a handler named off-pattern, or a new `Writeback/` collaborator — is not covered until the glob is widened. (c) **It closes exactly ONE refusal kind.** Every other refusal kind is still covered only by the level-keyed leg and its `Log::info` bound; this is a structural closure of the guard that was actually missed, not a general answer to "no refusal is silent".

**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Writeback/MappedBoardGuard.php`; `KanbanMoveCardHandler`, `KanbanBlockReasonHandler` and `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandler` each lose their copy of the compare and the report; `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` gains the KIND leg, its control and the class-docblock bound; `docs/writeback.md` (the three `card_not_on_mapped_board` rows, the accepted-set note, and the coverage-bound paragraph); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`; DL-241's Context annotated where it quotes the old spelling. 6 tests added (2 acting + 1 refusing per twin), 2 added to the class guard. **No config change, no new `.env`, no migration, and nothing about what the RECEIVER accepts** — the change is confined to what the writeback does with a card kanban hands back.

## DL-293 — the writeback resolves a repo by IDENTITY, not by spelling: one canonical index built at load, both sides through the vendored normalizer, and two keys naming one repo fail CLOSED (card#7124)

- **Date:** 2026-08-21
- **Status:** implemented (card#7124). **⛔ Hard-gate approved by the user 2026-08-21** — it widens what the writeback accepts (a mapping that matched nothing starts matching, and starts moving cards on a live board). Extends DL-009/019 (`writeback.json`); **honors DL-185's "Raw repo key, not canonical" ruling rather than overturning it** (Decision 2); no change to what the RECEIVER accepts or rejects.

**The defect.** `WritebackConfig::mappingFor()` was a raw array-key lookup — `$this->mappings[$repo] ?? null` — with neither side canonicalized: the keys were stored verbatim from the JSON, and the argument is the repo string off the GitHub payload (`repository.full_name` → `scope_id`). GitHub `owner/repo` is case-insensitive, so two spellings of one repo are one repo, and a raw `===` called them different. **The failure is silent by construction**: all 12 call sites read null as "this repo is not tracked" and return — the six handler sites on a `Log::info` nobody reads, the six classifier sites with no log at all — so *misconfigured* and *deliberately untracked* were the same output — no error, no alert, no `bridge:check` finding, no card moved, forever. The normalizing comparator already existed and was already applied to this exact question one file over (`KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler:293` compares a card's `canonRepo` to `canonicalizeSource($repo)`) — two answers to "is this the same repo?", one of them wrong (canon #5).

**⛔ Decision 1 — canonicalize at PARSE and at LOOKUP in the SAME change; a half-fix is an OUTAGE, not a partial fix.** Measured on both live installs before writing any code: **4 of 4 mapping keys are non-canonical** (`PupFuzz/agent-webhook-bridge`, `PupFuzz/kanban-board`, `PupFuzz/agent-board-toolkit` in prod; one in dev), and 349 retained real deliveries across 4 repos all carry `PupFuzz/…`. Both sides are non-canonical *in the same way*, which is why the raw `===` matches today and nothing is broken. ⇒ **Canonicalizing only the lookup argument yields `pupfuzz/…`, which matches NONE of the live keys — writeback dies on three production repos at once, silently, through the not-tracked path.** The armed shape is therefore the *natural* spelling (`pupfuzz/…`, what every GitHub URL accepts and every `gh` command echoes) and the disarmed one is the *unnatural* one the configs happen to carry. The two halves are one change; neither ships alone.

**Decision 2 — the STORED key keeps the operator's spelling; repo IDENTITY lives in a separate canonical index.** `WritebackConfig::$mappings` stays keyed exactly as `writeback.json` spells it, and the constructor builds `byCanonicalRepo` (+ `configuredRepos`) beside it; `mappingFor()` reads the index, `configuredRepoFor()` maps any spelling back to the configured one. **The raw key is load-bearing and this is DL-185's ruling, re-verified rather than inherited:** the credential store's `[git-credential-map]` is case-SENSITIVE (`git-credential-coord` sets `cp.optionxform = str` — read at source), and the live store maps `github.com/PupFuzz`. Measured against the installed helper: `path=PupFuzz/agent-webhook-bridge` → a `password=` line; `path=pupfuzz/agent-webhook-bridge` → none. ⇒ **Storing canonical keys would have been the same three-repo outage through a second door** — `bridge:reconcile` and its `bridge:check` preflight would resolve no per-repo token — and it would have silently overturned a ratified decision. The raw key is also what every operator-facing line prints, so an operator can find the line in their own file.

**Decision 2b — the contract has TWO runtime consumers, and both were newly-reachable paths that had to be brought back through `configuredRepoFor()` (review MAJOR 1).** Before this entry both were safe BY CONSTRUCTION: reaching them required `mappingFor()` to have matched byte-for-byte, so the payload spelling WAS the configured key. Decision 1 removes that guarantee, and a change that widens a match without restoring what the match used to guarantee is only half done. (1) **`KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler`** fed the PAYLOAD spelling to `GitHubTokenResolver::resolveFor()` — the case-SENSITIVE credential store — so it and `bridge:check` (which iterates the configured keys) would have probed DIFFERENT keys, making `GitHubTokenResolver`'s own "can never diverge" claim false for a third consumer, and making DL-185's "the resolver is invoked with the raw mapping key" false at this call site. (2) **`KanbanDependabotCardHandler`** rendered `{repo}` into a PERSISTED `id:` provenance tag from the payload spelling; a tag is text the operator declared, and an external tag-keyed reader correlates on it. Both now take `configuredRepoFor($repo) ?? $repo`, exactly as `ReconcileCommand` already did. **The audit was a pass over all 12 `mappingFor()` sites, not a patch of the one reported:** those two are the complete set of case-sensitive downstream consumers of the matched spelling — the remaining ten reach only kanban API calls (server-canonicalized `source`, case-insensitive by contract) or alert dedup keys, which are per-delivery and carry one spelling per install either way.

**Decision 3 — two keys naming one repo FAIL CLOSED at load, naming both spellings.** They were two mappings before the index and can only be one after it; keeping the last silently is how a board gets written by the wrong mapping. The diagnostic names both original spellings and the repo they collide on, and follows the `ConfigException` shape `writeback.json` already fails closed with. A **blank** key fails closed the same way and for the same reason, one step earlier: it can match no payload repo, so it is a dead mapping — the exact silent misconfiguration this entry exists to end. Both throws live in the CONSTRUCTOR, not in `load()`, so a hand-built config cannot dodge them. **The `REF_MAX` (255) truncation clause is scoped to the PARSE side, and the distinction is real (review minor 5).** At parse, two keys longer than 255 chars that differ only past the cap collide and FAIL CLOSED — the guard above catches them. At LOOKUP there is no such symmetry: a payload repo longer than the cap is truncated before the index read, so it can silently match a mapping it differs from past char 255. Unreachable in practice — GitHub caps `owner/repo` at 39 + 1 + 100 = 140 chars — and confirmed by construction rather than fixed in code, because narrowing the cap would fork the vendored normalizer this entry exists to converge on.

**Decision 4 — the `bridge:check` compares that read a mapping key against a scope map are canonicalized in the SAME change, because the fix would otherwise make them LIE.** `writebackEmittingScopes` / `coordCardMoveScopes` / `coordCardRelaneScopes` are keyed by an agent YAML's `scope_id` and read with a `writeback.json` mapping key — the same config-vs-config repo-identity compare, raw. Post-Decision-1 a case-differing pair produces a **working writeback that `bridge:check` calls ORPHANED (inert)** — a config accusation against a healthy install.
